texts.pro.28.18: El que en integridad camina, será salvo; Mas el de perversos caminos caerá en alguno.
texts.pro.28.19: El que labra su tierra, se hartará de pan: Mas el que sigue los ociosos, se hartará de pobreza.
texts.pro.28.20: El hombre de verdad tendrá muchas bendiciones: Mas el que se apresura á enriquecer, no será sin culpa.
texts.pro.28.21: Tener acepción de personas, no es bueno: Hasta por un bocado de pan prevaricará el hombre.
texts.pro.28.22: Apresúrase á ser rico el hombre de mal ojo; Y no conoce que le ha de venir pobreza.
texts.pro.28.23: El que reprende al hombre, hallará después mayor gracia Que el que lisonjea con la lengua.
texts.pro.28.24: El que roba á su padre ó á su madre, y dice que no es maldad, Compañero es del hombre destruidor.
texts.pro.28.25: El altivo de ánimo suscita contiendas: Mas el que en Jehová confía, medrará.
texts.pro.28.26: El que confía en su corazón es necio; Mas el que camina en sabiduría, será salvo.
texts.pro.28.27: El que da al pobre, no tendrá pobreza: Mas el que aparta sus ojos, tendrá muchas maldiciones.
texts.pro.28.28: Cuando los impíos son levantados, esconderáse el hombre: Mas cuando perecen, los justos se multiplican.
texts.pro.29.1: EL hombre que reprendido endurece la cerviz, De repente será quebrantado; ni habrá para él medicina.
texts.pro.29.2: Cuando los justos dominan, el pueblo se alegra: Mas cuando domina el impío, el pueblo gime.
texts.pro.29.3: El hombre que ama la sabiduría, alegra á su padre: Mas el que mantiene rameras, perderá la hacienda.
texts.pro.29.4: El rey con el juicio afirma la tierra: Mas el hombre de presentes la destruirá.
texts.pro.29.5: El hombre que lisonjea á su prójimo, Red tiende delante de sus pasos.
texts.pro.29.6: En la prevaricación del hombre malo hay lazo: Mas el justo cantará y se alegrará.
texts.pro.29.7: Conoce el justo la causa de los pobres: Mas el impío no entiende sabiduría.
texts.pro.29.8: Los hombres escarnecedores enlazan la ciudad: Mas los sabios apartan la ira.
texts.pro.29.9: Si el hombre sabio contendiere con el necio, Que se enoje ó que se ría, no tendrá reposo.
texts.pro.29.10: Los hombres sanguinarios aborrecen al perfecto: Mas los rectos buscan su contentamiento.
texts.pro.29.11: El necio da suelta á todo su espíritu; Mas el sabio al fin le sosiega.
texts.pro.29.12: Del señor que escucha la palabra mentirosa, Todos sus ministros son impíos.
texts.pro.29.13: El pobre y el usurero se encontraron: Jehová alumbra los ojos de ambos.
texts.pro.29.14: El rey que juzga con verdad á los pobres, Su trono será firme para siempre.
texts.pro.29.15: La vara y la corrección dan sabiduría: Mas el muchacho consentido avergonzará á su madre.
texts.pro.29.16: Cuando los impíos son muchos, mucha es la prevaricación; Mas los justos verán la ruina de ellos.
texts.pro.29.17: Corrige á tu hijo, y te dará descanso, Y dará deleite á tu alma.
texts.pro.29.18: Sin profecía el pueblo será disipado: Mas el que guarda la ley, bienaventurado él.
texts.pro.29.19: El siervo no se corregirá con palabras: Porque entiende, mas no corresponde.
texts.pro.29.20: ¿Has visto hombre ligero en sus palabras? Más esperanza hay del necio que de él.
texts.pro.29.21: El que regala á su siervo desde su niñez, A la postre será su hijo:
texts.pro.29.22: El hombre iracundo levanta contiendas; Y el furioso muchas veces peca.
texts.pro.29.23: La soberbia del hombre le abate; Pero al humilde de espíritu sustenta la honra.
texts.pro.29.24: El aparcero del ladrón aborrece su vida; Oirá maldiciones, y no lo denunciará.
texts.pro.29.25: El temor del hombre pondrá lazo: Mas el que confía en Jehová será levantado.
texts.pro.29.26: Muchos buscan el favor del príncipe: Mas de Jehová viene el juicio de cada uno.
texts.pro.29.27: Abominación es á los justos el hombre inicuo; Y abominación es al impío el de rectos caminos.
texts.pro.30.1: PALABRAS de Agur, hijo de Jachê: La profecía que dijo el varón á Ithiel, á Ithiel y á Ucal.
texts.pro.30.2: Ciertamente más rudo soy yo que ninguno, Ni tengo entendimiento de hombre.
texts.pro.30.3: Yo ni aprendí sabiduría, Ni conozco la ciencia del Santo.
texts.pro.30.4: ¿Quién subió al cielo, y descendió? ¿Quién encerró los vientos en sus puños? ¿Quién ató las aguas en un paño? ¿Quién afirmó todos los términos de la tierra? ¿Cuál es su nombre, y el nombre de su hijo, si sabes?
texts.pro.30.5: Toda palabra de Dios es limpia: Es escudo á los que en él esperan.
texts.pro.30.6: No añadas á sus palabras, porque no te reprenda, Y seas hallado mentiroso.
texts.pro.30.7: Dos cosas te he demandado; No me las niegues antes que muera.
texts.pro.30.8: Vanidad y palabra mentirosa aparta de mí. No me des pobreza ni riquezas; Manténme del pan que he menester;
texts.pro.30.9: No sea que me harte, y te niegue, y diga, ¿Quién es Jehová? O no sea que siendo pobre, hurte, Y blasfeme el nombre de mi Dios.
texts.pro.30.10: No acuses al siervo ante su señor, Porque no te maldiga, y peques.
texts.pro.30.11: Hay generación que maldice á su padre, Y á su madre no bendice.
texts.pro.30.12: Hay generación limpia en su opinión, Si bien no se ha limpiado su inmundicia.
texts.pro.30.13: Hay generación cuyos ojos son altivos, Y cuyos párpados son alzados.
texts.pro.30.14: Hay generación cuyos dientes son espadas, y sus muelas cuchillos, Para devorar á los pobres de la tierra, y de entre los hombres á los menesterosos.
texts.pro.30.15: La sanguijuela tiene dos hijas que se llaman, Trae, trae. Tres cosas hay que nunca se hartan; Aun la cuarta nunca dice, Basta:
texts.pro.30.16: El sepulcro, y la matriz estéril, La tierra no harta de aguas, Y el fuego que jamás dice, Basta.
texts.pro.30.17: El ojo que escarnece á su padre, Y menosprecia la enseñanza de la madre, Los cuervos lo saquen de la arroyada, Y tráguenlo los hijos del águila.
texts.pro.30.18: Tres cosas me son ocultas; Aun tampoco sé la cuarta:
texts.pro.30.19: El rastro del águila en el aire; El rastro de la culebra sobre la peña; El rastro de la nave en medio de la mar; Y el rastro del hombre en la moza.
texts.pro.30.20: Tal es el rastro de la mujer adúltera: Come, y limpia su boca, Y dice: No he hecho maldad.
texts.pro.30.21: Por tres cosas se alborota la tierra, Y la cuarta no puede sufrir:
texts.pro.30.22: Por el siervo cuando reinare; Y por el necio cuando se hartare de pan;
texts.pro.30.23: Por la aborrecida cuando se casare; Y por la sierva cuando heredare á su señora.
texts.pro.30.24: Cuatro cosas son de las más pequeñas de la tierra, Y las mismas son más sabias que los sabios:
texts.pro.30.25: Las hormigas, pueblo no fuerte, Y en el verano preparan su comida;
texts.pro.30.26: Los conejos, pueblo nada esforzado, Y ponen su casa en la piedra;
texts.pro.30.27: Las langostas, no tienen rey, Y salen todas acuadrilladas;
texts.pro.30.28: La araña, ase con las manos, Y está en palacios de rey.
texts.pro.30.29: Tres cosas hay de hermoso andar, Y la cuarta pasea muy bien:
texts.pro.30.30: El león, fuerte entre todos los animales, Que no torna atrás por nadie;
texts.pro.30.31: El lebrel ceñido de lomos; asimismo el macho cabrío; Y un rey contra el cual ninguno se levanta.
texts.pro.30.32: Si caiste, fué porque te enalteciste; Y si mal pensaste, Pon el dedo sobre la boca.
texts.pro.30.33: Ciertamente el que exprime la leche, sacará manteca; Y el que recio se suena las narices, sacará sangre: Y el que provoca la ira, causará contienda.
texts.pro.31.1: PALABRAS del rey Lemuel; la profecía con que le enseñó su madre.
texts.pro.31.2: ¿Qué, hijo mío? ¿y qué, hijo de mi vientre? ¿Y qué, hijo de mis deseos?
texts.pro.31.3: No des á las mujeres tu fuerza, Ni tus caminos á lo que es para destruir los reyes.
texts.pro.31.4: No es de los reyes, oh Lemuel, no es de los reyes beber vino, Ni de los príncipes la cerveza.
texts.pro.31.5: No sea que bebiendo olviden la ley, Y perviertan el derecho de todos los hijos afligidos.
texts.pro.31.6: Dad la cerveza al desfallecido, Y el vino á los de amargo ánimo:
texts.pro.31.7: Beban, y olvídense de su necesidad, Y de su miseria no más se acuerden.
texts.pro.31.8: Abre tu boca por el mudo, En el juicio de todos los hijos de muerte.
texts.pro.31.9: Abre tu boca, juzga justicia, Y el derecho del pobre y del menesteroso.
texts.pro.31.10: Mujer fuerte, ¿quién la hallará? Porque su estima sobrepuja largamente á la de piedras preciosas.
texts.pro.31.11: El corazón de su marido está en ella confiado, Y no tendrá necesidad de despojo.
texts.pro.31.12: Darále ella bien y no mal, Todos los días de su vida.
texts.pro.31.13: Buscó lana y lino, Y con voluntad labró de sus manos.
texts.pro.31.14: Fué como navío de mercader: Trae su pan de lejos.
texts.pro.31.15: Levantóse aun de noche, Y dió comida á su familia, Y ración á sus criadas.
texts.pro.31.16: Consideró la heredad, y compróla; Y plantó viña del fruto de sus manos.
texts.pro.31.17: Ciñó sus lomos de fortaleza, Y esforzó sus brazos.
texts.pro.31.18: Gustó que era buena su granjería: Su candela no se apagó de noche.
texts.pro.31.19: Aplicó sus manos al huso, Y sus manos tomaron la rueca.
texts.pro.31.20: Alargó su mano al pobre, Y extendió sus manos al menesteroso.
texts.pro.31.21: No tendrá temor de la nieve por su familia, Porque toda su familia está vestida de ropas dobles.
texts.pro.31.22: Ella se hizo tapices; De lino fino y púrpura es su vestido.
texts.pro.31.23: Conocido es su marido en las puertas, Cuando se sienta con los ancianos de la tierra.
texts.pro.31.24: Hizo telas, y vendió; Y dió cintas al mercader.
texts.pro.31.25: Fortaleza y honor son su vestidura; Y en el día postrero reirá.
texts.pro.31.26: Abrió su boca con sabiduría: Y la ley de clemencia está en su lengua.
texts.pro.31.27: Considera los caminos de su casa, Y no come el pan de balde.
texts.pro.31.28: Levantáronse sus hijos, y llamáronla bienaventurada; Y su marido también la alabó.
texts.pro.31.29: Muchas mujeres hicieron el bien; Mas tú las sobrepujaste á todas.
texts.pro.31.30: Engañosa es la gracia, y vana la hermosura: La mujer que teme á Jehová, ésa será alabada.
texts.pro.31.31: Dadle el fruto de sus manos, Y alábenla en las puertas sus hechos.

texts.pro.1.1: The proverbs of Solomon the son of David, king of Israel:
texts.pro.1.2: To know wisdom and instruction; To discern the words of understanding;
texts.pro.1.3: To receive instruction in wise dealing, In righteousness and justice and equity;
texts.pro.1.4: To give prudence to the simple, To the young man knowledge and discretion:
texts.pro.1.5: That the wise man may hear, and increase in learning; And that the man of understanding may attain unto sound counsels:
texts.pro.1.6: To understand a proverb, and a figure, The words of the wise, and their dark sayings.
texts.pro.1.7: The fear of Jehovah is the beginning of knowledge; [But] the foolish despise wisdom and instruction.
texts.pro.1.8: My son, hear the instruction of thy father, And forsake not the law of thy mother:
texts.pro.1.9: For they shall be a chaplet of grace unto thy head, And chains about thy neck.
texts.pro.1.10: My son, if sinners entice thee, Consent thou not.
texts.pro.1.11: If they say, Come with us, Let us lay wait for blood; Let us lurk privily for the innocent without cause;
texts.pro.1.12: Let us swallow them up alive as Sheol, And whole, as those that go down into the pit;
texts.pro.1.13: We shall find all precious substance; We shall fill our houses with spoil;
texts.pro.1.14: Thou shalt cast thy lot among us; We will all have one purse:
texts.pro.1.15: My son, walk not thou in the way with them; Refrain thy foot from their path:
texts.pro.1.16: For their feet run to evil, And they make haste to shed blood.
texts.pro.1.17: For in vain is the net spread In the sight of any bird:
texts.pro.1.18: And these lay wait for their own blood; They lurk privily for their own lives.
texts.pro.1.19: So are the ways of every one that is greedy of gain; It taketh away the life of the owners thereof.
texts.pro.1.20: Wisdom crieth aloud in the street; She uttereth her voice in the broad places;
texts.pro.1.21: She crieth in the chief place of concourse; At the entrance of the gates, In the city, she uttereth her words:
texts.pro.1.22: How long, ye simple ones, will ye love simplicity? And scoffers delight them in scoffing, And fools hate knowledge?
texts.pro.1.23: Turn you at my reproof: Behold, I will pour out my spirit upon you; I will make known my words unto you.
texts.pro.1.24: Because I have called, and ye have refused; I have stretched out my hand, and no man hath regarded;
texts.pro.1.25: But ye have set at nought all my counsel, And would none of my reproof:
texts.pro.1.26: I also will laugh in [the day of] your calamity; I will mock when your fear cometh;
texts.pro.1.27: When your fear cometh as a storm, And your calamity cometh on as a whirlwind; When distress and anguish come upon you.
texts.pro.1.28: Then will they call upon me, but I will not answer; They will seek me diligently, but they shall not find me:
texts.pro.1.29: For that they hated knowledge, And did not choose the fear of Jehovah:
texts.pro.1.30: They would none of my counsel; They despised all my reproof.
texts.pro.1.31: Therefore shall they eat of the fruit of their own way, And be filled with their own devices.
texts.pro.1.32: For the backsliding of the simple shall slay them, And the careless ease of fools shall destroy them.
texts.pro.1.33: But whoso hearkeneth unto me shall dwell securely, And shall be quiet without fear of evil.
texts.pro.2.1: My son, if thou wilt receive my words, And lay up my commandments with thee;
texts.pro.2.2: So as to incline thine ear unto wisdom, And apply thy heart to understanding;
texts.pro.2.3: Yea, if thou cry after discernment, And lift up thy voice for understanding;
texts.pro.2.4: If thou seek her as silver, And search for her as for hid treasures:
texts.pro.2.5: Then shalt thou understand the fear of Jehovah, And find the knowledge of God.
texts.pro.2.6: For Jehovah giveth wisdom; Out of his mouth [cometh] knowledge and understanding:
texts.pro.2.7: He layeth up sound wisdom for the upright; [He is] a shield to them that walk in integrity;
texts.pro.2.8: That he may guard the paths of justice, And preserve the way of his saints.
texts.pro.2.9: Then shalt thou understand righteousness and justice, And equity, [yea], every good path.
texts.pro.2.10: For wisdom shall enter into thy heart, And knowledge shall be pleasant unto thy soul;
texts.pro.2.11: Discretion shall watch over thee; Understanding shall keep thee:
texts.pro.2.12: To deliver thee from the way of evil, From the men that speak perverse things;
texts.pro.2.13: Who forsake the paths of uprightness, To walk in the ways of darkness;
texts.pro.2.14: Who rejoice to do evil, And delight in the perverseness of evil;
texts.pro.2.15: Who are crooked in their ways, And wayward in their paths:
texts.pro.2.16: To deliver thee from the strange woman, Even from the foreigner that flattereth with her words;
texts.pro.2.17: That forsaketh the friend of her youth, And forgetteth the covenant of her God:
texts.pro.2.18: For her house inclineth unto death, And her paths unto the dead;
texts.pro.2.19: None that go unto her return again, Neither do they attain unto the paths of life:
texts.pro.2.20: That thou mayest walk in the way of good men, And keep the paths of the righteous.
texts.pro.2.21: For the upright shall dwell in the land, And the perfect shall remain in it.
texts.pro.2.22: But the wicked shall be cut off from the land, And the treacherous shall be rooted out of it.
texts.pro.3.1: My son, forget not my law; But let thy heart keep my commandments:
texts.pro.3.2: For length of days, and years of life, And peace, will they add to thee.
texts.pro.3.3: Let not kindness and truth forsake thee: Bind them about thy neck; Write them upon the tablet of thy heart:
texts.pro.3.4: So shalt thou find favor and good understanding In the sight of God and man.
texts.pro.3.5: Trust in Jehovah with all thy heart, And lean not upon thine own understanding:
texts.pro.3.6: In all thy ways acknowledge him, And he will direct thy paths.
texts.pro.3.7: Be not wise in thine own eyes; Fear Jehovah, and depart from evil:
texts.pro.3.8: It will be health to thy navel, And marrow to thy bones.
texts.pro.3.9: Honor Jehovah with thy substance, And with the first-fruits of all thine increase:
texts.pro.3.10: So shall thy barns be filled with plenty, And thy vats shall overflow with new wine.
texts.pro.3.11: My son, despise not the chastening of Jehovah; Neither be weary of his reproof:
texts.pro.3.12: For whom Jehovah loveth he reproveth; Even as a father the son in whom he delighteth.
texts.pro.3.13: Happy is the man that findeth wisdom, And the man that getteth understanding.
texts.pro.3.14: For the gaining of it is better than the gaining of silver, And the profit thereof than fine gold.
texts.pro.3.15: She is more precious than rubies: And none of the things thou canst desire are to be compared unto her.
texts.pro.3.16: Length of days is in her right hand; In her left hand are riches and honor.
texts.pro.3.17: Her ways are ways of pleasantness, And all her paths are peace.
texts.pro.3.18: She is a tree of life to them that lay hold upon her: And happy is every one that retaineth her.
texts.pro.3.19: Jehovah by wisdom founded the earth; By understanding he established the heavens.
texts.pro.3.20: By his knowledge the depths were broken up, And the skies drop down the dew.
texts.pro.3.21: My son, let them not depart from thine eyes; Keep sound wisdom and discretion:
texts.pro.3.22: So shall they be life unto thy soul, And grace to thy neck.
texts.pro.3.23: Then shalt thou walk in thy way securely, And thy foot shall not stumble.
texts.pro.3.24: When thou liest down, thou shalt not be afraid: Yea, thou shalt lie down, and thy sleep shall be sweet.
texts.pro.3.25: Be not afraid of sudden fear, Neither of the desolation of the wicked, when it cometh:
texts.pro.3.26: For Jehovah will be thy confidence, And will keep thy foot from being taken.
texts.pro.3.27: Withhold not good from them to whom it is due, When it is in the power of thy hand to do it.
texts.pro.3.28: Say not unto thy neighbor, Go, and come again, And to-morrow I will give; When thou hast it by thee.
texts.pro.3.29: Devise not evil against thy neighbor, Seeing he dwelleth securely by thee.
texts.pro.3.30: Strive not with a man without cause, If he have done thee no harm.
texts.pro.3.31: Envy thou not the man of violence, And choose none of his ways.
texts.pro.3.32: For the perverse is an abomination to Jehovah; But his friendship is with the upright.
texts.pro.3.33: The curse of Jehovah is in the house of the wicked; But he blesseth the habitation of the righteous.
texts.pro.3.34: Surely he scoffeth at the scoffers; But he giveth grace unto the lowly.
texts.pro.3.35: The wise shall inherit glory; But shame shall be the promotion of fools.
texts.pro.4.1: Hear, [my] sons, the instruction of a father, And attend to know understanding:
texts.pro.4.2: For I give you good doctrine; Forsake ye not my law.
texts.pro.4.3: For I was a son unto my father, Tender and only beloved in the sight of my mother.
texts.pro.4.4: And he taught me, and said unto me: Let thy heart retain my words; Keep my commandments, and live;
texts.pro.4.5: Get wisdom, get understanding; Forget not, neither decline from the words of my mouth;
texts.pro.4.6: Forsake her not, and she will preserve thee; Love her, and she will keep thee.
texts.pro.4.7: Wisdom [is] the principal thing; [therefore] get wisdom; Yea, with all thy getting get understanding.
texts.pro.4.8: Exalt her, and she will promote thee; She will bring thee to honor, when thou dost embrace her.
texts.pro.4.9: She will give to thy head a chaplet of grace; A crown of beauty will she deliver to thee.
texts.pro.4.10: Hear, O my son, and receive my sayings; And the years of thy life shall be many.
texts.pro.4.11: I have taught thee in the way of wisdom; I have led thee in paths of uprightness.
texts.pro.4.12: When thou goest, thy steps shall not be straitened; And if thou runnest, thou shalt not stumble.
texts.pro.4.13: Take fast hold of instruction; let her not go: Keep her; for she is thy life.
texts.pro.4.14: Enter not into the path of the wicked, And walk not in the way of evil men.
texts.pro.4.15: Avoid it, pass not by it; Turn from it, and pass on.
texts.pro.4.16: For they sleep not, except they do evil; And their sleep is taken away, unless they cause some to fall.
texts.pro.4.17: For they eat the bread of wickedness, And drink the wine of violence.
texts.pro.4.18: But the path of the righteous is as the dawning light, That shineth more and more unto the perfect day.
texts.pro.4.19: The way of the wicked is as darkness: They know not at what they stumble.
texts.pro.4.20: My son, attend to my words; Incline thine ear unto my sayings.
texts.pro.4.21: Let them not depart from thine eyes; Keep them in the midst of thy heart.
texts.pro.4.22: For they are life unto those that find them, And health to all their flesh.
texts.pro.4.23: Keep thy heart with all diligence; For out of it are the issues of life.
texts.pro.4.24: Put away from thee a wayward mouth, And perverse lips put far from thee.
texts.pro.4.25: Let thine eyes look right on, And let thine eyelids look straight before thee.
texts.pro.4.26: Make level the path of thy feet, And let all thy ways be established.
texts.pro.4.27: Turn not to the right hand nor to the left: Remove thy foot from evil.
texts.pro.5.1: My son, attend unto my wisdom; Incline thine ear to my understanding:
texts.pro.5.2: That thou mayest preserve discretion, And that thy lips may keep knowledge.
texts.pro.5.3: For the lips of a strange woman drop honey, And her mouth is smoother than oil:
texts.pro.5.4: But in the end she is bitter as wormwood, Sharp as a two-edged sword.
texts.pro.5.5: Her feet go down to death; Her steps take hold on Sheol;
texts.pro.5.6: So that she findeth not the level path of life: Her ways are unstable, [and] she knoweth [it] not.
texts.pro.5.7: Now therefore, [my] sons, hearken unto me, And depart not from the words of my mouth.
texts.pro.5.8: Remove thy way far from her, And come not nigh the door of her house;
texts.pro.5.9: Lest thou give thine honor unto others, And thy years unto the cruel;
texts.pro.5.10: Lest strangers be filled with thy strength, And thy labors [be] in the house of an alien,
texts.pro.5.11: And thou mourn at thy latter end, When thy flesh and thy body are consumed,
texts.pro.5.12: And say, How have I hated instruction, And my heart despised reproof;
texts.pro.5.13: Neither have I obeyed the voice of my teachers, Nor inclined mine ear to them that instructed me!
texts.pro.5.14: I was well-nigh in all evil In the midst of the assembly and congregation.
texts.pro.5.15: Drink waters out of thine own cistern, And running waters out of thine own well.
texts.pro.5.16: Should thy springs be dispersed abroad, And streams of water in the streets?
texts.pro.5.17: Let them be for thyself alone, And not for strangers with thee.
texts.pro.5.18: Let thy fountain be blessed; And rejoice in the wife of thy youth.
texts.pro.5.19: [As] a loving hind and a pleasant doe, Let her breasts satisfy thee at all times; And be thou ravished always with her love.
texts.pro.5.20: For why shouldest thou, my son, be ravished with a strange woman, And embrace the bosom of a foreigner?
texts.pro.5.21: For the ways of man are before the eyes of Jehovah; And he maketh level all his paths.
texts.pro.5.22: His own iniquities shall take the wicked, And he shall be holden with the cords of his sin.
texts.pro.5.23: He shall die for lack of instruction; And in the greatness of his folly he shall go astray.
texts.pro.6.1: My son, if thou art become surety for thy neighbor, If thou hast stricken thy hands for a stranger;
texts.pro.6.2: Thou art snared with the words of thy mouth, Thou art taken with the words of thy mouth.
texts.pro.6.3: Do this now, my son, and deliver thyself, Seeing thou art come into the hand of thy neighbor: Go, humble thyself, and importune thy neighbor;
texts.pro.6.4: Give not sleep to thine eyes, Nor slumber to thine eyelids;
texts.pro.6.5: Deliver thyself as a roe from the hand [of the hunter], And as a bird from the hand of the fowler.
texts.pro.6.6: Go to the ant, thou sluggard; Consider her ways, and be wise:
texts.pro.6.7: Which having no chief, Overseer, or ruler,
texts.pro.6.8: Provideth her bread in the summer, And gathereth her food in the harvest.
texts.pro.6.9: How long wilt thou sleep, O sluggard? When wilt thou arise out of thy sleep?
texts.pro.6.10: [Yet] a little sleep, a little slumber, A little folding of the hands to sleep:
texts.pro.6.11: So shall thy poverty come as a robber, And thy want as an armed man.
texts.pro.6.12: A worthless person, a man of iniquity, Is he that walketh with a perverse mouth;
texts.pro.6.13: That winketh with his eyes, that speaketh with his feet, That maketh signs with his fingers;
texts.pro.6.14: In whose heart is perverseness, Who deviseth evil continually, Who soweth discord.
texts.pro.6.15: Therefore shall his calamity come suddenly; On a sudden shall he be broken, and that without remedy.
texts.pro.6.16: There are six things which Jehovah hateth; Yea, seven which are an abomination unto him:
texts.pro.6.17: Haughty eyes, a lying tongue, And hands that shed innocent blood;
texts.pro.6.18: A heart that deviseth wicked purposes, Feet that are swift in running to mischief,
texts.pro.6.19: A false witness that uttereth lies, And he that soweth discord among brethren.
texts.pro.6.20: My son, keep the commandment of thy father, And forsake not the law of thy mother:
texts.pro.6.21: Bind them continually upon thy heart; Tie them about thy neck.
texts.pro.6.22: When thou walkest, it shall lead thee; When thou sleepest, it shall watch over thee; And when thou awakest, it shall talk with thee.
texts.pro.6.23: For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light; And reproofs of instruction are the way of life:
texts.pro.6.24: To keep thee from the evil woman, From the flattery of the foreigner's tongue.
texts.pro.6.25: Lust not after her beauty in thy heart; Neither let her take thee with her eyelids.
texts.pro.6.26: For on account of a harlot [a man is brought] to a piece of bread; And the adulteress hunteth for the precious life.
texts.pro.6.27: Can a man take fire in his bosom, And his clothes not be burned?
texts.pro.6.28: Or can one walk upon hot coals, And his feet not be scorched?
texts.pro.6.29: So he that goeth in to his neighbor's wife; Whosoever toucheth her shall not be unpunished.
texts.pro.6.30: Men do not despise a thief, if he steal To satisfy himself when he is hungry:
texts.pro.6.31: But if he be found, he shall restore sevenfold; He shall give all the substance of his house.
texts.pro.6.32: He that committeth adultery with a woman is void of understanding: He doeth it who would destroy his own soul.
texts.pro.6.33: Wounds and dishonor shall he get; And his reproach shall not be wiped away.
texts.pro.6.34: For jealousy is the rage of a man; And he will not spare in the day of vengeance.
texts.pro.6.35: He will not regard any ransom; Neither will he rest content, though thou givest many gifts.
texts.pro.7.1: My son, keep my words, And lay up my commandments with thee.
texts.pro.7.2: Keep my commandments and live; And my law as the apple of thine eye.
texts.pro.7.3: Bind them upon thy fingers; Write them upon the tablet of thy heart.
texts.pro.7.4: Say unto wisdom, Thou art my sister; And call understanding [thy] kinswoman:
texts.pro.7.5: That they may keep thee from the strange woman, From the foreigner that flattereth with her words.
texts.pro.7.6: For at the window of my house I looked forth through my lattice;
texts.pro.7.7: And I beheld among the simple ones, I discerned among the youths, A young man void of understanding,
texts.pro.7.8: Passing through the street near her corner; And he went the way to her house,
texts.pro.7.9: In the twilight, in the evening of the day, In the middle of the night and in the darkness.
texts.pro.7.10: And, behold, there met him a woman With the attire of a harlot, and wily of heart.
texts.pro.7.11: She is clamorous and wilful; Her feet abide not in her house:
texts.pro.7.12: Now she is in the streets, now in the broad places, And lieth in wait at every corner.
texts.pro.7.13: So she caught him, and kissed him, [And] with an impudent face she said unto him:
texts.pro.7.14: Sacrifices of peace-offerings are with me; This day have I paid my vows.
texts.pro.7.15: Therefore came I forth to meet thee, Diligently to seek thy face, and I have found thee.
texts.pro.7.16: I have spread my couch with carpets of tapestry, With striped cloths of the yarn of Egypt.
texts.pro.7.17: I have perfumed my bed With myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon.
texts.pro.7.18: Come, let us take our fill of love until the morning; Let us solace ourselves with loves.
texts.pro.7.19: For the man is not at home; He is gone a long journey:
texts.pro.7.20: He hath taken a bag of money with him; He will come home at the full moon.
texts.pro.7.21: With her much fair speech she causeth him to yield; With the flattering of her lips she forceth him along.
texts.pro.7.22: He goeth after her straightway, As an ox goeth to the slaughter, Or as [one in] fetters to the correction of the fool;
texts.pro.7.23: Till an arrow strike through his liver; As a bird hasteth to the snare, And knoweth not that it is for his life.
texts.pro.7.24: Now therefore, [my] sons, hearken unto me, And attend to the words of my mouth.
texts.pro.7.25: Let not thy heart decline to her ways; Go not astray in her paths.
texts.pro.7.26: For she hath cast down many wounded: Yea, all her slain are a mighty host.
texts.pro.7.27: Her house is the way to Sheol, Going down to the chambers of death.
texts.pro.8.1: Doth not wisdom cry, And understanding put forth her voice?
texts.pro.8.2: On the top of high places by the way, Where the paths meet, she standeth;
texts.pro.8.3: Beside the gates, at the entry of the city, At the coming in at the doors, she crieth aloud:
texts.pro.8.4: Unto you, O men, I call; And my voice is to the sons of men.
texts.pro.8.5: O ye simple, understand prudence; And, ye fools, be of an understanding heart.
texts.pro.8.6: Hear, for I will speak excellent things; And the opening of my lips shall be right things.
texts.pro.8.7: For my mouth shall utter truth; And wickedness is an abomination to my lips.
texts.pro.8.8: All the words of my mouth are in righteousness; There is nothing crooked or perverse in them.
texts.pro.8.9: They are all plain to him that understandeth, And right to them that find knowledge.
texts.pro.8.10: Receive my instruction, and not silver; And knowledge rather than choice gold.
texts.pro.8.11: For wisdom is better than rubies; And all the things that may be desired are not to be compared unto it.
texts.pro.8.12: I wisdom have made prudence my dwelling, And find out knowledge [and] discretion.
texts.pro.8.13: The fear of Jehovah is to hate evil: Pride, and arrogancy, and the evil way, And the perverse mouth, do I hate.
texts.pro.8.14: Counsel is mine, and sound knowledge: I am understanding; I have might.
texts.pro.8.15: By me kings reign, And princes decree justice.
texts.pro.8.16: By me princes rule, And nobles, [even] all the judges of the earth.
texts.pro.8.17: I love them that love me; And those that seek me diligently shall find me.
texts.pro.8.18: Riches and honor are with me; [Yea], durable wealth and righteousness.
texts.pro.8.19: My fruit is better than gold, yea, than fine gold; And my revenue than choice silver.
texts.pro.8.20: I walk in the way of righteousness, In the midst of the paths of justice;
texts.pro.8.21: That I may cause those that love me to inherit substance, And that I may fill their treasuries.
texts.pro.8.22: Jehovah possessed me in the beginning of his way, Before his works of old.
texts.pro.8.23: I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, Before the earth was.
texts.pro.8.24: When there were no depths, I was brought forth, When there were no fountains abounding with water.
texts.pro.8.25: Before the mountains were settled, Before the hills was I brought forth;
texts.pro.8.26: While as yet he had not made the earth, nor the fields, Nor the beginning of the dust of the world.
texts.pro.8.27: When he established the heavens, I was there: When he set a circle upon the face of the deep,
texts.pro.8.28: When he made firm the skies above, When the fountains of the deep became strong,
texts.pro.8.29: When he gave to the sea its bound, That the waters should not transgress his commandment, When he marked out the foundations of the earth;
texts.pro.8.30: Then I was by him, [as] a master workman; And I was daily [his] delight, Rejoicing always before him,
texts.pro.8.31: Rejoicing in his habitable earth; And my delight was with the sons of men.
texts.pro.8.32: Now therefore, [my] sons, hearken unto me; For blessed are they that keep my ways.
texts.pro.8.33: Hear instruction, and be wise, And refuse it not.
texts.pro.8.34: Blessed is the man that heareth me, Watching daily at my gates, Waiting at the posts of my doors.
texts.pro.8.35: For whoso findeth me findeth life, And shall obtain favor of Jehovah.
texts.pro.8.36: But he that sinneth against me wrongeth his own soul: All they that hate me love death.
texts.pro.9.1: Wisdom hath builded her house; She hath hewn out her seven pillars:
texts.pro.9.2: She hath killed her beasts; She hath mingled her wine; She hath also furnished her table:
texts.pro.9.3: She hath sent forth her maidens; She crieth upon the highest places of the city:
texts.pro.9.4: Whoso is simple, let him turn in hither: As for him that is void of understanding, she saith to him,
texts.pro.9.5: Come, eat ye of my bread, And drink of the wine which I have mingled.
texts.pro.9.6: Leave off, ye simple ones, and live; And walk in the way of understanding.
texts.pro.9.7: He that correcteth a scoffer getteth to himself reviling; And he that reproveth a wicked man [getteth] himself a blot.
texts.pro.9.8: Reprove not a scoffer, lest he hate thee: Reprove a wise man, and he will love thee.
texts.pro.9.9: Give [instruction] to a wise man, and he will be yet wiser: Teach a righteous man, and he will increase in learning.
texts.pro.9.10: The fear of Jehovah is the beginning of wisdom; And the knowledge of the Holy One is understanding.
texts.pro.9.11: For by me thy days shall be multiplied, And the years of thy life shall be increased.
texts.pro.9.12: If thou art wise, thou art wise for thyself; And if thou scoffest, thou alone shalt bear it.
texts.pro.9.13: The foolish woman is clamorous; [She is] simple, and knoweth nothing.
texts.pro.9.14: And she sitteth at the door of her house, On a seat in the high places of the city,
texts.pro.9.15: To call to them that pass by, Who go right on their ways:
texts.pro.9.16: Whoso is simple, let him turn in hither; And as for him that is void of understanding, she saith to him,
texts.pro.9.17: Stolen waters are sweet, And bread [eaten] in secret is pleasant.
texts.pro.9.18: But he knoweth not that the dead are there; That her guests are in the depths of Sheol.
texts.pro.10.1: The proverbs of Solomon. A wise son maketh a glad father; But a foolish son is the heaviness of his mother.
texts.pro.10.2: Treasures of wickedness profit nothing; But righteousness delivereth from death.
texts.pro.10.3: Jehovah will not suffer the soul of the righteous to famish; But he thrusteth away the desire of the wicked.
texts.pro.10.4: He becometh poor that worketh with a slack hand; But the hand of the diligent maketh rich.
texts.pro.10.5: He that gathereth in summer is a wise son; [But] he that sleepeth in harvest is a son that causeth shame.
texts.pro.10.6: Blessings are upon the head of the righteous; But violence covereth the mouth of the wicked.
texts.pro.10.7: The memory of the righteous is blessed; But the name of the wicked shall rot.
texts.pro.10.8: The wise in heart will receive commandments; But a prating fool shall fall.
texts.pro.10.9: He that walketh uprightly walketh surely; But he that perverteth his ways shall be known.
texts.pro.10.10: He that winketh with the eye causeth sorrow; But a prating fool shall fall.
texts.pro.10.11: The mouth of the righteous is a fountain of life; But violence covereth the mouth of the wicked.
texts.pro.10.12: Hatred stirreth up strifes; But love covereth all transgressions.
texts.pro.10.13: In the lips of him that hath discernment wisdom is found; But a rod is for the back of him that is void of understanding.
texts.pro.10.14: Wise men lay up knowledge; But the mouth of the foolish is a present destruction.
texts.pro.10.15: The rich man's wealth is his strong city: The destruction of the poor is their poverty.
texts.pro.10.16: The labor of the righteous [tendeth] to life; The increase of the wicked, to sin.
texts.pro.10.17: He is in the way of life that heedeth correction; But he that forsaketh reproof erreth.
texts.pro.10.18: He that hideth hatred is of lying lips; And he that uttereth a slander is a fool.
texts.pro.10.19: In the multitude of words there wanteth not transgression; But he that refraineth his lips doeth wisely.
texts.pro.10.20: The tongue of the righteous is [as] choice silver: The heart of the wicked is little worth.
texts.pro.10.21: The lips of the righteous feed many; But the foolish die for lack of understanding.
texts.pro.10.22: The blessing of Jehovah, it maketh rich; And he addeth no sorrow therewith.
texts.pro.10.23: It is as sport to a fool to do wickedness; And [so is] wisdom to a man of understanding.
texts.pro.10.24: The fear of the wicked, it shall come upon him; And the desire of the righteous shall be granted.
texts.pro.10.25: When the whirlwind passeth, the wicked is no more; But the righteous is an everlasting foundation.
texts.pro.10.26: As vinegar to the teeth, and as smoke to the eyes, So is the sluggard to them that send him.
texts.pro.10.27: The fear of Jehovah prolongeth days; But the years of the wicked shall be shortened.
texts.pro.10.28: The hope of the righteous [shall be] gladness; But the expectation of the wicked shall perish.
texts.pro.10.29: The way of Jehovah is a stronghold to the upright; But it is a destruction to the workers of iniquity.
texts.pro.10.30: The righteous shall never be removed; But the wicked shall not dwell in the land.
texts.pro.10.31: The mouth of the righteous bringeth forth wisdom; But the perverse tongue shall be cut off.
texts.pro.10.32: The lips of the righteous know what is acceptable; But the mouth of the wicked [speaketh] perverseness.
texts.pro.11.1: A false balance is an abomination to Jehovah; But a just weight is his delight.
texts.pro.11.2: When pride cometh, then cometh shame; But with the lowly is wisdom.
texts.pro.11.3: The integrity of the upright shall guide them; But the perverseness of the treacherous shall destroy them.
texts.pro.11.4: Riches profit not in the day of wrath; But righteousness delivereth from death.
texts.pro.11.5: The righteousness of the perfect shall direct his way; But the wicked shall fall by his own wickedness.
texts.pro.11.6: The righteousness of the upright shall deliver them; But the treacherous shall be taken in their own iniquity.
texts.pro.11.7: When a wicked man dieth, [his] expectation shall perish; And the hope of iniquity perisheth.
texts.pro.11.8: The righteous is delivered out of trouble, And the wicked cometh in his stead.
texts.pro.11.9: With his mouth the godless man destroyeth his neighbor; But through knowledge shall the righteous be delivered.
texts.pro.11.10: When it goeth well with the righteous, the city rejoiceth; And when the wicked perish, there is shouting.
texts.pro.11.11: By the blessing of the upright the city is exalted; But it is overthrown by the mouth of the wicked.
texts.pro.11.12: He that despiseth his neighbor is void of wisdom; But a man of understanding holdeth his peace.
texts.pro.11.13: He that goeth about as a tale-bearer revealeth secrets; But he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth a matter.
texts.pro.11.14: Where no wise guidance is, the people falleth; But in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.
texts.pro.11.15: He that is surety for a stranger shall smart for it; But he that hateth suretyship is secure.
texts.pro.11.16: A gracious woman obtaineth honor; And violent men obtain riches.
texts.pro.11.17: The merciful man doeth good to his own soul; But he that is cruel troubleth his own flesh.
texts.pro.11.18: The wicked earneth deceitful wages; But he that soweth righteousness [hath] a sure reward.
texts.pro.11.19: He that is stedfast in righteousness [shall attain] unto life; And he that pursueth evil [doeth it] to his own death.
texts.pro.11.20: They that are perverse in heart are an abomination to Jehovah; But such as are perfect in [their] way are his delight.
texts.pro.11.21: [Though] hand [join] in hand, the evil man shall not be unpunished; But the seed of the righteous shall be delivered.
texts.pro.11.22: [As] a ring of gold in a swine's snout, [So is] a fair woman that is without discretion.
texts.pro.11.23: The desire of the righteous is only good; [But] the expectation of the wicked is wrath.
texts.pro.11.24: There is that scattereth, and increaseth yet more; And there is that withholdeth more than is meet, but [it tendeth] only to want.
texts.pro.11.25: The liberal soul shall be made fat; And he that watereth shall be watered also himself.
texts.pro.11.26: He that withholdeth grain, the people shall curse him; But blessing shall be upon the head of him that selleth it.
texts.pro.11.27: He that diligently seeketh good seeketh favor; But he that searcheth after evil, it shall come unto him.
texts.pro.11.28: He that trusteth in his riches shall fall; But the righteous shall flourish as the green leaf.
texts.pro.11.29: He that troubleth his own house shall inherit the wind; And the foolish shall be servant to the wise of heart.
texts.pro.11.30: The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life; And he that is wise winneth souls.
texts.pro.11.31: Behold, the righteous shall be recompensed in the earth: How much more the wicked and the sinner!
texts.pro.12.1: Whoso loveth correction loveth knowledge; But he that hateth reproof is brutish.
texts.pro.12.2: A good man shall obtain favor of Jehovah; But a man of wicked devices will he condemn.
texts.pro.12.3: A man shall not be established by wickedness; But the root of the righteous shall not be moved.
texts.pro.12.4: A worthy woman is the crown of her husband; But she that maketh ashamed is as rottenness in his bones.
texts.pro.12.5: The thoughts of the righteous are just; [But] the counsels of the wicked are deceit.
texts.pro.12.6: The words of the wicked are of lying in wait for blood; But the mouth of the upright shall deliver them.
texts.pro.12.7: The wicked are overthrown, and are not; But the house of the righteous shall stand.
texts.pro.12.8: A man shall be commended according to his wisdom; But he that is of a perverse heart shall be despised.
texts.pro.12.9: Better is he that is lightly esteemed, and hath a servant, Than he that honoreth himself, and lacketh bread.
texts.pro.12.10: A righteous man regardeth the life of his beast; But the tender mercies of the wicked are cruel.
texts.pro.12.11: He that tilleth his land shall have plenty of bread; But he that followeth after vain [persons] is void of understanding.
texts.pro.12.12: The wicked desireth the net of evil men; But the root of the righteous yieldeth [fruit].
texts.pro.12.13: In the transgression of the lips is a snare to the evil man; But the righteous shall come out of trouble.
texts.pro.12.14: A man shall be satisfied with good by the fruit of his mouth; And the doings of a man's hands shall be rendered unto him.
texts.pro.12.15: The way of a fool is right in his own eyes; But he that is wise hearkeneth unto counsel.
texts.pro.12.16: A fool's vexation is presently known; But a prudent man concealeth shame.
texts.pro.12.17: He that uttereth truth showeth forth righteousness; But a false witness, deceit.
texts.pro.12.18: There is that speaketh rashly like the piercings of a sword; But the tongue of the wise is health.
texts.pro.12.19: The lip of truth shall be established for ever; But a lying tongue is but for a moment.
texts.pro.12.20: Deceit is in the heart of them that devise evil; But to the counsellors of peace is joy.
texts.pro.12.21: There shall no mischief happen to the righteous; But the wicked shall be filled with evil.
texts.pro.12.22: Lying lips are an abomination to Jehovah; But they that deal truly are his delight.
texts.pro.12.23: A prudent man concealeth knowledge; But the heart of fools proclaimeth foolishness.
texts.pro.12.24: The hand of the diligent shall bear rule; But the slothful shall be put under taskwork.
texts.pro.12.25: Heaviness in the heart of a man maketh it stoop; But a good word maketh it glad.
texts.pro.12.26: The righteous is a guide to his neighbor; But the way of the wicked causeth them to err.
texts.pro.12.27: The slothful man roasteth not that which he took in hunting; But the precious substance of men [is to] the diligent.
texts.pro.12.28: In the way of righteousness is life; And in the pathway thereof there is no death.
texts.pro.13.1: A wise son [heareth] his father's instruction; But a scoffer heareth not rebuke.
texts.pro.13.2: A man shall eat good by the fruit of his mouth; But the soul of the treacherous [shall eat] violence.
texts.pro.13.3: He that guardeth his mouth keepeth his life; [But] he that openeth wide his lips shall have destruction.
texts.pro.13.4: The soul of the sluggard desireth, and hath nothing; But the soul of the diligent shall be made fat.
texts.pro.13.5: A righteous man hateth lying; But a wicked man is loathsome, and cometh to shame.
texts.pro.13.6: Righteousness guardeth him that is upright in the way; But wickedness overthroweth the sinner.
texts.pro.13.7: There is that maketh himself rich, yet hath nothing: There is that maketh himself poor, yet hath great wealth.
texts.pro.13.8: The ransom of a man's life is his riches; But the poor heareth no threatening.
texts.pro.13.9: The light of the righteous rejoiceth; But the lamp of the wicked shall be put out.
texts.pro.13.10: By pride cometh only contention; But with the well-advised is wisdom.
texts.pro.13.11: Wealth gotten by vanity shall be diminished; But he that gathereth by labor shall have increase.
texts.pro.13.12: Hope deferred maketh the heart sick; But when the desire cometh, it is a tree of life.
texts.pro.13.13: Whoso despiseth the word bringeth destruction on himself; But he that feareth the commandment shall be rewarded.
texts.pro.13.14: The law of the wise is a fountain of life, That one may depart from the snares of death.
texts.pro.13.15: Good understanding giveth favor; But the way of the transgressor is hard.
texts.pro.13.16: Every prudent man worketh with knowledge; But a fool flaunteth [his] folly.
texts.pro.13.17: A wicked messenger falleth into evil; But a faithful ambassador is health.
texts.pro.13.18: Poverty and shame [shall be to] him that refuseth correction; But he that regardeth reproof shall be honored.
texts.pro.13.19: The desire accomplished is sweet to the soul; But it is an abomination to fools to depart from evil.
texts.pro.13.20: Walk with wise men, and thou shalt be wise; But the companion of fools shall smart for it.
texts.pro.13.21: Evil pursueth sinners; But the righteous shall be recompensed with good.
texts.pro.13.22: A good man leaveth an inheritance to his children's children; And the wealth of the sinner is laid up for the righteous.
texts.pro.13.23: Much food [is in] the tillage of the poor; But there is that is destroyed by reason of injustice.
texts.pro.13.24: He that spareth his rod hateth his son; But he that loveth him chasteneth him betimes.
texts.pro.13.25: The righteous eateth to the satisfying of his soul; But the belly of the wicked shall want.
texts.pro.14.1: Every wise woman buildeth her house; But the foolish plucketh it down with her own hands.
texts.pro.14.2: He that walketh in his uprightness feareth Jehovah; But he that is perverse in his ways despiseth him.
texts.pro.14.3: In the mouth of the foolish is a rod for [his] pride; But the lips of the wise shall preserve them.
texts.pro.14.4: Where no oxen are, the crib is clean; But much increase is by the strength of the ox.
texts.pro.14.5: A faithful witness will not lie; But a false witness uttereth lies.
texts.pro.14.6: A scoffer seeketh wisdom, and [findeth it] not; But knowledge is easy unto him that hath understanding.
texts.pro.14.7: Go into the presence of a foolish man, And thou shalt not perceive [in him] the lips of knowledge.
texts.pro.14.8: The wisdom of the prudent is to understand his way; But the folly of fools is deceit.
texts.pro.14.9: A trespass-offering mocketh fools; But among the upright there is good will.
texts.pro.14.10: The heart knoweth its own bitterness; And a stranger doth not intermeddle with its joy.
texts.pro.14.11: The house of the wicked shall be overthrown; But the tent of the upright shall flourish.
texts.pro.14.12: There is a way which seemeth right unto a man; But the end thereof are the ways of death.
texts.pro.14.13: Even in laughter the heart is sorrowful; And the end of mirth is heaviness.
texts.pro.14.14: The backslider in heart shall be filled with his own ways; And a good man [shall be satisfied] from himself.
texts.pro.14.15: The simple believeth every word; But the prudent man looketh well to his going.
texts.pro.14.16: A wise man feareth, and departeth from evil; But the fool beareth himself insolently, and is confident.
texts.pro.14.17: He that is soon angry will deal foolishly; And a man of wicked devices is hated.
texts.pro.14.18: The simple inherit folly; But the prudent are crowned with knowledge.
texts.pro.14.19: The evil bow down before the good; And the wicked, at the gates of the righteous.
texts.pro.14.20: The poor is hated even of his own neighbor; But the rich hath many friends.
texts.pro.14.21: He that despiseth his neighbor sinneth; But he that hath pity on the poor, happy is he.
texts.pro.14.22: Do they not err that devise evil? But mercy and truth [shall be to] them that devise good.
texts.pro.14.23: In all labor there is profit; But the talk of the lips [tendeth] only to penury.
texts.pro.14.24: The crown of the wise is their riches; [But] the folly of fools is [only] folly.
texts.pro.14.25: A true witness delivereth souls; But he that uttereth lies [causeth] deceit.
texts.pro.14.26: In the fear of Jehovah is strong confidence; And his children shall have a place of refuge.
texts.pro.14.27: The fear of Jehovah is a fountain of life, That one may depart from the snares of death.
texts.pro.14.28: In the multitude of people is the king's glory; But in the want of people is the destruction of the prince.
texts.pro.14.29: He that is slow to anger is of great understanding; But he that is hasty of spirit exalteth folly.
texts.pro.14.30: A tranquil heart is the life of the flesh; But envy is the rottenness of the bones.
texts.pro.14.31: He that oppresseth the poor reproacheth his Maker; But he that hath mercy on the needy honoreth him.
texts.pro.14.32: The wicked is thrust down in his evil-doing; But the righteous hath a refuge in his death.
texts.pro.14.33: Wisdom resteth in the heart of him that hath understanding; But [that which is] in the inward part of fools is made known.
texts.pro.14.34: Righteousness exalteth a nation; But sin is a reproach to any people.
texts.pro.14.35: The king's favor is toward a servant that dealeth wisely; But his wrath will be [against] him that causeth shame.
texts.pro.15.1: A soft answer turneth away wrath; But a grievous word stirreth up anger.
texts.pro.15.2: The tongue of the wise uttereth knowledge aright; But the mouth of fools poureth out folly.
texts.pro.15.3: The eyes of Jehovah are in every place, Keeping watch upon the evil and the good.
texts.pro.15.4: A gentle tongue is a tree of life; But perverseness therein is a breaking of the spirit.
texts.pro.15.5: A fool despiseth his father's correction; But he that regardeth reproof getteth prudence.
texts.pro.15.6: In the house of the righteous is much treasure; But in the revenues of the wicked is trouble.
texts.pro.15.7: The lips of the wise disperse knowledge; But the heart of the foolish [doeth] not so.
texts.pro.15.8: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination to Jehovah; But the prayer of the upright is his delight.
texts.pro.15.9: The way of the wicked is an abomination to Jehovah; But he loveth him that followeth after righteousness.
texts.pro.15.10: There is grievous correction for him that forsaketh the way; [And] he that hateth reproof shall die.
texts.pro.15.11: Sheol and Abaddon are before Jehovah: How much more then the hearts of the children of men!
texts.pro.15.12: A scoffer loveth not to be reproved; He will not go unto the wise.
texts.pro.15.13: A glad heart maketh a cheerful countenance; But by sorrow of heart the spirit is broken.
texts.pro.15.14: The heart of him that hath understanding seeketh knowledge; But the mouth of fools feedeth on folly.
texts.pro.15.15: All the days of the afflicted are evil; But he that is of a cheerful heart [hath] a continual feast.
texts.pro.15.16: Better is little, with the fear of Jehovah, Than great treasure and trouble therewith.
texts.pro.15.17: Better is a dinner of herbs, where love is, Than a stalled ox and hatred therewith.
texts.pro.15.18: A wrathful man stirreth up contention; But he that is slow to anger appeaseth strife.
texts.pro.15.19: The way of the sluggard is as a hedge of thorns; But the path of the upright is made a highway.
texts.pro.15.20: A wise son maketh a glad father; But a foolish man despiseth his mother.
texts.pro.15.21: Folly is joy to him that is void of wisdom; But a man of understanding maketh straight his going.
texts.pro.15.22: Where there is no counsel, purposes are disappointed; But in the multitude of counsellors they are established.
texts.pro.15.23: A man hath joy in the answer of his mouth; And a word in due season, how good is it!
texts.pro.15.24: To the wise the way of life [goeth] upward, That he may depart from Sheol beneath.
texts.pro.15.25: Jehovah will root up the house of the proud; But he will establish the border of the widow.
texts.pro.15.26: Evil devices are an abomination to Jehovah; But pleasant words [are] pure.
texts.pro.15.27: He that is greedy of gain troubleth his own house; But he that hateth bribes shall live.
texts.pro.15.28: The heart of the righteous studieth to answer; But the mouth of the wicked poureth out evil things.
texts.pro.15.29: Jehovah is far from the wicked; But he heareth the prayer of the righteous.
texts.pro.15.30: The light of the eyes rejoiceth the heart; [And] good tidings make the bones fat.
texts.pro.15.31: The ear that hearkeneth to the reproof of life Shall abide among the wise.
texts.pro.15.32: He that refuseth correction despiseth his own soul; But he that hearkeneth to reproof getteth understanding.
texts.pro.15.33: The fear of Jehovah is the instruction of wisdom; And before honor [goeth] humility.
texts.pro.16.1: The plans of the heart belong to man; But the answer of the tongue is from Jehovah.
texts.pro.16.2: All the ways of a man are clean in his own eyes; But Jehovah weigheth the spirits.
texts.pro.16.3: Commit thy works unto Jehovah, And thy purposes shall be established.
texts.pro.16.4: Jehovah hath made everything for its own end; Yea, even the wicked for the day of evil.
texts.pro.16.5: Every one that is proud in heart is an abomination to Jehovah: [Though] hand [join] in hand, he shall not be unpunished.
texts.pro.16.6: By mercy and truth iniquity is atoned for; And by the fear of Jehovah men depart from evil.
texts.pro.16.7: When a man's ways please Jehovah, He maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him.
texts.pro.16.8: Better is a little, with righteousness, Than great revenues with injustice.
texts.pro.16.9: A man's heart deviseth his way; But Jehovah directeth his steps.
texts.pro.16.10: A divine sentence is in the lips of the king; His mouth shall not transgress in judgment.
texts.pro.16.11: A just balance and scales are Jehovah's; All the weights of the bag are his work.
texts.pro.16.12: It is an abomination to kings to commit wickedness; For the throne is established by righteousness.
texts.pro.16.13: Righteous lips are the delight of kings; And they love him that speaketh right.
texts.pro.16.14: The wrath of a king is [as] messengers of death; But a wise man will pacify it.
texts.pro.16.15: In the light of the king's countenance is life; And his favor is as a cloud of the latter rain.
texts.pro.16.16: How much better is it to get wisdom than gold! Yea, to get understanding is rather to be chosen than silver.
texts.pro.16.17: The highway of the upright is to depart from evil: He that keepeth his way preserveth his soul.
texts.pro.16.18: Pride [goeth] before destruction, And a haughty spirit before a fall.
texts.pro.16.19: Better it is to be of a lowly spirit with the poor, Than to divide the spoil with the proud.
texts.pro.16.20: He that giveth heed unto the word shall find good; And whoso trusteth in Jehovah, happy is he.
texts.pro.16.21: The wise in heart shall be called prudent; And the sweetness of the lips increaseth learning.
texts.pro.16.22: Understanding is a well-spring of life unto him that hath it; But the correction of fools is [their] folly.
texts.pro.16.23: The heart of the wise instructeth his mouth, And addeth learning to his lips.
texts.pro.16.24: Pleasant words are [as] a honeycomb, Sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.
texts.pro.16.25: There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, But the end thereof are the ways of death.
texts.pro.16.26: The appetite of the laboring man laboreth for him; For his mouth urgeth him [thereto].
texts.pro.16.27: A worthless man deviseth mischief; And in his lips there is as a scorching fire.
texts.pro.16.28: A perverse man scattereth abroad strife; And a whisperer separateth chief friends.
texts.pro.16.29: A man of violence enticeth his neighbor, And leadeth him in a way that is not good.
texts.pro.16.30: He that shutteth his eyes, [it is] to devise perverse things: He that compresseth his lips bringeth evil to pass.
texts.pro.16.31: The hoary head is a crown of glory; It shall be found in the way of righteousness.
texts.pro.16.32: He that is slow to anger is better than the mighty; And he that ruleth his spirit, than he that taketh a city.
texts.pro.16.33: The lot is cast into the lap; But the whole disposing thereof is of Jehovah.
texts.pro.17.1: Better is a dry morsel, and quietness therewith, Than a house full of feasting with strife.
texts.pro.17.2: A servant that dealeth wisely shall have rule over a son that causeth shame, And shall have part in the inheritance among the brethren.
texts.pro.17.3: The refining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold; But Jehovah trieth the hearts.
texts.pro.17.4: An evil-doer giveth heed to wicked lips; [And] a liar giveth ear to a mischievous tongue.
texts.pro.17.5: Whoso mocketh the poor reproacheth his Maker; [And] he that is glad at calamity shall not be unpunished.
texts.pro.17.6: Children's children are the crown of old men; And the glory of children are their fathers.
texts.pro.17.7: Excellent speech becometh not a fool; Much less do lying lips a prince.
texts.pro.17.8: A bribe is [as] a precious stone in the eyes of him that hath it; Whithersoever it turneth, it prospereth.
texts.pro.17.9: He that covereth a transgression seeketh love; But he that harpeth on a matter separateth chief friends.
texts.pro.17.10: A rebuke entereth deeper into one that hath understanding Than a hundred stripes into a fool.
texts.pro.17.11: An evil man seeketh only rebellion; Therefore a cruel messenger shall be sent against him.
texts.pro.17.12: Let a bear robbed of her whelps meet a man, Rather than a fool in his folly.
texts.pro.17.13: Whoso rewardeth evil for good, Evil shall not depart from his house.
texts.pro.17.14: The beginning of strife is [as] when one letteth out water: Therefore leave off contention, before there is quarrelling.
texts.pro.17.15: He that justifieth the wicked, and he that condemneth the righteous, Both of them alike are an abomination to Jehovah.
texts.pro.17.16: Wherefore is there a price in the hand of a fool to buy wisdom, Seeing he hath no understanding?
texts.pro.17.17: A friend loveth at all times; And a brother is born for adversity.
texts.pro.17.18: A man void of understanding striketh hands, And becometh surety in the presence of his neighbor.
texts.pro.17.19: He loveth transgression that loveth strife: He that raiseth high his gate seeketh destruction.
texts.pro.17.20: He that hath a wayward heart findeth no good; And he that hath a perverse tongue falleth into mischief.
texts.pro.17.21: He that begetteth a fool [doeth it] to his sorrow; And the father of a fool hath no joy.
texts.pro.17.22: A cheerful heart is a good medicine; But a broken spirit drieth up the bones.
texts.pro.17.23: A wicked man receiveth a bribe out of the bosom, To pervert the ways of justice.
texts.pro.17.24: Wisdom is before the face of him that hath understanding; But the eyes of a fool are in the ends of the earth.
texts.pro.17.25: A foolish son is a grief to his father, And bitterness to her that bare him.
texts.pro.17.26: Also to punish the righteous is not good, [Nor] to smite the noble for [their] uprightness.
texts.pro.17.27: He that spareth his words hath knowledge; And he that is of a cool spirit is a man of understanding.
texts.pro.17.28: Even a fool, when he holdeth his peace, is counted wise; When he shutteth his lips, he is [esteemed as] prudent.
texts.pro.18.1: He that separateth himself seeketh [his own] desire, And rageth against all sound wisdom.
texts.pro.18.2: A fool hath no delight in understanding, But only that his heart may reveal itself.
texts.pro.18.3: When the wicked cometh, there cometh also contempt, And with ignominy [cometh] reproach.
texts.pro.18.4: The words of a man's mouth are [as] deep waters; The wellspring of wisdom is [as] a flowing brook.
texts.pro.18.5: To respect the person of the wicked is not good, [Nor] to turn aside the righteous in judgment.
texts.pro.18.6: A fool's lips enter into contention, And his mouth calleth for stripes.
texts.pro.18.7: A fool's mouth is his destruction, And his lips are the snare of his soul.
texts.pro.18.8: The words of a whisperer are as dainty morsels, And they go down into the innermost parts.
texts.pro.18.9: He also that is slack in his work Is brother to him that is a destroyer.
texts.pro.18.10: The name of Jehovah is a strong tower; The righteous runneth into it, and is safe.
texts.pro.18.11: The rich man's wealth is his strong city, And as a high wall in his own imagination.
texts.pro.18.12: Before destruction the heart of man is haughty; And before honor [goeth] humility.
texts.pro.18.13: He that giveth answer before he heareth, It is folly and shame unto him.
texts.pro.18.14: The spirit of a man will sustain his infirmity; But a broken spirit who can bear?
texts.pro.18.15: The heart of the prudent getteth knowledge; And the ear of the wise seeketh knowledge.
texts.pro.18.16: A man's gift maketh room for him, And bringeth him before great men.
texts.pro.18.17: He that pleadeth his cause first [seemeth] just; But his neighbor cometh and searcheth him out.
texts.pro.18.18: The lot causeth contentions to cease, And parteth between the mighty.
texts.pro.18.19: A brother offended [is harder to be won] than a strong city; And [such] contentions are like the bars of a castle.
texts.pro.18.20: A man's belly shall be filled with the fruit of his mouth; With the increase of his lips shall he be satisfied.
texts.pro.18.21: Death and life are in the power of the tongue; And they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof.
texts.pro.18.22: Whoso findeth a wife findeth a good thing, And obtaineth favor of Jehovah.
texts.pro.18.23: The poor useth entreaties; But the rich answereth roughly.
texts.pro.18.24: He that maketh many friends [doeth it] to his own destruction; But there is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother.
texts.pro.19.1: Better is the poor that walketh in his integrity Than he that is perverse in his lips and is a fool.
texts.pro.19.2: Also, that the soul be without knowledge is not good; And he that hasteth with his feet sinneth.
texts.pro.19.3: The foolishness of man subverteth his way; And his heart fretteth against Jehovah.
texts.pro.19.4: Wealth addeth many friends; But the poor is separated from his friend.
texts.pro.19.5: A false witness shall not be unpunished; And he that uttereth lies shall not escape.
texts.pro.19.6: Many will entreat the favor of the liberal man; And every man is a friend to him that giveth gifts.
texts.pro.19.7: All the brethren of the poor do hate him: How much more do his friends go far from him! He pursueth [them with] words, [but] they are gone.
texts.pro.19.8: He that getteth wisdom loveth his own soul: He that keepeth understanding shall find good.
texts.pro.19.9: A false witness shall not be unpunished; And he that uttereth lies shall perish.
texts.pro.19.10: Delicate living is not seemly for a fool; Much less for a servant to have rule over princes.
texts.pro.19.11: The discretion of a man maketh him slow to anger; And it is his glory to pass over a transgression.
texts.pro.19.12: The king's wrath is as the roaring of a lion; But his favor is as dew upon the grass.
texts.pro.19.13: A foolish son is the calamity of his father; And the contentions of a wife are a continual dropping.
texts.pro.19.14: House and riches are an inheritance from fathers; But a prudent wife is from Jehovah.
texts.pro.19.15: Slothfulness casteth into a deep sleep; And the idle soul shall suffer hunger.
texts.pro.19.16: He that keepeth the commandment keepeth his soul; [But] he that is careless of his ways shall die.
texts.pro.19.17: He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto Jehovah, And his good deed will he pay him again.
texts.pro.19.18: Chasten thy son, seeing there is hope; nd set not thy heart on his destruction.
texts.pro.19.19: A man of great wrath shall bear the penalty; For if thou deliver [him], thou must do it yet again.
texts.pro.19.20: Hear counsel, and receive instruction, That thou mayest be wise in thy latter end.
texts.pro.19.21: There are many devices in a man's heart; But the counsel of Jehovah, that shall stand.
texts.pro.19.22: That which maketh a man to be desired is his kindness; And a poor man is better than a liar.
texts.pro.19.23: The fear of Jehovah [tendeth] to life; And he [that hath it] shall abide satisfied; He shall not be visited with evil.
texts.pro.19.24: The sluggard burieth his hand in the dish, And will not so much as bring it to his mouth again.
texts.pro.19.25: Smite a scoffer, and the simple will learn prudence; And reprove one that hath understanding, [and] he will understand knowledge.
texts.pro.19.26: He that doeth violence to his father, and chaseth away his mother, Is a son that causeth shame and bringeth reproach.
texts.pro.19.27: Cease, my son, to hear instruction [Only] to err from the words of knowledge.
texts.pro.19.28: A worthless witness mocketh at justice; And the mouth of the wicked swalloweth iniquity.
texts.pro.19.29: Judgments are prepared for scoffers, And stripes for the back of fools.
texts.pro.20.1: Wine is a mocker, strong drink a brawler; And whosoever erreth thereby is not wise.
texts.pro.20.2: The terror of a king is as the roaring of a lion: He that provoketh him to anger sinneth [against] his own life.
texts.pro.20.3: It is an honor for a man to keep aloof from strife; But every fool will be quarrelling.
texts.pro.20.4: The sluggard will not plow by reason of the winter; Therefore he shall beg in harvest, and have nothing.
texts.pro.20.5: Counsel in the heart of man is [like] deep water; But a man of understanding will draw it out.
texts.pro.20.6: Most men will proclaim every one his own kindness; But a faithful man who can find?
texts.pro.20.7: A righteous man that walketh in his integrity, Blessed are his children after him.
texts.pro.20.8: A king that sitteth on the throne of judgment Scattereth away all evil with his eyes.
texts.pro.20.9: Who can say, I have made my heart clean, I am pure from my sin?
texts.pro.20.10: Diverse weights, and diverse measures, Both of them alike are an abomination to Jehovah.
texts.pro.20.11: Even a child maketh himself known by his doings, Whether his work be pure, and whether it be right.
texts.pro.20.12: The hearing ear, and the seeing eye, Jehovah hath made even both of them.
texts.pro.20.13: Love not sleep, let thou come to poverty; Open thine eyes, [and] thou shalt be satisfied with bread.
texts.pro.20.14: It is bad, it is bad, saith the buyer; But when he is gone his way, then he boasteth.
texts.pro.20.15: There is gold, and abundance of rubies; But the lips of knowledge are a precious jewel.
texts.pro.20.16: Take his garment that is surety for a stranger; And hold him in pledge [that is surety] for foreigners.
texts.pro.20.17: Bread of falsehood is sweet to a man; But afterwards his mouth shall be filled with gravel.
texts.pro.20.18: Every purpose is established by counsel; And by wise guidance make thou war.
texts.pro.20.19: He that goeth about as a tale-bearer revealeth secrets; Therefore company not with him that openeth wide his lips.
texts.pro.20.20: Whoso curseth his father or his mother, His lamp shall be put out in blackness of darkness.
texts.pro.20.21: An inheritance [may be] gotten hastily at the beginning; But the end thereof shall not be blessed.
texts.pro.20.22: Say not thou, I will recompense evil: Wait for Jehovah, and he will save thee.
texts.pro.20.23: Diverse weights are an abomination to Jehovah; And a false balance is not good.
texts.pro.20.24: A man's goings are of Jehovah; How then can man understand his way?
texts.pro.20.25: It is a snare to a man rashly to say, [It is] holy, And after vows to make inquiry.
texts.pro.20.26: A wise king winnoweth the wicked, And bringeth the [threshing] -wheel over them.
texts.pro.20.27: The spirit of man is the lamp of Jehovah, Searching all his innermost parts.
texts.pro.20.28: Kindness and truth preserve the king; And his throne is upholden by kindness.
texts.pro.20.29: The glory of young men is their strength; And the beauty of old men is the hoary head.
texts.pro.20.30: Stripes that wound cleanse away evil; And strokes [reach] the innermost parts.
texts.pro.21.1: The king's heart is in the hand of Jehovah as the watercourses: He turneth it whithersoever he will.
texts.pro.21.2: Every way of a man is right in his own eyes; But Jehovah weigheth the hearts.
texts.pro.21.3: To do righteousness and justice Is more acceptable to Jehovah than sacrifice.
texts.pro.21.4: A high look, and a proud heart, [Even] the lamp of the wicked, is sin.
texts.pro.21.5: The thoughts of the diligent [tend] only to plenteousness; But every one that is hasty [hasteth] only to want.
texts.pro.21.6: The getting of treasures by a lying tongue Is a vapor driven to and fro by them that seek death.
texts.pro.21.7: The violence of the wicked shall sweep them away, Because they refuse to do justice.
texts.pro.21.8: The way of him that is laden with guilt is exceeding crooked; But as for the pure, his work is right.
texts.pro.21.9: It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop, Than with a contentious woman in a wide house.
texts.pro.21.10: The soul of the wicked desireth evil: His neighbor findeth no favor in his eyes.
texts.pro.21.11: When the scoffer is punished, the simple is made wise; And when the wise is instructed, he receiveth knowledge.
texts.pro.21.12: The righteous man considereth the house of the wicked, [How] the wicked are overthrown to [their] ruin.
texts.pro.21.13: Whoso stoppeth his ears at the cry of the poor, He also shall cry, but shall not be heard.
texts.pro.21.14: A gift in secret pacifieth anger; And a present in the bosom, strong wrath.
texts.pro.21.15: It is joy to the righteous to do justice; But it is a destruction to the workers of iniquity.
texts.pro.21.16: The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding Shall rest in the assembly of the dead.
texts.pro.21.17: He that loveth pleasure shall be a poor man: He that loveth wine and oil shall not be rich.
texts.pro.21.18: The wicked is a ransom for the righteous; And the treacherous [cometh] in the stead of the upright.
texts.pro.21.19: It is better to dwell in a desert land, Than with a contentious and fretful woman.
texts.pro.21.20: There is precious treasure and oil in the dwelling of the wise; But a foolish man swalloweth it up.
texts.pro.21.21: He that followeth after righteousness and kindness Findeth life, righteousness, and honor.
texts.pro.21.22: A wise man scaleth the city of the mighty, And bringeth down the strength of the confidence thereof.
texts.pro.21.23: Whoso keepeth his mouth and his tongue Keepeth his soul from troubles.
texts.pro.21.24: The proud and haughty man, scoffer is his name; He worketh in the arrogance of pride.
texts.pro.21.25: The desire of the sluggard killeth him; For his hands refuse to labor.
texts.pro.21.26: There is that coveteth greedily all the day long; But the righteous giveth and withholdeth not.
texts.pro.21.27: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination: How much more, when he bringeth it with a wicked mind!
texts.pro.21.28: A false witness shall perish; But the man that heareth shall speak so as to endure.
texts.pro.21.29: A wicked man hardeneth his face; But as for the upright, he establisheth his ways.
texts.pro.21.30: There is no wisdom nor understanding Nor counsel against Jehovah.
texts.pro.21.31: The horse is prepared against the day of battle; But victory is of Jehovah.
texts.pro.22.1: A [good] name is rather to be chosen than great riches, [And] loving favor rather than silver and gold.
texts.pro.22.2: The rich and the poor meet together: Jehovah is the maker of them all.
texts.pro.22.3: A prudent man seeth the evil, and hideth himself; But the simple pass on, and suffer for it.
texts.pro.22.4: The reward of humility [and] the fear of Jehovah [Is] riches, and honor, and life.
texts.pro.22.5: Thorns [and] snares are in the way of the perverse: He that keepeth his soul shall be far from them.
texts.pro.22.6: Train up a child in the way he should go, And even when he is old he will not depart from it.
texts.pro.22.7: The rich ruleth over the poor; And the borrower is servant to the lender.
texts.pro.22.8: He that soweth iniquity shall reap calamity; And the rod of his wrath shall fail.
texts.pro.22.9: He that hath a bountiful eye shall be blessed; For he giveth of his bread to the poor.
texts.pro.22.10: Cast out the scoffer, and contention will go out; Yea, strife and ignominy will cease.
texts.pro.22.11: He that loveth pureness of heart, [For] the grace of his lips the king will be his friend.
texts.pro.22.12: The eyes of Jehovah preserve [him that hath] knowledge; But he overthroweth the words of the treacherous man.
texts.pro.22.13: The sluggard saith, There is a lion without: I shall be slain in the streets.
texts.pro.22.14: The mouth of strange women is a deep pit: He that is abhorred of Jehovah shall fall therein.
texts.pro.22.15: Foolishness is bound up in the heart of a child; [But] the rod of correction shall drive it far from him.
texts.pro.22.16: He that oppresseth the poor to increase his [gain], [And] he that giveth to the rich, [shall come] only to want.
texts.pro.22.17: Incline thine ear, and hear the words of the wise, And apply thy heart unto my knowledge.
texts.pro.22.18: For it is a pleasant thing if thou keep them within thee, If they be established together upon thy lips.
texts.pro.22.19: That thy trust may be in Jehovah, I have made [them] known to thee this day, even to thee.
texts.pro.22.20: Have not I written unto thee excellent things Of counsels and knowledge,
texts.pro.22.21: To make thee know the certainty of the words of truth, That thou mayest carry back words of truth to them that send thee?
texts.pro.22.22: Rob not the poor, because he is poor; Neither oppress the afflicted in the gate:
texts.pro.22.23: For Jehovah will plead their cause, And despoil of life those that despoil them.
texts.pro.22.24: Make no friendship with a man that is given to anger; And with a wrathful man thou shalt not go:
texts.pro.22.25: Lest thou learn this ways, And get a snare to thy soul.
texts.pro.22.26: Be thou not one of them that strike hands, [Or] of them that are sureties for debts.
texts.pro.22.27: If thou hast not wherewith to pay, Why should he take away thy bed from under thee?
texts.pro.22.28: Remove not the ancient landmark, Which thy fathers have set.
texts.pro.22.29: Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; He shall not stand before mean men.
texts.pro.23.1: When thou sittest to eat with a ruler, Consider diligently him that is before thee;
texts.pro.23.2: And put a knife to thy throat, If thou be a man given to appetite.
texts.pro.23.3: Be not desirous of his dainties; Seeing they are deceitful food.
texts.pro.23.4: Weary not thyself to be rich; Cease from thine own wisdom.
texts.pro.23.5: Wilt thou set thine eyes upon that which is not? For [riches] certainly make themselves wings, Like an eagle that flieth toward heaven.
texts.pro.23.6: Eat thou not the bread of him that hath an evil eye, Neither desire thou his dainties:
texts.pro.23.7: For as he thinketh within himself, so is he: Eat and drink, saith he to thee; But his heart is not with thee.
texts.pro.23.8: The morsel which thou hast eaten shalt thou vomit up, And lose thy sweet words.
texts.pro.23.9: Speak not in the hearing of a fool; For he will despise the wisdom of thy words.
texts.pro.23.10: Remove not the ancient landmark; And enter not into the fields of the fatherless:
texts.pro.23.11: For their Redeemer is strong; He will plead their cause against thee.
texts.pro.23.12: Apply thy heart unto instruction, And thine ears to the words of knowledge.
texts.pro.23.13: Withhold not correction from the child; [For] if thou beat him with the rod, he will not die.
texts.pro.23.14: Thou shalt beat him with the rod, And shalt deliver his soul from Sheol.
texts.pro.23.15: My son, if thy heart be wise, My heart will be glad, even mine:
texts.pro.23.16: Yea, my heart will rejoice, When thy lips speak right things.
texts.pro.23.17: Let not thy heart envy sinners; But [be thou] in the fear of Jehovah all the day long:
texts.pro.23.18: For surely there is a reward; And thy hope shall not be cut off.
texts.pro.23.19: Hear thou, my son, and be wise, And guide thy heart in the way.
texts.pro.23.20: Be not among winebibbers, Among gluttonous eaters of flesh:
texts.pro.23.21: For the drunkard and the glutton shall come to poverty; And drowsiness will clothe [a man] with rags.
texts.pro.23.22: Hearken unto thy father that begat thee, And despise not thy mother when she is old.
texts.pro.23.23: Buy the truth, and sell it not; [Yea], wisdom, and instruction, and understanding.
texts.pro.23.24: The father of the righteous will greatly rejoice; And he that begetteth a wise child will have joy of him.
texts.pro.23.25: Let thy father and thy mother be glad, And let her that bare thee rejoice.
texts.pro.23.26: My son, give me thy heart; And let thine eyes delight in my ways.
texts.pro.23.27: For a harlot is a deep ditch; And a foreign woman is a narrow pit.
texts.pro.23.28: Yea, she lieth in wait as a robber, And increaseth the treacherous among men.
texts.pro.23.29: Who hath woe? who hath sorrow? who hath contentions? Who hath complaining? who hath wounds without cause? Who hath redness of eyes?
