texts.pro.28.25: He that is of a proud heart stirreth up strife: but he that putteth his trust in the LORD shall be made fat.
texts.pro.28.26: He that trusteth in his own heart is a fool: but whoever walketh wisely, he shall be delivered.
texts.pro.28.27: He that giveth to the poor shall not want: but he that hideth his eyes shall have many a curse.
texts.pro.28.28: When the wicked rise, men hide themselves: but when they perish, the righteous increase.
texts.pro.29.1: He, that being often reproved hardeneth his neck, shall suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy.
texts.pro.29.2: When the righteous are in authority, the people rejoice: but when the wicked beareth rule, the people mourn.
texts.pro.29.3: He that loveth wisdom rejoiceth his father: but he that keepeth company with harlots spendeth his substance.
texts.pro.29.4: The king by judgment establisheth the land: but he that receiveth gifts overthroweth it.
texts.pro.29.5: A man that flattereth his neighbor spreadeth a net for his feet.
texts.pro.29.6: In the transgression of an evil man there is a snare: but the righteous doth sing and rejoice.
texts.pro.29.7: The righteous considereth the cause of the poor: but the wicked regardeth not to know it.
texts.pro.29.8: Scornful men bring a city into a snare: but wise men turn away wrath.
texts.pro.29.9: If a wise man contendeth with a foolish man, whether he rageth or laugheth, there is no rest.
texts.pro.29.10: The blood-thirsty hate the upright: but the just seek his soul.
texts.pro.29.11: A fool uttereth all his mind: but a wise man keepeth it in till afterwards.
texts.pro.29.12: If a ruler hearkeneth to lies, all his servants are wicked.
texts.pro.29.13: The poor and the deceitful man meet together: the LORD enlighteneth both their eyes.
texts.pro.29.14: The king that faithfully judgeth the poor, his throne shall be established for ever.
texts.pro.29.15: The rod and reproof give wisdom: but a child left to himself bringeth his mother to shame.
texts.pro.29.16: When the wicked are multiplied, transgression increaseth: but the righteous shall see their fall.
texts.pro.29.17: Correct thy son, and he shall give thee rest; yes, he shall give delight to thy soul.
texts.pro.29.18: Where there is no vision, the people perish: but he that keepeth the law, happy is he.
texts.pro.29.19: A servant will not be corrected by words: for though he understandeth, he will not answer.
texts.pro.29.20: Seest thou a man that is hasty in his words? there is more hope of a fool than of him.
texts.pro.29.21: He that delicately bringeth up his servant from a child shall have him at length become his son.
texts.pro.29.22: An angry man stirreth up strife, and a furious man aboundeth in transgression.
texts.pro.29.23: A man's pride shall bring him low: but honor shall uphold the humble in spirit.
texts.pro.29.24: Whoever is partner with a thief, hateth his own soul: he heareth cursing, and discloseth it not.
texts.pro.29.25: The fear of man bringeth a snare: but he who putteth his trust in the LORD shall be safe.
texts.pro.29.26: Many seek the ruler's favor; but every man's judgment cometh from the LORD.
texts.pro.29.27: An unjust man is an abomination to the just: and he that is upright in the way is abomination to the wicked.
texts.pro.30.1: The words of Agur the son of Jakeh, even the prophecy: the man spoke to Ithiel, even to Ithiel and Ucal,
texts.pro.30.2: Surely I am more brutish than any man, and have not the understanding of a man.
texts.pro.30.3: I neither learned wisdom, nor have the knowledge of the holy.
texts.pro.30.4: Who hath ascended into heaven, or descended? who hath gathered the wind in his fists? who hath bound the waters in a garment? who hath established all the ends of the earth? what is his name, and what is his son's name, if thou canst tell?
texts.pro.30.5: Every word of God is pure: he is a shield to them that put their trust in him.
texts.pro.30.6: Add thou not to his words, lest he reprove thee, and thou be found a liar.
texts.pro.30.7: Two things have I required of thee; deny them not to me before I die:
texts.pro.30.8: Remove far from me vanity and lies; give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with food convenient for me:
texts.pro.30.9: Lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, Who is the LORD? or lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God in vain.
texts.pro.30.10: Accuse not a servant to his master, lest he curse thee, and thou be found guilty.
texts.pro.30.11: There is a generation that curseth their father, and doth not bless their mother.
texts.pro.30.12: There is a generation that are pure in their own eyes, and yet are not washed from their filthiness.
texts.pro.30.13: There is a generation, O how lofty are their eyes! and their eyelids are lifted up.
texts.pro.30.14: There is a generation, whose teeth are as swords, and their jaw-teeth as knives, to devour the poor from off the earth, and the needy from among men.
texts.pro.30.15: The horse-leech hath two daughters, crying, Give, give. There are three things that are never satisfied, yes, four things say not, It is enough:
texts.pro.30.16: The grave; and the barren womb; the earth that is not filled with water; and the fire that saith not, It is enough.
texts.pro.30.17: The eye that mocketh at its father, and despiseth to obey its mother, the ravens of the valley shall pick it out, and the young eagles shall eat it.
texts.pro.30.18: There are three things which are too wonderful for me, yes, four which I know not:
texts.pro.30.19: The way of an eagle in the air; the way of a serpent upon a rock; the way of a ship in the midst of the sea; and the way of a man with a maid.
texts.pro.30.20: Such is the way of an adulterous woman; she eateth, and wipeth her mouth, and saith, I have done no wickedness.
texts.pro.30.21: For three things the earth is disquieted, and for four which it cannot bear:
texts.pro.30.22: For a servant when he reigneth; and a fool when he is filled with food.
texts.pro.30.23: For an odious woman when she is married; and a handmaid that is heir to her mistress.
texts.pro.30.24: There are four things which are little upon the earth, but they are very wise:
texts.pro.30.25: The ants are a people not strong, yet they prepare their food in the summer;
texts.pro.30.26: The conies are but a feeble people, yet they make their houses in the rocks;
texts.pro.30.27: The locusts have no king, yet go they forth all of them by bands;
texts.pro.30.28: The spider taketh hold with her hands, and is in king's palaces.
texts.pro.30.29: There are three things which go well, yes, four are comely in going:
texts.pro.30.30: A lion, which is strongest among beasts, and turneth not away for any;
texts.pro.30.31: A greyhound; a he-goat also; and a king, against whom there is no rising up.
texts.pro.30.32: If thou hast done foolishly in lifting up thyself, or if thou hast thought evil, lay thy hand upon thy mouth.
texts.pro.30.33: Surely the churning of milk bringeth forth butter, and the wringing of the nose bringeth forth blood: so the forcing of wrath bringeth forth strife.
texts.pro.31.1: The words of king Lemuel, the prophecy that his mother taught him.
texts.pro.31.2: What, my son? and what, the son of my womb? and what, the son of my vows?
texts.pro.31.3: Give not thy strength to women, nor thy ways to that which destroyeth kings.
texts.pro.31.4: It is not for kings, O Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine; nor for princes strong drink:
texts.pro.31.5: Lest they drink, and forget the law, and pervert the judgment of any of the afflicted.
texts.pro.31.6: Give strong drink to him that is ready to perish, and wine to those that are of heavy hearts.
texts.pro.31.7: Let him drink, and forget his poverty, and remember his misery no more.
texts.pro.31.8: Open thy mouth for the dumb in the cause of all such as are appointed to destruction.
texts.pro.31.9: Open thy mouth, judge righteously, and plead the cause of the poor and needy.
texts.pro.31.10: Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price is far above rubies.
texts.pro.31.11: The heart of her husband doth safely trust in her, so that he shall have no need of spoil.
texts.pro.31.12: She will do him good and not evil all the days of her life.
texts.pro.31.13: She seeketh wool, and flax, and worketh willingly with her hands.
texts.pro.31.14: She is like the merchant's ships; she bringeth her food from afar.
texts.pro.31.15: She riseth also while it is yet night, and giveth food to her household, and a portion to her maidens.
texts.pro.31.16: She considereth a field, and buyeth it: with the fruit of her hands she planteth a vineyard.
texts.pro.31.17: She girdeth her loins with strength, and strengtheneth her arms.
texts.pro.31.18: She perceiveth that her merchandise is good: her candle goeth not out by night.
texts.pro.31.19: She layeth her hands to the spindle, and her hands hold the distaff.
texts.pro.31.20: She stretcheth out her hand to the poor; yes, she reacheth forth her hands to the needy.
texts.pro.31.21: She is not afraid of the snow for her household: for all her household are clothed with scarlet.
texts.pro.31.22: She maketh herself coverings of tapestry; her clothing is silk and purple.
texts.pro.31.23: Her husband is known in the gates, when he sitteth among the elders of the land.
texts.pro.31.24: She maketh fine linen, and selleth it; and delivereth girdles to the merchant.
texts.pro.31.25: Strength and honor are her clothing; and she shall rejoice in time to come.
texts.pro.31.26: She openeth her mouth with wisdom; and on her tongue is the law of kindness.
texts.pro.31.27: She looketh well to the ways of her household, and eateth not the bread of idleness.
texts.pro.31.28: Her children rise up, and call her blessed; her husband also, and he praiseth her.
texts.pro.31.29: Many daughters have done virtuously, but thou excellest them all.
texts.pro.31.30: Favor is deceitful, and beauty is vain: but a woman that feareth the LORD, she shall be praised.
texts.pro.31.31: Give her of the fruit of her hands; and let her own works praise her in the gates.

texts.pro.1.1: Proverbs of Solomon, son of David, king of Israel:
texts.pro.1.2: to know wisdom and instruction; to discern the words of understanding;
texts.pro.1.3: to receive the instruction of wisdom, righteousness and judgment, and equity;
texts.pro.1.4: to give prudence to the simple, to the young man knowledge and discretion.
texts.pro.1.5: He that is wise will hear, and will increase learning; and the intelligent will gain wise counsels:
texts.pro.1.6: to understand a proverb and an allegory, the words of the wise and their enigmas.
texts.pro.1.7: The fear of Jehovah is the beginning of knowledge: fools despise wisdom and instruction.
texts.pro.1.8: Hear, my son, the instruction of thy father, and forsake not the teaching of thy mother;
texts.pro.1.9: for they shall be a garland of grace unto thy head, and chains about thy neck.
texts.pro.1.10: My son, if sinners entice thee, consent not.
texts.pro.1.11: If they say, Come with us, let us lay wait for blood, let us lurk secretly for the innocent without cause;
texts.pro.1.12: let us swallow them up alive as Sheol, and whole, as those that go down into the pit;
texts.pro.1.13: we shall find all precious substance, we shall fill our houses with spoil:
texts.pro.1.14: cast in thy lot among us; we will all have one purse:
texts.pro.1.15: -- my son, walk not in the way with them, keep back thy foot from their path;
texts.pro.1.16: for their feet run to evil, and they make haste to shed blood.
texts.pro.1.17: For in vain the net is spread in the sight of anything which hath wings.
texts.pro.1.18: And these lay wait for their own blood; they lurk secretly for their own lives.
texts.pro.1.19: So are the paths of every one that is greedy of gain: it taketh away the life of its possessors.
texts.pro.1.20: Wisdom crieth without; she raiseth her voice in the broadways;
texts.pro.1.21: she calleth in the chief [place] of concourse, in the entry of the gates; in the city she uttereth her words:
texts.pro.1.22: How long, simple ones, will ye love simpleness, and scorners take pleasure in their scorning, and the foolish hate knowledge?
texts.pro.1.23: Turn you at my reproof: behold, I will pour forth my spirit unto you, I will make known to you my words.
texts.pro.1.24: Because I have called, and ye refused; I have stretched out my hand, and no one regarded;
texts.pro.1.25: and ye have rejected all my counsel, and would none of my reproof:
texts.pro.1.26: I also will laugh in your calamity, I will mock when your fear cometh;
texts.pro.1.27: when your fear cometh as sudden destruction, and your calamity cometh as a whirlwind; when distress and anguish come upon you:
texts.pro.1.28: -- then will they call upon me, but I will not answer; they will seek me early, and shall not find me.
texts.pro.1.29: Because they hated knowledge, and did not choose the fear of Jehovah;
texts.pro.1.30: they would none of my counsel, they despised all my reproof:
texts.pro.1.31: therefore shall they eat of the fruit of their way, and be filled with their own devices.
texts.pro.1.32: For the turning away of the simple shall slay them, and the prosperity of the foolish shall cause them to perish.
texts.pro.1.33: But whoso hearkeneth unto me shall dwell safely, and shall be at rest from fear of evil.
texts.pro.2.1: My son, if thou receivest my words, and layest up my commandments with thee,
texts.pro.2.2: so that thou incline thine ear unto wisdom [and] thou apply thy heart to understanding;
texts.pro.2.3: yea, if thou criest after discernment [and] liftest up thy voice to understanding;
texts.pro.2.4: if thou seekest her as silver and searchest for her as for hidden treasures:
texts.pro.2.5: then shalt thou understand the fear of Jehovah, and find the knowledge of God.
texts.pro.2.6: For Jehovah giveth wisdom; out of his mouth [come] knowledge and understanding.
texts.pro.2.7: He layeth up sound wisdom for the upright; [he] is a shield to them that walk in integrity;
texts.pro.2.8: guarding the paths of just judgment and keeping the way of his godly ones.
texts.pro.2.9: Then shalt thou understand righteousness and judgment and equity: every good path.
texts.pro.2.10: When wisdom entereth into thy heart and knowledge is pleasant unto thy soul,
texts.pro.2.11: discretion shall keep thee, understanding shall preserve thee:
texts.pro.2.12: To deliver thee from the way of evil, from the man that speaketh froward things;
texts.pro.2.13: [from those] who leave the paths of uprightness, to walk in the ways of darkness;
texts.pro.2.14: who rejoice to do evil, [and] delight in the frowardness of evil;
texts.pro.2.15: whose paths are crooked, and who are perverted in their course:
texts.pro.2.16: To deliver thee from the strange woman, from the stranger who flattereth with her words;
texts.pro.2.17: who forsaketh the guide of her youth, and forgetteth the covenant of her God;
texts.pro.2.18: -- for her house inclineth unto death, and her paths unto the dead;
texts.pro.2.19: none that go unto her return again, neither do they attain to the paths of life:
texts.pro.2.20: -- that thou mayest walk in the way of the good, and keep the paths of the righteous.
texts.pro.2.21: For the upright shall dwell in the land, and the perfect shall remain in it;
texts.pro.2.22: but the wicked shall be cut off from the land, and the unfaithful shall be plucked up out of it.
texts.pro.3.1: My son, forget not my teaching, and let thy heart observe my commandments;
texts.pro.3.2: for length of days, and years of life, and peace shall they add to thee.
texts.pro.3.3: Let not loving-kindness and truth forsake thee; bind them about thy neck, write them upon the tablet of thy heart:
texts.pro.3.4: and thou shalt find favour and good understanding in the sight of God and man.
texts.pro.3.5: Confide in Jehovah with all thy heart, and lean not unto thine own intelligence;
texts.pro.3.6: in all thy ways acknowledge him, and he will make plain thy paths.
texts.pro.3.7: Be not wise in thine own eyes; fear Jehovah, and depart from evil:
texts.pro.3.8: it shall be health for thy navel, and moisture for thy bones.
texts.pro.3.9: Honour Jehovah with thy substance, and with the first-fruits of all thine increase;
texts.pro.3.10: so shall thy barns be filled with plenty, and thy vats shall overflow with new wine.
texts.pro.3.11: My son, despise not the instruction of Jehovah, neither be weary of his chastisement;
texts.pro.3.12: for whom Jehovah loveth he chasteneth, even as a father the son in whom he delighteth.
texts.pro.3.13: Blessed is the man that findeth wisdom, and the man that getteth understanding.
texts.pro.3.14: For the gain thereof is better than the gain of silver, and her revenue than fine gold.
texts.pro.3.15: She is more precious than rubies; and all the things thou canst desire are not equal unto her.
texts.pro.3.16: Length of days is in her right hand; in her left hand riches and honour.
texts.pro.3.17: Her ways are ways of pleasantness, and all her paths are peace.
texts.pro.3.18: She is a tree of life to them that lay hold upon her; and happy is he that retaineth her.
texts.pro.3.19: Jehovah by wisdom founded the earth; by understanding he established the heavens.
texts.pro.3.20: By his knowledge the deeps were broken up, and the skies drop down the dew.
texts.pro.3.21: My son, let them not depart from thine eyes; keep sound wisdom and discretion:
texts.pro.3.22: so shall they be life unto thy soul, and grace unto thy neck.
texts.pro.3.23: Then shalt thou walk in thy way securely, and thy foot shall not stumble;
texts.pro.3.24: when thou liest down, thou shalt not be afraid, but thou shalt lie down and thy sleep shall be sweet.
texts.pro.3.25: Be not afraid of sudden fear, neither of the destruction of the wicked, when it cometh;
texts.pro.3.26: for Jehovah shall be thy confidence, and he will keep thy foot from being taken.
texts.pro.3.27: Withhold not good from them to whom it is due, when it is in the power of thy hand to do it.
texts.pro.3.28: Say not unto thy neighbour, Go, and come again, and to-morrow I will give, when thou hast it by thee.
texts.pro.3.29: Devise not evil against thy neighbour, seeing he dwelleth securely by thee.
texts.pro.3.30: Strive not with a man without cause, if he have done thee no harm.
texts.pro.3.31: Envy not the man of violence, and choose none of his ways.
texts.pro.3.32: For the perverse is an abomination to Jehovah; but his secret is with the upright.
texts.pro.3.33: The curse of Jehovah is in the house of the wicked; but he blesseth the habitation of the righteous.
texts.pro.3.34: He indeed scorneth the scorners; but he giveth grace unto the lowly.
texts.pro.3.35: The wise shall inherit glory; but shame shall be the promotion of the foolish.
texts.pro.4.1: Hear, ye children, the instruction of a father, and attend to know intelligence;
texts.pro.4.2: for I give you good doctrine: forsake ye not my law.
texts.pro.4.3: For I was a son unto my father, tender and an only one in the sight of my mother.
texts.pro.4.4: And he taught me, and said unto me, Let thy heart retain my words; keep my commandments and live.
texts.pro.4.5: Get wisdom, get intelligence: forget [it] not; neither decline from the words of my mouth.
texts.pro.4.6: Forsake her not, and she shall keep thee; love her, and she shall preserve thee.
texts.pro.4.7: The beginning of wisdom [is], Get wisdom; and with all thy getting get intelligence.
texts.pro.4.8: Exalt her, and she shall promote thee; she shall bring thee to honour when thou dost embrace her.
texts.pro.4.9: She shall give to thy head a garland of grace; a crown of glory will she bestow upon thee.
texts.pro.4.10: Hear, my son, and receive my sayings, and the years of thy life shall be multiplied.
texts.pro.4.11: I will teach thee in the way of wisdom, I will lead thee in paths of uprightness.
texts.pro.4.12: When thou goest, thy steps shall not be straitened; and when thou runnest, thou shalt not stumble.
texts.pro.4.13: Take fast hold of instruction, let [her] not go: keep her, for she is thy life.
texts.pro.4.14: Enter not into the path of the wicked, and go not in the way of evil [men]:
texts.pro.4.15: avoid it, pass not by it; turn from it, and pass away.
texts.pro.4.16: For they sleep not except they have done mischief, and their sleep is taken away unless they have caused [some] to fall.
texts.pro.4.17: For they eat the bread of wickedness, and drink the wine of violence.
texts.pro.4.18: But the path of the righteous is as the shining light, going on and brightening until the day be fully come.
texts.pro.4.19: The way of the wicked is as darkness: they know not at what they stumble.
texts.pro.4.20: My son, attend to my words; incline thine ear unto my sayings.
texts.pro.4.21: Let them not depart from thine eyes; keep them in the midst of thy heart.
texts.pro.4.22: For they are life unto those that find them, and health to all their flesh.
texts.pro.4.23: Keep thy heart more than anything that is guarded; for out of it are the issues of life.
texts.pro.4.24: Put away from thee perverseness of mouth, and corrupt lips put far from thee.
texts.pro.4.25: Let thine eyes look right on, and let thine eyelids look straight before thee.
texts.pro.4.26: Ponder the path of thy feet, and let all thy ways be well-ordered.
texts.pro.4.27: Turn not to the right hand nor to the left; remove thy foot from evil.
texts.pro.5.1: My son, attend unto my wisdom, incline thine ear to my understanding;
texts.pro.5.2: that thou mayest keep reflection, and that thy lips may preserve knowledge.
texts.pro.5.3: For the lips of the strange woman drop honey, and her mouth is smoother than oil;
texts.pro.5.4: but her end is bitter as wormwood, sharp as a two-edged sword.
texts.pro.5.5: Her feet go down to death; her steps take hold on Sheol.
texts.pro.5.6: Lest she should ponder the path of life, her ways wander, she knoweth not [whither].
texts.pro.5.7: And now, children, hearken unto me, and depart not from the words of my mouth.
texts.pro.5.8: Remove thy way far from her, and come not nigh the door of her house:
texts.pro.5.9: lest thou give thine honour unto others, and thy years unto the cruel;
texts.pro.5.10: lest strangers be filled with thy wealth, and the fruits of thy toil [come] into the house of a stranger;
texts.pro.5.11: and thou mourn in thine end, when thy flesh and thy body are consumed;
texts.pro.5.12: and thou say, How have I hated instruction, and my heart despised reproof!
texts.pro.5.13: and I have not hearkened unto the voice of my teachers, nor inclined mine ear to those that instructed me;
texts.pro.5.14: I was well nigh in all evil in the midst of the congregation and assembly.
texts.pro.5.15: Drink waters out of thine own cistern, and running waters out of thine own well.
texts.pro.5.16: Thy fountains shall be poured forth, as water-brooks in the broadways.
texts.pro.5.17: Let them be only thine own, and not strangers' with thee.
texts.pro.5.18: Let thy fountain be blessed; and have joy of the wife of thy youth.
texts.pro.5.19: As a lovely hind and a graceful roe, let her breasts satisfy thee at all times: be thou ravished continually with her love.
texts.pro.5.20: And why shouldest thou, my son, be ravished with a strange woman, and embrace the bosom of a stranger?
texts.pro.5.21: For the ways of man are before the eyes of Jehovah, and he pondereth all his paths.
texts.pro.5.22: His own iniquities shall take the wicked, and he shall be holden with the cords of his sin.
texts.pro.5.23: He shall die for want of discipline; and in the greatness of his folly he shall go astray.
texts.pro.6.1: My son, if thou hast become surety for thy friend, if thou hast stricken thy hand for a stranger,
texts.pro.6.2: thou art snared with the words of thy mouth, thou art taken with the words of thy mouth.
texts.pro.6.3: Do this now, my son, and deliver thyself, since thou hast come into the hand of thy friend: go, humble thyself, and be urgent with thy friend.
texts.pro.6.4: Give not sleep to thine eyes, nor slumber to thine eyelids:
texts.pro.6.5: deliver thyself as a gazelle from the hand [of the hunter], and as a bird from the hand of the fowler.
texts.pro.6.6: Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways and be wise:
texts.pro.6.7: which having no chief, overseer, or ruler,
texts.pro.6.8: provideth her bread in the summer, [and] gathereth her food in the harvest.
texts.pro.6.9: How long, sluggard, wilt thou lie down? When wilt thou arise out of thy sleep?
texts.pro.6.10: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest!
texts.pro.6.11: So shall thy poverty come as a roving plunderer, and thy penury as an armed man.
texts.pro.6.12: A man of Belial, a wicked person, is he that goeth about with a perverse mouth;
texts.pro.6.13: he winketh with his eyes, he speaketh with his feet, he teacheth with his fingers;
texts.pro.6.14: deceits are in his heart; he deviseth mischief at all times, he soweth discords.
texts.pro.6.15: Therefore shall his calamity come suddenly: in a moment shall he be broken, and without remedy.
texts.pro.6.16: These six [things] doth Jehovah hate, yea, seven are an abomination unto him:
texts.pro.6.17: haughty eyes, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood;
texts.pro.6.18: a heart that deviseth wicked imaginations; feet that are swift in running to mischief;
texts.pro.6.19: a false witness that uttereth lies, and he that soweth discords among brethren.
texts.pro.6.20: My son, observe thy father's commandment, and forsake not the teaching of thy mother;
texts.pro.6.21: bind them continually upon thy heart, tie them about thy neck:
texts.pro.6.22: when thou walkest, it shall lead thee; when thou sleepest, it shall keep thee; and [when] thou awakest, it shall talk with thee.
texts.pro.6.23: For the commandment is a lamp, and the teaching a light, and reproofs of instruction are the way of life:
texts.pro.6.24: to keep thee from the evil woman, from the flattery of the tongue of a strange woman.
texts.pro.6.25: Lust not after her beauty in thy heart, neither let her take thee with her eyelids;
texts.pro.6.26: for by means of a whorish woman [a man is brought] to a loaf of bread, and another's wife doth hunt for the precious soul.
texts.pro.6.27: Can a man take fire in his bosom, and his garments not be burned?
texts.pro.6.28: Can one go upon hot coals, and his feet not be scorched?
texts.pro.6.29: So he that goeth in to his neighbour's wife: whosoever toucheth her shall not be innocent.
texts.pro.6.30: They do not despise a thief, if he steal to satisfy his soul when he is hungry:
texts.pro.6.31: and if he be found, he shall restore sevenfold; he shall give all the substance of his house.
texts.pro.6.32: Whoso committeth adultery with a woman is void of understanding: he that doeth it destroyeth his own soul.
texts.pro.6.33: A wound and contempt shall he get; and his reproach shall not be wiped away.
texts.pro.6.34: For jealousy is the rage of a man, and he will not spare in the day of vengeance;
texts.pro.6.35: he will not regard any ransom, neither will he rest content though thou multipliest [thy] gifts.
texts.pro.7.1: My son, keep my words, and lay up my commandments with thee.
texts.pro.7.2: Keep my commandments, and live; and my teaching, as the apple of thine eye.
texts.pro.7.3: Bind them upon thy fingers, write them upon the tablet of thy heart.
texts.pro.7.4: Say unto wisdom, Thou art my sister, and call intelligence [thy] kinswoman:
texts.pro.7.5: that they may keep thee from the strange woman, from the stranger who flattereth with her words.
texts.pro.7.6: For at the window of my house, I looked forth through my lattice,
texts.pro.7.7: and I beheld among the simple ones, I discerned among the sons, a young man void of understanding,
texts.pro.7.8: passing through the street near her corner; and he went the way to her house,
texts.pro.7.9: in the twilight, in the evening of the day, in the blackness of night and the darkness.
texts.pro.7.10: And behold, there met him a woman in the attire of a harlot, and subtle of heart.
texts.pro.7.11: She is clamorous and unmanageable; her feet abide not in her house:
texts.pro.7.12: now without, now in the broadways, -- and she lieth in wait at every corner.
texts.pro.7.13: And she caught him and kissed him, and with an impudent face said unto him,
texts.pro.7.14: I have peace-offerings with me; this day have I paid my vows:
texts.pro.7.15: therefore came I forth to meet thee, to seek earnestly thy face, and I have found thee.
texts.pro.7.16: I have decked my bed with tapestry coverlets of variegated linen from Egypt;
texts.pro.7.17: I have perfumed my couch with myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon.
texts.pro.7.18: Come, let us revel in love until the morning, let us delight ourselves with loves.
texts.pro.7.19: For the husband is not at home, he is gone a long journey;
texts.pro.7.20: he hath taken the money-bag with him, he will come home on the day of the full moon.
texts.pro.7.21: With her much enticement she beguiled him; with the smoothness of her lips she constrained him.
texts.pro.7.22: He went after her straightway, as an ox goeth to the slaughter, and as stocks [serve] for the correction of the fool;
texts.pro.7.23: till an arrow strike through his liver: as a bird hasteth to the snare, and knoweth not that it is for its life.
texts.pro.7.24: And now, ye sons, hearken unto me, and attend to the words of my mouth.
texts.pro.7.25: Let not thy heart decline to her ways, go not astray in her paths:
texts.pro.7.26: for she hath cast down many wounded, and all slain by her were strong.
texts.pro.7.27: Her house is the way to Sheol, going down to the chambers of death.
texts.pro.8.1: Doth not wisdom cry? and understanding give forth her voice?
texts.pro.8.2: On the top of high places by the way, at the cross-paths she taketh her stand.
texts.pro.8.3: Beside the gates, at the entry of the city, at the coming in at the doors, she crieth aloud.
texts.pro.8.4: Unto you, men, I call, and my voice is to the sons of man:
texts.pro.8.5: O ye simple, understand prudence; and ye foolish, understand sense.
texts.pro.8.6: Hear, for I will speak excellent things, and the opening of my lips shall be right things.
texts.pro.8.7: For my palate shall meditate truth, and wickedness is an abomination to my lips.
texts.pro.8.8: All the words of my mouth are in righteousness; there is nothing tortuous or perverse in them.
texts.pro.8.9: They are all plain to him that understandeth, and right to them that find knowledge.
texts.pro.8.10: Receive my instruction, and not silver; and knowledge rather than choice gold:
texts.pro.8.11: for wisdom is better than rubies, and all the things that may be desired are not equal to it.
texts.pro.8.12: I wisdom dwell [with] prudence, and find the knowledge [which cometh] of reflection.
texts.pro.8.13: The fear of Jehovah is to hate evil; pride, and arrogancy, and the evil way, and the froward mouth do I hate.
texts.pro.8.14: Counsel is mine, and sound wisdom: I am intelligence; I have strength.
texts.pro.8.15: By me kings reign, and rulers make just decrees;
texts.pro.8.16: by me princes rule, and nobles, all the judges of the earth.
texts.pro.8.17: I love those that love me; and they that seek me early shall find me.
texts.pro.8.18: Riches and honour are with me; durable wealth and righteousness.
texts.pro.8.19: My fruit is better than fine gold, yea, than pure gold; and my revenue than choice silver.
texts.pro.8.20: I walk in the path of righteousness, in the midst of the paths of judgment:
texts.pro.8.21: that I may cause those that love me to inherit substance; and I will fill their treasuries.
texts.pro.8.22: Jehovah possessed me in the beginning of his way, before his works of old.
texts.pro.8.23: I was set up from eternity, from the beginning, before the earth was.
texts.pro.8.24: When there were no depths, I was brought forth, when there were no fountains abounding with water.
texts.pro.8.25: Before the mountains were settled, before the hills was I brought forth;
texts.pro.8.26: while as yet he had not made the earth, nor the fields, nor the beginning of the dust of the world.
texts.pro.8.27: When he prepared the heavens I was there; when he ordained the circle upon the face of the deep;
texts.pro.8.28: when he established the skies above, when the fountains of the deep became strong;
texts.pro.8.29: when he imposed on the sea his decree that the waters should not pass his commandment, when he appointed the foundations of the earth:
texts.pro.8.30: then I was by him [his] nursling, and I was daily his delight, rejoicing always before him;
texts.pro.8.31: rejoicing in the habitable part of his earth, and my delights [were] with the sons of men.
texts.pro.8.32: And now, sons, hearken unto me, and blessed are they that keep my ways:
texts.pro.8.33: hear instruction and be wise, and refuse it not.
texts.pro.8.34: Blessed is the man that heareth me, watching daily at my gates, waiting at the posts of my doors.
texts.pro.8.35: For whoso findeth me findeth life, and obtaineth favour of Jehovah;
texts.pro.8.36: but he that sinneth against me doeth violence to his own soul: all they that hate me love death.
texts.pro.9.1: Wisdom hath built her house, she hath hewn out her seven pillars;
texts.pro.9.2: she hath slaughtered her cattle, she hath mingled her wine, she hath also prepared her table;
texts.pro.9.3: she hath sent forth her maidens: she crieth upon the summits of the high places of the city,
texts.pro.9.4: Whoso is simple, let him turn in hither. To him that is void of understanding, she saith,
texts.pro.9.5: Come, eat ye of my bread, and drink of the wine that I have mingled.
texts.pro.9.6: Forsake follies and live, and go in the way of intelligence.
texts.pro.9.7: He that instructeth a scorner getteth to himself shame; and he that reproveth a wicked [man] [getteth] to himself a blot.
texts.pro.9.8: Reprove not a scorner, lest he hate thee; reprove a wise [man], and he will love thee.
texts.pro.9.9: Impart to a wise [man], and he will become yet wiser; teach a righteous [man], and he will increase learning.
texts.pro.9.10: The fear of Jehovah is the beginning of wisdom; and the knowledge of the Holy is intelligence.
texts.pro.9.11: For by me thy days shall be multiplied, and years of life shall be added to thee.
texts.pro.9.12: If thou art wise, thou shalt be wise for thyself; and if thou scornest, thou alone shalt bear it.
texts.pro.9.13: The foolish woman is clamorous; she is stupid, and knoweth nothing.
texts.pro.9.14: And she sitteth at the entry of her house, on a seat in the high places of the city,
texts.pro.9.15: to call passers-by who go right on their ways:
texts.pro.9.16: Whoso is simple, let him turn in hither. And to him that is void of understanding she saith,
texts.pro.9.17: Stolen waters are sweet, and the bread of secrecy is pleasant.
texts.pro.9.18: But he knoweth not that the dead are there; [that] her guests are in the depths of Sheol.
texts.pro.10.1: The Proverbs of Solomon. A wise son maketh a glad father; but a foolish son is the grief of his mother.
texts.pro.10.2: Treasures of wickedness profit nothing; but righteousness delivereth from death.
texts.pro.10.3: Jehovah suffereth not the soul of the righteous [man] to famish; but he repelleth the craving of the wicked.
texts.pro.10.4: He cometh to want that dealeth with a slack hand; but the hand of the diligent maketh rich.
texts.pro.10.5: He that gathereth in summer is a wise son; he that sleepeth in harvest is a son that causeth shame.
texts.pro.10.6: Blessings are upon the head of a righteous [man]; but the mouth of the wicked covereth violence.
texts.pro.10.7: The memory of the righteous [man] shall be blessed; but the name of the wicked shall rot.
texts.pro.10.8: The wise in heart receiveth commandments; but a prating fool shall fall.
texts.pro.10.9: He that walketh in integrity walketh securely; but he that perverteth his ways shall be known.
texts.pro.10.10: He that winketh with the eye causeth grief, and a prating fool shall fall.
texts.pro.10.11: The mouth of a righteous [man] is a fountain of life; but the mouth of the wicked covereth violence.
texts.pro.10.12: Hatred stirreth up strifes; but love covereth all transgressions.
texts.pro.10.13: In the lips of an intelligent [man] wisdom is found; but a rod is for the back of him that is void of understanding.
texts.pro.10.14: The wise lay up knowledge; but the mouth of the fool is near destruction.
texts.pro.10.15: The rich man's wealth is his strong city; the destruction of the poor is their poverty.
texts.pro.10.16: The labour of a righteous [man] [tendeth] to life; the revenue of a wicked [man], to sin.
texts.pro.10.17: Keeping instruction is the path to life; but he that forsaketh reproof goeth astray.
texts.pro.10.18: He that covereth hatred hath lying lips, and he that sendeth forth a slander is a fool.
texts.pro.10.19: In the multitude of words there wanteth not transgression; but he that restraineth his lips doeth wisely.
texts.pro.10.20: The tongue of the righteous [man] is [as] choice silver; the heart of the wicked is little worth.
texts.pro.10.21: The lips of a righteous [man] feed many; but fools die for want of understanding.
texts.pro.10.22: The blessing of Jehovah, it maketh rich, and he addeth no sorrow to it.
texts.pro.10.23: It is as sport to a foolish [man] to do wickedness; but a man of understanding hath wisdom.
texts.pro.10.24: The fear of a wicked [man], it shall come upon him; but the desire of the righteous shall be granted.
texts.pro.10.25: As a whirlwind passeth, so is the wicked no [more]; but the righteous is an everlasting foundation.
texts.pro.10.26: As vinegar to the teeth, and as smoke to the eyes, so is the sluggard to them that send him.
texts.pro.10.27: The fear of Jehovah prolongeth days; but the years of the wicked shall be shortened.
texts.pro.10.28: The hope of the righteous is joy; but the expectation of the wicked shall perish.
texts.pro.10.29: The way of Jehovah is strength to the perfect [man], but destruction to the workers of iniquity.
texts.pro.10.30: The righteous [man] shall never be moved; but the wicked shall not inhabit the land.
texts.pro.10.31: The mouth of a righteous [man] putteth forth wisdom; but the froward tongue shall be cut out.
texts.pro.10.32: The lips of a righteous [man] know what is acceptable; but the mouth of the wicked is frowardness.
texts.pro.11.1: A false balance is an abomination to Jehovah; but a just weight is his delight.
texts.pro.11.2: [When] pride cometh, then cometh shame; but with the lowly is wisdom.
texts.pro.11.3: The integrity of the upright guideth them; but the crookedness of the unfaithful destroyeth them.
texts.pro.11.4: Wealth profiteth not in the day of wrath; but righteousness delivereth from death.
texts.pro.11.5: The righteousness of the perfect maketh plain his way; but the wicked falleth by his own wickedness.
texts.pro.11.6: The righteousness of the upright delivereth them; but the treacherous are taken in their own craving.
texts.pro.11.7: When a wicked man dieth, [his] expectation shall perish; and the hope of evil [men] perisheth.
texts.pro.11.8: The righteous is delivered out of trouble, and the wicked cometh in his stead.
texts.pro.11.9: With his mouth a hypocrite destroyeth his neighbour; but through knowledge are the righteous delivered.
texts.pro.11.10: When it goeth well with the righteous, the city rejoiceth; and when the wicked perish, there is shouting.
texts.pro.11.11: By the blessing of the upright the city is exalted; but it is overthrown by the mouth of the wicked.
texts.pro.11.12: He that despiseth his neighbour is void of heart; but a man of understanding holdeth his peace.
texts.pro.11.13: He that goeth about talebearing revealeth secrets; but he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth the matter.
texts.pro.11.14: Where no advice is, the people fall; but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.
texts.pro.11.15: It goeth ill with him that is surety for another; but he that hateth suretyship is secure.
texts.pro.11.16: A gracious woman retaineth honour; and the violent retain riches.
texts.pro.11.17: The merciful man doeth good to his own soul; but the cruel troubleth his own flesh.
texts.pro.11.18: The wicked worketh a deceitful work; but he that soweth righteousness hath a sure reward.
texts.pro.11.19: As righteousness [tendeth] to life, so he that pursueth evil [doeth it] to his own death.
texts.pro.11.20: The perverse in heart are abomination to Jehovah; but they that are perfect in [their] way are his delight.
texts.pro.11.21: Hand for hand! an evil [man] shall not be held innocent; but the seed of the righteous shall be delivered.
texts.pro.11.22: A fair woman who is without discretion, is [as] a gold ring in a swine's snout.
texts.pro.11.23: The desire of the righteous is only good; the expectation of the wicked is wrath.
texts.pro.11.24: There is that scattereth, and yet increaseth; and there is that withholdeth more than is right, but [it tendeth] only to want.
texts.pro.11.25: The liberal soul shall be made fat, and he that watereth shall be watered also himself.
texts.pro.11.26: He that withholdeth corn, the people curse him; but blessing shall be upon the head of him that selleth it.
texts.pro.11.27: He that is earnest after good seeketh favour; but he that searcheth for mischief, it shall come upon him.
texts.pro.11.28: He that trusteth in his riches shall fall; but the righteous shall flourish as a leaf.
texts.pro.11.29: He that troubleth his own house shall inherit wind; and the fool shall be servant to the wise of heart.
texts.pro.11.30: The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life; and the wise winneth souls.
texts.pro.11.31: Behold, the righteous shall be requited on the earth: how much more the wicked and the sinner.
texts.pro.12.1: Whoso loveth discipline loveth knowledge, but he that hateth reproof is brutish.
texts.pro.12.2: A good [man] obtaineth favour of Jehovah; but a man of mischievous devices will he condemn.
texts.pro.12.3: A man shall not be established by wickedness; but the root of the righteous shall not be moved.
texts.pro.12.4: A woman of worth is a crown to her husband; but she that maketh ashamed is as rottenness in his bones.
texts.pro.12.5: The thoughts of the righteous are right; the counsels of the wicked are deceit.
texts.pro.12.6: The words of the wicked are a lying-in-wait for blood; but the mouth of the upright shall deliver them.
texts.pro.12.7: Overthrow the wicked, and they are no [more]; but the house of the righteous shall stand.
texts.pro.12.8: A man is commended according to his wisdom; but he that is of a perverted heart shall be despised.
texts.pro.12.9: Better is he that is lightly esteemed, and hath a servant, than he that honoureth himself, and lacketh bread.
texts.pro.12.10: A righteous man is concerned for the life of his beast; but the tender mercies of the wicked are cruel.
texts.pro.12.11: He that tilleth his land shall be satisfied with bread; but he that followeth the worthless is void of understanding.
texts.pro.12.12: The wicked desireth the net of evil [men]; but the root of the righteous yieldeth [fruit].
texts.pro.12.13: In the transgression of the lips is an evil snare; but a righteous [man] shall go forth out of trouble.
texts.pro.12.14: A man is satisfied with good by the fruit of his mouth; and the recompense of a man's hands shall be rendered unto him.
texts.pro.12.15: The way of a fool is right in his own eyes; but he that is wise hearkeneth unto counsel.
texts.pro.12.16: The vexation of the fool is presently known; but a prudent [man] covereth shame.
texts.pro.12.17: He that uttereth truth sheweth forth righteousness; but a false witness deceit.
texts.pro.12.18: There is that babbleth like the piercings of a sword; but the tongue of the wise is health.
texts.pro.12.19: The lip of truth shall be established for ever; but a lying tongue is but for a moment.
texts.pro.12.20: Deceit is in the heart of them that devise evil; but to the counsellors of peace is joy.
texts.pro.12.21: There shall no evil happen to a righteous [man]; but the wicked shall be filled with mischief.
texts.pro.12.22: Lying lips are an abomination to Jehovah; but they that deal truly are his delight.
texts.pro.12.23: A prudent man concealeth knowledge; but the heart of the foolish proclaimeth folly.
texts.pro.12.24: The hand of the diligent shall bear rule; but the slothful [hand] shall be under tribute.
texts.pro.12.25: Heaviness in the heart of man maketh it stoop; but a good word maketh it glad.
texts.pro.12.26: The righteous guideth his neighbour; but the way of the wicked misleadeth them.
texts.pro.12.27: The slothful roasteth not what he took in hunting; but man's precious substance is to the diligent.
texts.pro.12.28: In the path of righteousness is life, and in the pathway thereof there is no death.
texts.pro.13.1: A wise son [heareth] his father's instruction; but a scorner heareth not rebuke.
texts.pro.13.2: A man shall eat good by the fruit of his mouth; but the soul of the treacherous, violence.
texts.pro.13.3: He that guardeth his mouth keepeth his soul; destruction shall be to him that openeth wide his lips.
texts.pro.13.4: A sluggard's soul desireth and hath nothing; but the soul of the diligent shall be made fat.
texts.pro.13.5: A righteous [man] hateth lying; but the wicked maketh himself odious and cometh to shame.
texts.pro.13.6: Righteousness preserveth him that is perfect in the way; but wickedness overthroweth the sinner.
texts.pro.13.7: There is that feigneth himself rich, and hath nothing; there is that maketh himself poor, and hath great wealth.
texts.pro.13.8: The ransom of a man's life is his riches; but the indigent heareth not rebuke.
texts.pro.13.9: The light of the righteous rejoiceth; but the lamp of the wicked shall be put out.
texts.pro.13.10: By pride there only cometh contention; but with the well-advised is wisdom.
texts.pro.13.11: Wealth [gotten] by vanity diminisheth; but he that gathereth by manual-labour shall increase [it].
texts.pro.13.12: Hope deferred maketh the heart sick; but the desire [that] cometh to pass is a tree of life.
texts.pro.13.13: Whoso despiseth the word shall be held by it; but he that feareth the commandment shall be rewarded.
texts.pro.13.14: The teaching of the wise [man] is a fountain of life, to turn away from the snares of death.
texts.pro.13.15: Good understanding procureth favour; but the way of the treacherous is hard.
texts.pro.13.16: Every prudent [man] acteth with knowledge; but the foolish layeth open [his] folly.
texts.pro.13.17: A wicked messenger falleth into evil; but a faithful ambassador is health.
texts.pro.13.18: Poverty and shame shall be [to] him that refuseth instruction; but he that regardeth reproof shall be honoured.
texts.pro.13.19: The desire accomplished is sweet to the soul; but it is abomination to the foolish to depart from evil.
texts.pro.13.20: He that walketh with wise [men] becometh wise; but a companion of the foolish will be depraved.
texts.pro.13.21: Evil pursueth sinners; but to the righteous good shall be repaid.
texts.pro.13.22: A good man leaveth an inheritance to his children's children; but the wealth of the sinner is laid up for the righteous [man].
texts.pro.13.23: Much food is in the tillage of the poor; but there is that is lost for want of judgment.
texts.pro.13.24: He that spareth his rod hateth his son; but he that loveth him chasteneth him betimes.
texts.pro.13.25: The righteous eateth to the satisfying of his soul; but the belly of the wicked shall want.
texts.pro.14.1: The wisdom of women buildeth their house; but folly plucketh it down with her hands.
texts.pro.14.2: He that walketh in his uprightness feareth Jehovah; but he that is perverted in his ways despiseth him.
texts.pro.14.3: In the fool's mouth is a rod of pride; but the lips of the wise shall preserve them.
texts.pro.14.4: Where no oxen are, the crib is clean; but much increase is by the strength of the ox.
texts.pro.14.5: A faithful witness will not lie; but a false witness uttereth lies.
texts.pro.14.6: A scorner seeketh wisdom, and there is none [for him]; but knowledge is easy unto the intelligent.
texts.pro.14.7: Go from the presence of a foolish man, in whom thou perceivest not the lips of knowledge.
texts.pro.14.8: The wisdom of the prudent is to discern his way; but the folly of the foolish is deceit.
texts.pro.14.9: Fools make a mock at trespass; but for the upright there is favour.
texts.pro.14.10: The heart knoweth its own bitterness, and a stranger doth not intermeddle with its joy.
texts.pro.14.11: The house of the wicked shall be overthrown; but the tent of the upright shall flourish.
texts.pro.14.12: There is a way that seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof is the ways of death.
texts.pro.14.13: Even in laughter the heart is sorrowful, and the end of mirth is sadness.
texts.pro.14.14: The backslider in heart shall be filled with his own ways, and the good man from what is in himself.
texts.pro.14.15: The simple believeth every word; but the prudent [man] heedeth his going.
texts.pro.14.16: A wise [man] feareth and departeth from evil; but the foolish is overbearing and confident.
texts.pro.14.17: He that is soon angry dealeth foolishly, and a man of mischievous devices is hated.
texts.pro.14.18: The simple inherit folly; but the prudent are crowned with knowledge.
texts.pro.14.19: The evil bow before the good, and the wicked at the gates of the righteous [man].
texts.pro.14.20: He that is poor is hated even of his own neighbour; but the rich hath many friends.
texts.pro.14.21: He that despiseth his neighbour sinneth; but he that is gracious to the afflicted, happy is he.
texts.pro.14.22: Do they not err that devise evil? but loving-kindness and truth are for those that devise good.
texts.pro.14.23: In all labour there is profit; but the talk of the lips [tendeth] only to want.
texts.pro.14.24: The crown of the wise is their riches; the folly of the foolish is folly.
texts.pro.14.25: A true witness delivereth souls; but deceit uttereth lies.
texts.pro.14.26: In the fear of Jehovah is strong confidence, and his children shall have a place of refuge.
texts.pro.14.27: The fear of Jehovah is a fountain of life, to turn away from the snares of death.
texts.pro.14.28: In the multitude of people is the king's glory; but in the lack of people is the ruin of a prince.
texts.pro.14.29: He that is slow to anger is of great understanding; but he that is hasty of spirit exalteth folly.
texts.pro.14.30: A sound heart is the life of the flesh; but envy the rottenness of the bones.
texts.pro.14.31: He that oppresseth the poor reproacheth his Maker; but he that honoureth Him is gracious to the needy.
texts.pro.14.32: The wicked is driven away by his evil-doing; but the righteous trusteth, [even] in his death.
texts.pro.14.33: Wisdom resteth in the heart of the intelligent [man]; but that which is in the foolish maketh itself known.
texts.pro.14.34: Righteousness exalteth a nation; but sin is a reproach to peoples.
texts.pro.14.35: The king's favour is toward a wise servant; but his wrath is [against] him that causeth shame.
texts.pro.15.1: A soft answer turneth away fury; but a grievous word stirreth up anger.
texts.pro.15.2: The tongue of the wise useth knowledge aright; but the mouth of the foolish poureth out folly.
texts.pro.15.3: The eyes of Jehovah are in every place, beholding the evil and the good.
texts.pro.15.4: Gentleness of tongue is a tree of life; but crookedness therein is a breaking of the spirit.
texts.pro.15.5: A fool despiseth his father's instruction; but he that regardeth reproof becometh prudent.
texts.pro.15.6: In the house of a righteous [man] is much treasure; but in the revenue of a wicked [man] is disturbance.
texts.pro.15.7: The lips of the wise disperse knowledge, but not so the heart of the foolish.
texts.pro.15.8: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination to Jehovah; but the prayer of the upright is his delight.
texts.pro.15.9: The way of a wicked [man] is an abomination to Jehovah; but him that pursueth righteousness he loveth.
texts.pro.15.10: Grievous correction is for him that forsaketh the path; he that hateth reproof shall die.
texts.pro.15.11: Sheol and destruction are before Jehovah; how much more then the hearts of the children of men!
texts.pro.15.12: A scorner loveth not one that reproveth him; he will not go unto the wise.
texts.pro.15.13: A joyful heart maketh a cheerful countenance; but by sorrow of heart the spirit is broken.
texts.pro.15.14: The heart of an intelligent [man] seeketh knowledge; but the mouth of the foolish feedeth on folly.
texts.pro.15.15: All the days of the afflicted are evil; but a cheerful heart is a continual feast.
texts.pro.15.16: Better is little with the fear of Jehovah than great store and disquietude therewith.
texts.pro.15.17: Better is a meal of herbs where love is, than a fatted ox and hatred therewith.
texts.pro.15.18: A furious man stirreth up contention; but he that is slow to anger appeaseth strife.
texts.pro.15.19: The way of the sluggard is as a hedge of thorns; but the path of the upright is made plain.
texts.pro.15.20: A wise son maketh a glad father; but a foolish man despiseth his mother.
texts.pro.15.21: Folly is joy to him that is void of sense; but a man of understanding regulateth his walk.
texts.pro.15.22: Without counsel purposes are disappointed; but in the multitude of counsellors they are established.
texts.pro.15.23: A man hath joy by the answer of his mouth; and a word in its season, how good is it!
texts.pro.15.24: The path of life is upwards for the wise, that he may depart from Sheol beneath.
texts.pro.15.25: Jehovah plucketh up the house of the proud; but he establisheth the boundary of the widow.
texts.pro.15.26: The thoughts of the evil [man] are an abomination to Jehovah; but pure words are pleasant.
texts.pro.15.27: He that is greedy of gain troubleth his own house; but he that hateth gifts shall live.
texts.pro.15.28: The heart of a righteous [man] studieth to answer; but the mouth of the wicked poureth out evil things.
texts.pro.15.29: Jehovah is far from the wicked; but he heareth the prayer of the righteous.
texts.pro.15.30: That which enlighteneth the eyes rejoiceth the heart; good tidings make the bones fat.
texts.pro.15.31: The ear that heareth the reproof of life shall abide among the wise.
texts.pro.15.32: He that refuseth instruction despiseth his own soul; but he that heareth reproof getteth sense.
texts.pro.15.33: The fear of Jehovah is the discipline of wisdom, and before honour [goeth] humility.
texts.pro.16.1: The purposes of the heart are of man, but the answer of the tongue is from Jehovah.
texts.pro.16.2: All the ways of a man are clean in his own eyes; but Jehovah weigheth the spirits.
texts.pro.16.3: Commit thy works unto Jehovah, and thy thoughts shall be established.
texts.pro.16.4: Jehovah hath wrought everything on his own account, yea, even the wicked for the day of evil.
texts.pro.16.5: Every proud heart is an abomination to Jehovah: hand for hand, he shall not be held innocent.
texts.pro.16.6: By loving-kindness and truth iniquity is atoned for; and by the fear of Jehovah [men] depart from evil.
texts.pro.16.7: When a man's ways please Jehovah, he maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him.
texts.pro.16.8: Better is a little with righteousness, than great revenues without right.
texts.pro.16.9: The heart of man deviseth his way, but Jehovah directeth his steps.
texts.pro.16.10: An oracle is on the lips of the king: his mouth will not err in judgment.
texts.pro.16.11: The just balance and scales are Jehovah's; all the weights of the bag are his work.
texts.pro.16.12: It is an abomination to kings to commit wickedness; for the throne is established by righteousness.
texts.pro.16.13: Righteous lips are the delight of kings, and they love him that speaketh aright.
texts.pro.16.14: The fury of a king is [as] messengers of death; but a wise man will pacify it.
texts.pro.16.15: In the light of the king's countenance is life, and his favour is as a cloud of the latter rain.
texts.pro.16.16: How much better is it to get wisdom than fine gold, and the getting of intelligence to be preferred to silver!
texts.pro.16.17: The highway of the upright is to depart from evil: he that taketh heed to his way keepeth his soul.
texts.pro.16.18: Pride [goeth] before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.
texts.pro.16.19: Better is it to be of a humble spirit with the meek, than to divide the spoil with the proud.
texts.pro.16.20: He that giveth heed to the word shall find good; and whoso confideth in Jehovah, happy is he.
texts.pro.16.21: The wise in heart is called intelligent, and the sweetness of the lips increaseth learning.
texts.pro.16.22: Wisdom is a fountain of life for him that hath it; but the instruction of fools is folly.
texts.pro.16.23: The heart of the wise maketh his mouth intelligent, and upon his lips increaseth learning.
texts.pro.16.24: Pleasant words are [as] a honeycomb, sweet to the soul, and health for the bones.
texts.pro.16.25: There is a way that seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof is the ways of death.
texts.pro.16.26: The appetite of the labourer laboureth for him, for his mouth urgeth him on.
texts.pro.16.27: A man of Belial diggeth up evil, and on his lips there is as a scorching fire.
texts.pro.16.28: A false man soweth contention; and a talebearer separateth very friends.
texts.pro.16.29: A violent man enticeth his neighbour, and leadeth him into a way that is not good.
texts.pro.16.30: He that shutteth his eyes, [it is] to devise froward things; biting his lips, he bringeth evil to pass.
texts.pro.16.31: The hoary head is a crown of glory, [if] it is found in the way of righteousness.
texts.pro.16.32: He that is slow to anger is better than the mighty, and he that ruleth his spirit than he that taketh a city.
texts.pro.16.33: The lot is cast into the lap; but the whole decision is of Jehovah.
texts.pro.17.1: Better is a dry morsel, and quietness therewith, than a house full of feasting [with] strife.
texts.pro.17.2: A wise servant shall rule over a son that causeth shame, and shall have part in the inheritance among the brethren.
texts.pro.17.3: The fining-pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold; but Jehovah trieth the hearts.
texts.pro.17.4: The evil-doer giveth heed to iniquitous lips; the liar giveth ear to a mischievous tongue.
texts.pro.17.5: Whoso mocketh a poor [man] reproacheth his Maker; he that is glad at calamity shall not be held innocent.
texts.pro.17.6: Children's children are the crown of old men; and the glory of children are their fathers.
texts.pro.17.7: Excellent speech becometh not a vile [man]; how much less do lying lips a noble!
texts.pro.17.8: A gift is a precious stone in the eyes of the possessor: whithersoever it turneth it prospereth.
texts.pro.17.9: He that covereth transgression seeketh love; but he that bringeth a matter up again separateth very friends.
texts.pro.17.10: A reproof entereth more deeply into him that hath understanding than a hundred stripes into a fool.
texts.pro.17.11: An evil [man] seeketh only rebellion; but a cruel messenger shall be sent against him.
texts.pro.17.12: Let a bear robbed of her whelps meet a man rather than a fool in his folly.
texts.pro.17.13: Whoso rewardeth evil for good, evil shall not depart from his house.
texts.pro.17.14: The beginning of contention is [as] when one letteth out water; therefore leave off strife before it become vehement.
texts.pro.17.15: He that justifieth the wicked, and he that condemneth the righteous, even they both are abomination to Jehovah.
texts.pro.17.16: To what purpose is there a price in the hand of a fool to get wisdom, seeing [he] hath no sense?
texts.pro.17.17: The friend loveth at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.
texts.pro.17.18: A senseless man striketh hands, becoming surety for his neighbour.
texts.pro.17.19: He loveth transgression that loveth a quarrel; he that maketh high his gate seeketh destruction.
texts.pro.17.20: He that hath a perverse heart findeth no good; and he that shifteth about with his tongue falleth into evil.
texts.pro.17.21: He that begetteth a fool [doeth it] to his sorrow, and the father of a vile [man] hath no joy.
texts.pro.17.22: A joyful heart promoteth healing; but a broken spirit drieth up the bones.
texts.pro.17.23: A wicked [man] taketh a gift out of the bosom, to pervert the paths of judgment.
texts.pro.17.24: Wisdom is before him that hath understanding; but the eyes of a fool are in the ends of the earth.
texts.pro.17.25: A foolish son is a grief to his father, and bitterness to her that bore him.
texts.pro.17.26: To punish a righteous [man] is not good, nor to strike nobles because of [their] uprightness.
texts.pro.17.27: He that hath knowledge spareth his words; and a man of understanding is of a cool spirit.
texts.pro.17.28: Even a fool when he holdeth his peace is reckoned wise, [and] he that shutteth his lips, intelligent.
texts.pro.18.1: He that separateth himself seeketh [his] pleasure, he is vehement against all sound wisdom.
texts.pro.18.2: A fool hath no delight in understanding, but only that his heart may reveal itself.
texts.pro.18.3: When the wicked cometh, there cometh also contempt, and with ignominy reproach.
texts.pro.18.4: The words of a man's mouth are deep waters, [and] the fountain of wisdom is a gushing brook.
texts.pro.18.5: It is not good to accept the person of the wicked, to wrong the righteous in judgment.
texts.pro.18.6: A fool's lips enter into contention, and his mouth calleth for stripes.
texts.pro.18.7: A fool's mouth is destruction to him, and his lips are a snare to his soul.
texts.pro.18.8: The words of a talebearer are as dainty morsels, and they go down into the innermost parts of the belly.
texts.pro.18.9: He also who is indolent in his work is brother of the destroyer.
texts.pro.18.10: The name of Jehovah is a strong tower: the righteous runneth into it, and is safe.
texts.pro.18.11: The rich man's wealth is his strong city, and as a high wall in his own imagination.
texts.pro.18.12: Before destruction the heart of man is haughty; and before honour [goeth] humility.
texts.pro.18.13: He that giveth answer before he heareth, it is folly and shame unto him.
texts.pro.18.14: The spirit of a man sustaineth his infirmity; but a broken spirit who can bear?
texts.pro.18.15: The heart of an intelligent [man] getteth knowledge, and the ear of the wise seeketh knowledge.
texts.pro.18.16: A man's gift maketh room for him, and bringeth him before great men.
texts.pro.18.17: He that is first in his own cause [seemeth] just; but his neighbour cometh and searcheth him.
texts.pro.18.18: The lot causeth contentions to cease, and parteth between the mighty.
texts.pro.18.19: A brother offended is [harder to be won] than a strong city; and contentions are as the bars of a palace.
texts.pro.18.20: A man's belly is satisfied with the fruit of his mouth; with the increase of his lips is he satisfied.
texts.pro.18.21: Death and life are in the power of the tongue, and they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof.
texts.pro.18.22: Whoso hath found a wife hath found a good thing, and hath obtained favour from Jehovah.
texts.pro.18.23: He that is poor speaketh with supplications, but the rich answereth roughly.
texts.pro.18.24: A man of [many] friends will come to ruin but there is a friend [that] sticketh closer than a brother.
texts.pro.19.1: Better is a poor [man] that walketh in his integrity, than he that is perverse in his lips, and is a fool.
texts.pro.19.2: Also that a person be without knowledge is not good; and he that hasteth with his feet maketh false steps.
texts.pro.19.3: The folly of man distorteth his way, and his heart is irritated against Jehovah.
texts.pro.19.4: Wealth addeth many friends; but the poor is separated from his friend.
texts.pro.19.5: A false witness shall not be held innocent, and he that uttereth lies shall not escape.
texts.pro.19.6: Many court the favour of a noble; and every one is friend to a man that giveth.
texts.pro.19.7: All the brethren of a poor [man] hate him; how much more do his friends go far from him: he pursueth [them] with words, -- they are not [to be found].
texts.pro.19.8: He that getteth sense loveth his own soul; he that keepeth understanding shall find good.
texts.pro.19.9: A false witness shall not be held innocent, and he that uttereth lies shall perish.
texts.pro.19.10: Good living beseemeth not a fool; how much less for a servant to have rule over princes.
texts.pro.19.11: The discretion of a man maketh him slow to anger, and it is his glory to pass over a transgression.
texts.pro.19.12: The king's displeasure is as the roaring of a lion; but his favour is as dew upon the grass.
texts.pro.19.13: A foolish son is the calamity of his father; and the contentions of a wife are a continual dropping.
texts.pro.19.14: House and wealth are an inheritance from fathers; but a prudent wife is from Jehovah.
texts.pro.19.15: Slothfulness casteth into a deep sleep, and the idle soul shall suffer hunger.
texts.pro.19.16: He that keepeth the commandment keepeth his soul; he that is careless of his ways shall die.
texts.pro.19.17: He that is gracious to the poor lendeth unto Jehovah; and what he hath bestowed will he repay unto him.
texts.pro.19.18: Chasten thy son, seeing there is hope; but set not thy soul upon killing him.
texts.pro.19.19: A man of great wrath shall suffer punishment; for if thou deliver [him], yet thou must do it again.
texts.pro.19.20: Hear counsel, and receive instruction, that thou mayest be wise in thy latter end.
texts.pro.19.21: Many are the thoughts in a man's heart, but the counsel of Jehovah, that doth stand.
texts.pro.19.22: The charm of a man is his kindness; and a poor [man] is better than a liar.
texts.pro.19.23: The fear of Jehovah [tendeth] to life, and he [that hath it] shall rest satisfied without being visited with evil.
texts.pro.19.24: A sluggard burieth his hand in the dish, and will not even bring it to his mouth again.
texts.pro.19.25: Smite a scorner, and the simple will beware; reprove the intelligent, and he will understand knowledge.
texts.pro.19.26: He that ruineth [his] father and chaseth away [his] mother is a son that causeth shame and bringeth reproach.
texts.pro.19.27: Cease, my son, to hear the instruction which causeth to stray from the words of knowledge.
texts.pro.19.28: A witness of Belial scorneth judgment, and the mouth of the wicked swalloweth down iniquity.
texts.pro.19.29: Judgments are prepared for scorners, and stripes for the back of the foolish.
texts.pro.20.1: Wine is a scorner, strong drink is raging; and whoso erreth thereby is not wise.
texts.pro.20.2: The terror of a king is as the roaring of a lion: he that provoketh him to anger sinneth against his own soul.
texts.pro.20.3: It is an honour for a man to cease from strife; but every fool rusheth into it.
texts.pro.20.4: The sluggard will not plough by reason of the winter; he shall beg in harvest, and have nothing.
texts.pro.20.5: Counsel in the heart of man is deep water, and a man of understanding draweth it out.
texts.pro.20.6: Most men will proclaim every one his own kindness; but a faithful man who shall find?
texts.pro.20.7: The righteous walketh in his integrity: blessed are his children after him!
texts.pro.20.8: A king sitting on the throne of judgment scattereth away all evil with his eyes.
texts.pro.20.9: Who can say, I have made my heart clean, I am pure from my sin?
texts.pro.20.10: Divers weights, divers measures, even both of them are abomination to Jehovah.
texts.pro.20.11: Even a child is known by his doings, whether his work be pure, and whether it be right.
texts.pro.20.12: The hearing ear, and the seeing eye, Jehovah hath made even both of them.
texts.pro.20.13: Love not sleep, lest thou come to poverty; open thine eyes, [and] thou shalt be satisfied with bread.
texts.pro.20.14: Bad! bad! saith the buyer; but when he is gone his way, then he boasteth.
texts.pro.20.15: There is gold, and a multitude of rubies; but the lips of knowledge are a precious Jewel.
texts.pro.20.16: Take his garment that is become surety [for] another, and hold him in pledge for strangers.
texts.pro.20.17: Bread of falsehood is sweet to a man, but afterwards his mouth shall be filled with gravel.
texts.pro.20.18: Plans are established by counsel; and with good advice make war.
texts.pro.20.19: He that goeth about talebearing revealeth secrets; therefore meddle not with him that openeth his lips.
texts.pro.20.20: Whoso curseth his father or his mother, his lamp shall be put out in the blackest darkness.
texts.pro.20.21: An inheritance obtained hastily at the beginning will not be blessed in the end.
texts.pro.20.22: Say not, I will recompense evil: wait on Jehovah, and he shall save thee.
texts.pro.20.23: Divers weights are an abomination unto Jehovah; and a false balance is not good.
texts.pro.20.24: The steps of a man are from Jehovah; and how can a man understand his own way?
texts.pro.20.25: It is a snare to a man rashly to say, It is hallowed, and after vows to make inquiry.
texts.pro.20.26: A wise king scattereth the wicked, and bringeth the wheel over them.
texts.pro.20.27: Man's spirit is the lamp of Jehovah, searching all the inner parts of the belly.
texts.pro.20.28: Mercy and truth preserve the king; and he upholdeth his throne by mercy.
texts.pro.20.29: The glory of young men is their strength; and the beauty of old men is the grey head.
texts.pro.20.30: Wounding stripes purge away evil, and strokes [purge] the inner parts of the belly.
texts.pro.21.1: The king's heart in the hand of Jehovah is [as] brooks of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will.
texts.pro.21.2: Every way of a man is right in his own eyes; but Jehovah weigheth the hearts.
texts.pro.21.3: To exercise justice and judgment is more acceptable to Jehovah than sacrifice.
texts.pro.21.4: Lofty eyes, and a proud heart, the lamp of the wicked, is sin.
texts.pro.21.5: The thoughts of the diligent [tend] only to plenteousness; but of every one that is hasty, only to want.
texts.pro.21.6: The getting of treasures by a lying tongue is a fleeting breath of them that seek death.
texts.pro.21.7: The devastation of the wicked sweepeth them away, because they refuse to do what is right.
texts.pro.21.8: Very crooked is the way of a guilty man; but as for the pure, his work is upright.
texts.pro.21.9: It is better to dwell in a corner of the housetop, than with a contentious woman, and a house in common.
texts.pro.21.10: The soul of the wicked desireth evil: his neighbour findeth no favour in his eyes.
texts.pro.21.11: When the scorner is punished, the simple becometh wise; and when the wise is instructed, he receiveth knowledge.
texts.pro.21.12: One that is righteous wisely considereth the house of the wicked: he overthroweth the wicked to [their] ruin.
texts.pro.21.13: Whoso stoppeth his ears at the cry of the poor, he also himself shall cry, and shall not be heard.
texts.pro.21.14: A gift in secret pacifieth anger; and a present in the bosom, vehement fury.
texts.pro.21.15: It is joy to a righteous [man] to do what is right; but it is ruin for the workers of iniquity.
texts.pro.21.16: The man that wandereth out of the way of wisdom shall abide in the congregation of the dead.
texts.pro.21.17: He that loveth mirth shall be a poor man; he that loveth wine and oil shall not be rich.
texts.pro.21.18: The wicked is a ransom for the righteous, and a treacherous [man] in the stead of the upright.
texts.pro.21.19: It is better to dwell in a desert land. than with a contentious and irritable woman.
texts.pro.21.20: There is costly store and oil in the dwelling of a wise [man]; but a foolish man swalloweth it up.
texts.pro.21.21: He that followeth after righteousness and mercy findeth life, righteousness, and honour.
texts.pro.21.22: A wise [man] scaleth the city of the mighty, and casteth down the strength of the confidence thereof.
texts.pro.21.23: Whoso keepeth his mouth and his tongue keepeth his soul from troubles.
texts.pro.21.24: Proud, arrogant, scorner is his name who dealeth in proud wrath.
texts.pro.21.25: The desire of the sluggard killeth him; for his hands refuse to work:
texts.pro.21.26: He coveteth greedily all the day long; but the righteous giveth and spareth not.
texts.pro.21.27: The sacrifice of the wicked is abomination: how much more when they bring it with a wicked purpose!
texts.pro.21.28: A lying witness shall perish; and a man that heareth shall speak constantly.
texts.pro.21.29: A wicked man hardeneth his face; but as for the upright, he establisheth his way.
texts.pro.21.30: There is no wisdom, nor understanding, nor counsel against Jehovah.
texts.pro.21.31: The horse is prepared for the day of battle; but safety is of Jehovah.
texts.pro.22.1: A [good] name is rather to be chosen than great riches; loving favour rather than silver and gold.
texts.pro.22.2: The rich and poor meet together; Jehovah is the maker of them all.
texts.pro.22.3: A prudent [man] seeth the evil, and hideth himself; but the simple pass on, and are punished.
texts.pro.22.4: The reward of humility [and] the fear of Jehovah is riches, and honour, and life.
texts.pro.22.5: Thorns [and] snares are in the way of the perverse: he that keepeth his soul holdeth himself far from them.
texts.pro.22.6: Train up the child according to the tenor of his way, and when he is old he will not depart from it.
texts.pro.22.7: The rich ruleth over the poor; and the borrower is servant to the lender.
texts.pro.22.8: He that soweth unrighteousness shall reap iniquity, and the rod of his wrath shall have an end.
texts.pro.22.9: He that hath a bountiful eye shall be blessed, for he giveth of his bread to the poor.
texts.pro.22.10: Cast out the scorner, and contention will depart, and strife and ignominy shall cease.
texts.pro.22.11: He that loveth pureness of heart, upon whose lips is grace, the king is his friend.
texts.pro.22.12: The eyes of Jehovah preserve knowledge; but he overthroweth the words of the unfaithful.
texts.pro.22.13: The sluggard saith, There is a lion without, I shall be killed in the streets!
texts.pro.22.14: The mouth of strange women is a deep ditch: he with whom Jehovah is displeased shall fall therein.
texts.pro.22.15: Folly is bound in the heart of a child; the rod of correction shall drive it far from him.
texts.pro.22.16: He that oppresseth the poor, it is to enrich him; he that giveth to the rich, [bringeth] only to want.
texts.pro.22.17: Incline thine ear, and hear the words of the wise, and apply thy heart unto my knowledge.
texts.pro.22.18: For it is a pleasant thing if thou keep them within thee: they shall be together fitted on thy lips.
texts.pro.22.19: That thy confidence may be in Jehovah, I have made [them] known to thee this day, even to thee.
texts.pro.22.20: Have not I written to thee excellent things, in counsels and knowledge,
texts.pro.22.21: that I might make thee know the certainty of the words of truth; that thou mightest carry back words of truth to them that send thee?
texts.pro.22.22: Rob not the poor, because he is poor, neither oppress the afflicted in the gate;
texts.pro.22.23: for Jehovah will plead their cause, and despoil the soul of those that despoil them.
texts.pro.22.24: Make no friendship with an angry man, and go not with a furious man;
texts.pro.22.25: lest thou learn his paths, and get a snare to thy soul.
texts.pro.22.26: Be not of them that strike hands, of them that are sureties for debts:
texts.pro.22.27: if thou hast nothing to pay, why should he take away thy bed from under thee?
texts.pro.22.28: Remove not the ancient landmark which thy fathers have set.
texts.pro.22.29: Hast thou seen a man diligent in his work? He shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before the mean.
texts.pro.23.1: When thou sittest to eat with a ruler, consider well who is before thee;
texts.pro.23.2: and put a knife to thy throat, if thou be a man given to appetite.
texts.pro.23.3: Be not desirous of his dainties; for they are deceitful food.
texts.pro.23.4: Weary not thyself to become rich; cease from thine own intelligence:
texts.pro.23.5: wilt thou set thine eyes upon it, it is gone; for indeed it maketh itself wings and it flieth away as an eagle towards the heavens.
texts.pro.23.6: Eat thou not the food of him that hath an evil eye, neither desire thou his dainties.
texts.pro.23.7: For as he thinketh in his soul, so is he. Eat and drink! will he say unto thee; but his heart is not with thee.
texts.pro.23.8: Thy morsel which thou hast eaten must thou vomit up, and thou wilt have wasted thy sweet words.
texts.pro.23.9: Speak not in the ears of a foolish [man], for he will despise the wisdom of thy words.
texts.pro.23.10: Remove not the ancient landmark; and enter not into the fields of the fatherless:
texts.pro.23.11: for their redeemer is mighty; he will plead their cause against thee.
texts.pro.23.12: Apply thy heart unto instruction, and thine ears to the words of knowledge.
texts.pro.23.13: Withhold not correction from the child; for [if] thou beatest him with the rod, he shall not die:
texts.pro.23.14: thou shalt beat him with the rod, and shalt deliver his soul from Sheol.
texts.pro.23.15: My son, if thy heart be wise, my heart shall rejoice, even mine;
texts.pro.23.16: and my reins shall exult, when thy lips speak right things.
texts.pro.23.17: Let not thy heart envy sinners, but [be thou] in the fear of Jehovah all the day;
texts.pro.23.18: for surely there is a result, and thine expectation shall not be cut off.
texts.pro.23.19: Thou, my son, hear and be wise, and direct thy heart in the way.
texts.pro.23.20: Be not among winebibbers, among riotous eaters of flesh.
texts.pro.23.21: For the drunkard and the glutton shall come to poverty; and drowsiness clotheth with rags.
texts.pro.23.22: Hearken unto thy father that begat thee, and despise not thy mother when she is old.
texts.pro.23.23: Buy the truth, and sell it not; wisdom, and instruction, and intelligence.
texts.pro.23.24: The father of a righteous [man] shall greatly rejoice, and he that begetteth a wise [son] shall have joy of him:
texts.pro.23.25: let thy father and thy mother have joy, and let her that bore thee rejoice.
texts.pro.23.26: My son, give me thy heart, and let thine eyes observe my ways.
texts.pro.23.27: For a whore is a deep ditch; and a strange woman is a narrow pit.
texts.pro.23.28: She also lieth in wait as a robber, and increaseth the treacherous among men.
texts.pro.23.29: Who hath woe? Who hath sorrow? Who contentions? Who complaining? Who wounds without cause? Who redness of eyes?
texts.pro.23.30: -- They that tarry long at the wine; they that go to try mixed wine.
texts.pro.23.31: Look not upon the wine when it is red, when it sparkleth in the cup, and goeth down smoothly:
texts.pro.23.32: at the last it biteth like a serpent, and stingeth like an adder.
texts.pro.23.33: Thine eyes shall behold strange women, and thy heart shall speak froward things;
texts.pro.23.34: and thou shalt be as he that lieth down in the midst of the sea, and as he that lieth down upon the top of a mast:
texts.pro.23.35: -- ''They have smitten me, [and] I am not sore; they have beaten me, [and] I knew it not. When shall I awake? I will seek it yet again.''
texts.pro.24.1: Be not thou envious of evil men, neither desire to be with them;
texts.pro.24.2: for their heart studieth destruction, and their lips talk of mischief.
texts.pro.24.3: Through wisdom is a house built, and by understanding it is established;
