texts.pro.11.13: He that goeth about talebearing, revealeth a secret, but, he that is faithful in spirit, concealeth a matter.
texts.pro.11.14: With no guidance, a people will fall, but, safety, lieth in the greatness of the counsellor.
texts.pro.11.15: He that becometh surety for a stranger, goeth to utter ruin, but, he that hateth striking hands, is secure.
texts.pro.11.16: A gracious wife, obtaineth honour, but, the diligent, shall obtain wealth.
texts.pro.11.17: The man of lovingkindness, dealeth well with his own soul, but the cruel man, troubleth his own flesh.
texts.pro.11.18: The lawless man, earneth the wages of falsehood, but, he that soweth righteousness, hath the reward of fidelity.
texts.pro.11.19: A righteous son, [turneth] to life, but, he that pursueth wickedness, to his own death.
texts.pro.11.20: The abomination of Yahweh, are they of perverse heart, but, his delight, are the men of blameless life.
texts.pro.11.21: Hand to hand, the wicked man shall not be held innocent, but, the seed of the righteous, hath been delivered.
texts.pro.11.22: As a ring of gold in the snout of a swine, is a woman of beauty who hath abandoned discretion.
texts.pro.11.23: The desire of the righteous, is only good, the expectation of the lawless, is wrath.
texts.pro.11.24: There is who scattereth, and increaseth yet more, and who withholdeth of what is due, only to come to want.
texts.pro.11.25: The liberal soul, shall be enriched, and, he that refresheth, shall himself also be refreshed.
texts.pro.11.26: He that keepeth back corn, the populace will curse him, but there is, a blessing, for the head of him that selleth.
texts.pro.11.27: He that diligently seeketh good, aimeth at favour, but, he that studieth mischief, it shall come on himself.
texts.pro.11.28: He that trusteth in his riches, the same, shall fall, but, like the leaf, shall the righteous break forth.
texts.pro.11.29: He that troubleth his own house, shall inherit the wind, but, a servant, shall the foolish be, to the wise in heart.
texts.pro.11.30: The fruit of the righteous, is a tree of life, and, he that rescueth souls, is wise.
texts.pro.11.31: Lo! the righteous, in the earth shall be recompensed, how much more the lawless and the sinner.
texts.pro.12.1: He that loveth correction, loveth knowledge, but, he that hateth reproof, is brutish.
texts.pro.12.2: A good man, obtaineth favour from Yahweh, but, a man of wicked devices, will he condemn.
texts.pro.12.3: A son of earth, shall not be established, by lawlessness, but, the root of the righteous, shall not be disturbed.
texts.pro.12.4: A virtuous woman, is the crown of her husband, but, a veritable decay in his bones, is she that causeth shame.
texts.pro.12.5: The plans of the righteous, are just, but, the counsels of the lawless, are deceitful.
texts.pro.12.6: The words of the lawless, are—of lying in wait for blood, but, the mouth of the upright, shall deliver them.
texts.pro.12.7: Overthrown are the lawless and they are not, but, the house of the righteous, shall stand.
texts.pro.12.8: In proportion to his prudence, is a man, to be praised, but, the perverse in heart, shall be an object of contempt.
texts.pro.12.9: Better slighted, and have a servant, than to honour oneself, and come short of bread.
texts.pro.12.10: A righteous man, regardeth the desire of his beast, but, the compassions of the lawless, are cruel.
texts.pro.12.11: He that tilleth his land, shall be filled with food, but, he that runneth after worthless men, lacketh sense.
texts.pro.12.12: A lawless man craveth the prey of the wicked, but, the root of the righteous, is enduring.
texts.pro.12.13: By the transgression of the lips, is the wicked man, ensnared, but the righteous, cometh out of distress.
texts.pro.12.14: Of the fruit of a man’s mouth, shall he be satisfied with good, and, the dealing of the hands of a son of earth, shall be paid back to him.
texts.pro.12.15: The way of the foolish, is right in his own eyes, but, he that hearkeneth to counsel, is wise.
texts.pro.12.16: A foolish man, on the [same] day, letteth his vexation be known, but, he that concealeth an affront, is prudent.
texts.pro.12.17: He that whispereth faithfulness, declareth righteousness, but, a false witness, is a fraud.
texts.pro.12.18: There is who babbleth, as with thrusts of a sword, but, the tongue of the wise, hath healing.
texts.pro.12.19: A lip that is faithful, shall be firm to futurity, but, only for a twinkling, is the tongue that is false.
texts.pro.12.20: Deceit, is in the heart of contrivers of mischief, but, to the counsellors of peace, shall be joy.
texts.pro.12.21: Unseemly to the righteous, is any trouble, but, the lawless, are full of misfortune.
texts.pro.12.22: An abomination to Yahweh, are lips that are false, but, he that dealeth faithfully, is his delight.
texts.pro.12.23: A prudent man, concealeth knowledge, but, the heart of dullards, proclaimeth folly.
texts.pro.12.24: The hand of the diligent, shall bear rule, but, the indolent, shall come under tribute.
texts.pro.12.25: When anxiety is in the heart of a man, one may bow him down, but, a good word, maketh him glad.
texts.pro.12.26: The righteous man guideth his neighbour, but, the way of the lawless, leadeth them astray.
texts.pro.12.27: Indolence, roasteth not, his own game, but, the substance of a man, is precious, when he is diligent.
texts.pro.12.28: In the way of righteousness, is life, and, in the path thereof, immortality,
texts.pro.13.1: A wise son, [cometh of] a father’s correction, but, a scoffer, heareth not a rebuke.
texts.pro.13.2: Of the fruit of his mouth, shall a man eat what is good, but, the soul of the treacherous, [shall be sated with] violence.
texts.pro.13.3: He that watcheth his mouth, guardeth his soul, He that openeth wide his lips, [it shall be] his ruin.
texts.pro.13.4: The sluggard, desireth, but his soul hath, nothing. But, the soul of the diligent, shall be enriched.
texts.pro.13.5: A word of falsehood, the righteous man, hateth, but, the lawless, causeth shame and disgrace.
texts.pro.13.6: Righteousness, guardeth the man of blameless way, but, lawlessness, overthroweth the sinner.
texts.pro.13.7: There is who feigneth himself rich, yet hath nothing at all, who pleadeth poverty, yet hath great substance.
texts.pro.13.8: The ransom of a man’s life, is his wealth, but, the poor, heareth not rebuke.
texts.pro.13.9: The light of the righteous, rejoiceth, but, the lamp of the lawless, goeth out.
texts.pro.13.10: Only by pride, doth one cause contention, but, with the well-advised, is wisdom.
texts.pro.13.11: Wealth gotten by greed, diminisheth, but, he that gathereth by little, increaseth.
texts.pro.13.12: Hope deferred, sickeneth the heart,—but, a tree of life, is desire fulfilled.
texts.pro.13.13: He that despiseth a matter, shall get pledged thereto, but, he that revereth a commandment, the same shall be recompensed.
texts.pro.13.14: the instruction of the wise, is a well-spring of life, by departing from the snares of death.
texts.pro.13.15: Sound discretion, yieldeth favour, but, the way of the treacherous, is rugged.
texts.pro.13.16: Every prudent man, maketh use of knowledge, but, a dullard, spreadeth folly.
texts.pro.13.17: A lawless messenger, falleth into mischief, but, a faithful herald, bringeth healing.
texts.pro.13.18: Poverty and contempt, are for him that neglecteth correction, but, he that regardeth reproof, shall be honoured.
texts.pro.13.19: A desire fulfilled, is sweet to the soul, but it is, an abomination to the lawless, to depart from evil.
texts.pro.13.20: He that walketh with the wise, becometh wise, but, the friend of dullards, becometh foolish.
texts.pro.13.21: Evil pursueth, sinners, but, unto the righteous, shall good be recompensed.
texts.pro.13.22: A good man, leaveth an inheritance to children’s children, but, laid up for the righteous, is the wealth of the sinner.
texts.pro.13.23: Much food, is in the fallow ground of the poor, but there is that is swept away, for want of justice.
texts.pro.13.24: He that withholdeth his rod, hateth his son,—but, he that loveth him, carefully correcteth him.
texts.pro.13.25: The righteous, eateth to satisfy his appetite, but, the belly of the lawless, shall want.
texts.pro.14.1: Every, wise woman, buildeth up her house, but, a foolish one, with her own hands, would break it down.
texts.pro.14.2: He that walketh in his uprightness, is one who revereth Yahweh, but, he that is crooked in his way, is one who despiseth him.
texts.pro.14.3: In the mouth of the foolish, is a haughty rod, but, as for the lips of the wise, thou shalt give heed to them!
texts.pro.14.4: Without cattle, the crib is clean, but, much increase, is in the strength of the ox.
texts.pro.14.5: A faithful witness, will not deceive, but a false witness, uttereth deceitful things.
texts.pro.14.6: A scoffer seeketh wisdom, and there is none, but, knowledge, to the discerning, is easy.
texts.pro.14.7: Get thee from the presence of a man that is a dullard, when thou perceivest not the lips of knowledge.
texts.pro.14.8: The wisdom of the prudent, is to understand his way, but, the folly of dullards, is a fraud.
texts.pro.14.9: the foolish, scoff at guilt, but, between the upright, is good pleasure.
texts.pro.14.10: The heart, knoweth its own bitterness, and, in its joy, no stranger shareth.
texts.pro.14.11: The house of the lawless, shall be destroyed, but, the tent of the upright, shall flourish.
texts.pro.14.12: There is a way that enticeth a man, but, at the latter end thereof, are the ways of death!
texts.pro.14.13: Even, in laughter, the heart may be in pain, and, the latter end of gladness, be grief.
texts.pro.14.14: With his own ways, shall be filled the backslider in heart, and, from himself, shall a good man [be satisfied].
texts.pro.14.15: The simple, believeth every word, but, the prudent, looketh well to his going.
texts.pro.14.16: A wise man, feareth, and avoideth evil, but, a dullard, is haughty and confident.
texts.pro.14.17: The impatient, worketh folly, and, a man of wicked devices, is hated.
texts.pro.14.18: The simple inherit folly, but, the shrewd, crowneth himself with knowledge.
texts.pro.14.19: Abased are the wicked, before the good, and, the lawless, at the gates of the righteous.
texts.pro.14.20: Even by his neighbour, is a poor man hated, but, the lovers of the rich man, are many.
texts.pro.14.21: He that sheweth contempt for his neighbour, sinneth, but, he that sheweth favour to the afflicted, how happy is he!
texts.pro.14.22: Shall they not, become vagrants, who devise evil? but, lovingkindness and faithfulness, [be to] them who devise good.
texts.pro.14.23: By all labour, there will be abundance, but, the talk of the lips, tendeth only to want.
texts.pro.14.24: the crown of the wise, is their wealth, but, the folly of dullards, is, folly.
texts.pro.14.25: A deliverer of souls, is a faithful witness, but, he that uttereth falsehoods, is a fraud.
texts.pro.14.26: In the reverence of Yahweh, is strong security, and, his children, shall have a place of refuge.
texts.pro.14.27: The reverence of Yahweh, is a well-spring of life, that a man may avoid the snares of death.
texts.pro.14.28: In the multitude of a people, is the majesty of the king, but, in the ceasing of population, is the ruin of the prince.
texts.pro.14.29: One slow to anger, hath great understanding, but, the hasty in spirit, exalteth folly.
texts.pro.14.30: The life of the whole body, is a tranquil mind, but, a decay of the bones, is jealousy.
texts.pro.14.31: The oppressor of the poor, hath reproached his Maker, but he that sheweth favour to the needy, is one who, holdeth Him in honour.
texts.pro.14.32: By his own wickedness, shall the lawless man, be thrust down, but the righteous, seeketh refuge in his integrity.
texts.pro.14.33: In the heart of the intelligent, reposeth wisdom, but, in the midst of dullards, it maketh itself known.
texts.pro.14.34: Righteousness, exalteth a nation, but, a reproach to any people, is sin.
texts.pro.14.35: The good-pleasure of a king, is due to a servant who is discreet, but, his indignation, shall be against him that bringeth shame.
texts.pro.15.1: A soft answer, turneth away wrath, but a cutting word raiseth anger.
texts.pro.15.2: The tongue of the wise, adorneth knowledge,—but, the mouth of dullards, belcheth out folly.
texts.pro.15.3: In every place, are the eyes of Yahweh, observing the evil and the good.
texts.pro.15.4: Gentleness of the tongue, is a tree of life, but, crookedness therein, a grievous wound in the spirit.
texts.pro.15.5: A foolish [son], spurneth the correction of his father, but, he that heedeth a reproof, sheweth prudence.
texts.pro.15.6: The household of the righteous man, is a great treasure, but, in the increase of the lawless, is disturbance.
texts.pro.15.7: The lips of the wise, scatter abroad knowledge, but, the heart of dullards, is not right.
texts.pro.15.8: The sacrifice of lawless men, is an abomination to Yahweh, but, the prayer of the upright, is his delight.
texts.pro.15.9: An abomination to Yahweh, is the way of the lawless, but, the pursuer of righteousness, he loveth.
texts.pro.15.10: There is, grievous correction, for him that forsaketh the right path, He that hateth rebuke, shall die.
texts.pro.15.11: Hades and destruction, are before Yahweh, how much more then, the hearts of the sons of men.
texts.pro.15.12: A scoffer, loveth not, one who reproveth him, unto the wise, doth he not go.
texts.pro.15.13: A joyful heart, maketh a pleasing countenance,—but, in sorrow of heart, is a stricken spirit.
texts.pro.15.14: The heart of the intelligent, seeketh knowledge, but, the mouth of dullards, feedeth on folly.
texts.pro.15.15: All the days of the afflicted, are sorrowful, but, a cheerful heart, is a continual banquet.
texts.pro.15.16: Better is a little, with the reverence of Yahweh, than great treasure, and disquietude therewith.
texts.pro.15.17: Better is an allowance of herbs, and love, there, than a fatted ox, and hatred therewith.
texts.pro.15.18: A wrathful man, stirreth up strife, but, he that is slow to anger, calmeth contention.
texts.pro.15.19: The way of the sluggard, is like a thorn hedge, but, the path of the upright, is a raised road.
texts.pro.15.20: A wise son, maketh a glad father,—but, a dullard, despiseth his own mother.
texts.pro.15.21: Folly, is joy to him that lacketh sense,—but, a man of understanding, taketh a straight course.
texts.pro.15.22: Plans, are frustrated, for lack of consultation, but, by the multitude of counsellors, shall counsel, be established.
texts.pro.15.23: A man hath joy, in the answer of his own mouth, and, a word in its season,—how good!
texts.pro.15.24: The way of life, is upwards to the prudent, that he may depart from hades beneath.
texts.pro.15.25: The house of proud men, will Yahweh tear down, but he will maintain the boundary of the widow.
texts.pro.15.26: An abomination to Yahweh, are the plottings of the wicked, but, with the pure, are sayings of sweetness.
texts.pro.15.27: He, troubleth his own house, who graspeth with greed, but, he that hateth gifts, shall live.
texts.pro.15.28: The heart of the righteous, studieth to answer, but, the mouth of the lawless, belcheth out mischiefs.
texts.pro.15.29: Far off is Yahweh, from the lawless, but, the prayer of the righteous, will he hear.
texts.pro.15.30: The sparkling of bright eyes, rejoiceth the heart, Good news, giveth marrow to the bones.
texts.pro.15.31: The ear that heareth the reproof which giveth life, in the midst of the wise, shall remain.
texts.pro.15.32: He that declineth correction, despiseth his own soul, but, he that heareth reproof, gaineth sense.
texts.pro.15.33: The reverence of Yahweh, is the correction of wisdom, and, before honour, is humility.
texts.pro.16.1: To man, belong the preparations of the heart, but, from Yahweh, cometh the answer of the tongue.
texts.pro.16.2: All the ways of a man, [may be] pure in his own eyes, but, he that testeth spirits, is Yahweh.
texts.pro.16.3: Roll, upon Yahweh, thy doings, that thy plans, may be established.
texts.pro.16.4: Everything, hath Yahweh made for its own purpose, yea, even the lawless one, for the day of calamity.
texts.pro.16.5: An abomination to Yahweh, is every one who is haughty in heart, hand to hand, he shall not be held innocent.
texts.pro.16.6: By lovingkindness and fidelity, shall iniquity be covered, and, in the revering of Yahweh, is a turning away from wrong.
texts.pro.16.7: When, acceptable to Yahweh, are the ways of a man, even his enemies, doth he cause to make peace with him.
texts.pro.16.8: Better a little with righteousness, than large revenues, without justice.
texts.pro.16.9: A man’s heart, deviseth his way, but, Yahweh, directeth his steps.
texts.pro.16.10: An oracle, is on the lips of a king, in giving sentence, his mouth must not be unfaithful.
texts.pro.16.11: The balance and scales of justice, belong to Yahweh, and, his handiwork, are all the weights of the bag.
texts.pro.16.12: The abomination of kings, is to work lawlessness, for, by righteousness, is established a throne.
texts.pro.16.13: The delight of kings, are lips of righteousness,—and, the words of uprightness, he loveth.
texts.pro.16.14: The wrath of a king, [meaneth] messengers of death, but, a man who is wise, will appease it.
texts.pro.16.15: In the light of a king’s countenance, is life, and, his good-pleasure, is like the cloud of harvest-rain.
texts.pro.16.16: To acquire wisdom, how much better than gold! and, to get hold of understanding, more choice than silver!
texts.pro.16.17: The highway of the upright, is to avoid evil, He preserveth his soul, who guardeth his way.
texts.pro.16.18: Before grievous injury, pride! and, before a fall, haughtiness of spirit!
texts.pro.16.19: Better is lowliness of spirit, with the patient, than a portion of spoil, with the proud.
texts.pro.16.20: He that showeth discretion concerning a matter, shall find good, and, he that trusteth in Yahweh, how happy is he!
texts.pro.16.21: The wise in heart, shall be called intelligent, and, sweetness of lips, increaseth persuasiveness.
texts.pro.16.22: A well-spring of life, is discretion to its owner, but, the correction of the foolish, is folly.
texts.pro.16.23: The heart of the wise, giveth discretion to his mouth, and, upon his lips, increaseth persuasiveness.
texts.pro.16.24: A comb of honey, are pleasant words, sweet to the taste and healing to the bone.
texts.pro.16.25: There is a way that enticeth a man, but, at the latter end thereof, are the ways of death.
texts.pro.16.26: The appetite of the toiler, hath toiled for him, for his mouth, hath urged him on.
texts.pro.16.27: An abandoned man, diggeth up mischief,—and, upon his lips, as it were a fire is scorching.
texts.pro.16.28: A perverse man, sendeth forth strife, and, a tattler, separateth intimate friends.
texts.pro.16.29: A ruthless man, enticeth his neighbour, and leadeth him in a way, not good.
texts.pro.16.30: Closing his eyes, to devise perverse things, biting his lips, he hath plotted mischief.
texts.pro.16.31: A crown of adorning, is a hoary head, in the way of righteousness, it should be found.
texts.pro.16.32: Better he that is slow to anger, than a hero, and he that ruleth his spirit, than he that captureth a city.
texts.pro.16.33: Into the lap, is cast the lot, but, from Yahweh, is its every decision.
texts.pro.17.1: Better a dry morsel, and peace therewith, than a house full of contentious sacrifices.
texts.pro.17.2: A prudent servant, shall rule over a son who causeth shame, and, in the midst of brothers, shall he share the inheritance.
texts.pro.17.3: Fining-pot for silver, crucible for gold, but, he that trieth hearts, is Yahweh.
texts.pro.17.4: Discord, giveth heed to the aggrieving lip,—Falsehood, giveth ear to the destroying tongue.
texts.pro.17.5: He that mocketh the poor, hath reproached his Maker, He that maketh merry at distress, shall not be held innocent.
texts.pro.17.6: The crown of old men, consists of children’s children, and the adornment of children, is their fathers.
texts.pro.17.7: Unseemly in an unworthy man, is the lip of excellence, much more, in one of noble mind, the lip of falsehood.
texts.pro.17.8: A gift, in the eyes of its owner, is, a stone of beauty, whithersoever it turneth, it bringeth prosperity.
texts.pro.17.9: He that hideth a transgression, seeketh love, but, he that repeateth a matter, separateth intimate friends.
texts.pro.17.10: A reproof sinketh more deeply into an intelligent man than a hundred stripes, into a dullard!
texts.pro.17.11: Nothing less than rebellion, doth a wicked man seek, and, a relentless messenger, shall be sent out against him.
texts.pro.17.12: Let a bereaved bear encounter man, rather than a dullard, with his folly!
texts.pro.17.13: He that returneth evil for good, evil shall not depart from his house.
texts.pro.17.14: A letting forth of water, is the beginning of strife, therefore, before it breaketh out, abandon, contention.
texts.pro.17.15: He that justifieth the lawless, and he that condemneth the righteous, an abomination to Yahweh, are they, both.
texts.pro.17.16: Wherefore is there a price in the hand of a dullard? that he who is without sense, may acquire wisdom.
texts.pro.17.17: At all times, doth a friend love, and, a brother for distress, must be born.
texts.pro.17.18: A man lacking sense, is one who striketh hands, giving security, before his neighbour.
texts.pro.17.19: A lover of transgression, is one who loveth strife, he that heighteneth his door, seeketh grievous harm.
texts.pro.17.20: The crooked in heart, shall not find good, and, he that is perverse with his tongue, shall fall into wickedness.
texts.pro.17.21: He that begetteth a dullard, it is to his own grief, neither can the father of the base, rejoice.
texts.pro.17.22: A joyful heart, worketh an excellent cure,—but, a stricken spirit, drieth up the bone.
texts.pro.17.23: A bribe out of his bosom, doth a lawless man take, to pervert the ways of justice.
texts.pro.17.24: Before the face of the discerning, is wisdom, but, the eyes of a dullard, are in the ends of the earth.
texts.pro.17.25: A vexation to his father, is the son that is a dullard, and a bitterness, to her that bare him.
texts.pro.17.26: Surely, to chastise the righteous, is not good, to smite the noble-minded for equity.
texts.pro.17.27: Sparing of his words, is one who valueth knowledge, and, of a thoughtful spirit, is a man of intelligence.
texts.pro.17.28: Even a fool, holding his peace, is accounted, wise,—He that closeth his lips, [is thought] to have understanding.
texts.pro.18.1: A man seeketh, for satisfaction, going his own way, through all safe counsel, he breaketh.
texts.pro.18.2: A dullard, delighteth not, in understanding, in nothing save the exposing of his own heart.
texts.pro.18.3: When the lawless man cometh in, then cometh also contempt, and, with shame, reproach.
texts.pro.18.4: Deep waters, are the words of a man’s mouth,—a bubbling brook, the well-spring of wisdom.
texts.pro.18.5: To prefer a lawless man, is not good, thrusting away the righteous, in judgment.
texts.pro.18.6: the lips of a dullard, enter into contention, and his mouth, for blows, crieth out.
texts.pro.18.7: The mouth of a dullard, is his ruin, and, his lips, are a snare to his soul.
texts.pro.18.8: the words of a tattler, are dainties, they, therefore go down into the chambers of the inner man.
texts.pro.18.9: Surely he that is slothful in his work, brother, is he to a master at laying waste.
texts.pro.18.10: A tower of strength, is the Name of Yahweh, thereinto, runneth the righteous, and is safe.
texts.pro.18.11: The substance of a rich man, is his strong city, and like a high wall, in his imagination.
texts.pro.18.12: Before grievous injury, a man’s heart is haughty, and, before honour, is humility.
texts.pro.18.13: He that answereth before he heareth, a folly, it is to him, and, a reproach.
texts.pro.18.14: The spirit of a man, sustaineth his sickness, but, a dejected spirit, who can bear it?
texts.pro.18.15: the heart of the intelligent, acquireth knowledge, yea, the ear of the wise, seeketh knowledge.
texts.pro.18.16: The gift of a man, maketh room for him, and, before great men, setteth him down.
texts.pro.18.17: Righteous is he that is first in his own cause, then cometh his neighbour, and thoroughly searcheth him.
texts.pro.18.18: The lot causeth, contentions, to cease, and, the mighty, it parteth.
texts.pro.18.19: A brother estranged, [is worse] than a strong city,—and, contentions, are as the bar of a citadel.
texts.pro.18.20: Of the fruit of a man’s mouth, shall his inmost mind be satisfied, with the product of his lips, shall he be satisfied.
texts.pro.18.21: Death and life, are in the power of the tongue, and, its friends, shall eat its fruits.
texts.pro.18.22: Who hath found a wife, hath found a blessing, and hath obtained favour from Yahweh.
texts.pro.18.23: Supplications, doth the poor man utter, but, the rich, answereth fiercely.
texts.pro.18.24: A man having [many] friends, shall come to ruin, but there is a loving one, who sticketh closer than a brother.
texts.pro.19.1: Better is a poor man, walking in his integrity, than one of perverse lips, and, he, a dullard.
texts.pro.19.2: Surely, for the soul to be, without knowledge, is not good, and, he that hasteth with his feet, strayeth.
texts.pro.19.3: The folly of a man, subverteth his way, and, against Yahweh, his heart is angry.
texts.pro.19.4: Wealth, addeth many friends, but, the poor man, from his own friend, is parted.
texts.pro.19.5: A false witness, shall not be held innocent, and, he that uttereth lies, shall not escape.
texts.pro.19.6: Many, will entreat the favour of a noble, and, every one, is a friend to a man abounding in gifts.
texts.pro.19.7: All the brethren of a poor man, hate him, how much more have, his friends, gone far from him, he may hunt up promises—there are none.
texts.pro.19.8: He that acquireth sense, loveth his own soul, he that guardeth understanding, shall find blessing.
texts.pro.19.9: A false witness, shall not be held innocent, and, he that uttereth lies, shall perish.
texts.pro.19.10: Unseemly for a dullard, is delicate living, how much more for, a servant, to bear rule over princes.
texts.pro.19.11: The discretion of a man, deferreth his anger, and, his adorning, is to pass over transgression.
texts.pro.19.12: The growl as of a young lion, is the rage of a king, but, like dew upon the grass, is his good pleasure.
texts.pro.19.13: Engulfing ruin to his father, is a son that is a dullard,—and, a continuous dripping, are the contentions of a wife.
texts.pro.19.14: House and substance, are an inheritance from one’s fathers, but, from Yahweh, cometh a wife who is prudent.
texts.pro.19.15: Sloth, falleth into a deep sleep, and, a soul that is indolent, shall famish.
texts.pro.19.16: One who guardeth the commandment, guardeth his life, he that is reckless in his ways, shall die.
texts.pro.19.17: A lender to Yahweh, is one who sheweth favour to the poor, and, his good deed, He will pay him back.
texts.pro.19.18: Correct thy son, because there is hope, yet, not so as to slay him, let thy passion be excited.
texts.pro.19.19: A man in a rage, taketh away the penalty,—nevertheless, if thou let him go free, the more [stripes] must thou add.
texts.pro.19.20: Hear counsel, receive correction, that thou mayest be wise in thine after-life.
texts.pro.19.21: Many are the devices in a man’s heart, but, the counsel of Yahweh, that, shall stand.
texts.pro.19.22: The charm of a man, is his lovingkindness,—and better a poor man, than one who deceiveth.
texts.pro.19.23: The reverence of Yahweh, leadeth to life, satisfied then, let a man remain—let him not be visited by calamity.
texts.pro.19.24: A sluggard burieth his hand in the dish, even unto his own mouth, will he not bring it back.
texts.pro.19.25: The scoffer, thou shalt smite, and, the simple, will beware, but correct a man of intelligence—he will understand teaching.
texts.pro.19.26: He that ruineth his father, and chaseth away his mother, is a son causing shame and reproach.
texts.pro.19.27: Cease, my son, to hear instruction that would cause thee to wander from the sayings of knowledge.
texts.pro.19.28: An abandoned witness, scorneth justice, and, the mouth of lawless men, swalloweth iniquity.
texts.pro.19.29: Prepared for scoffers, are punishments, and stripes, for the back of dullards.
texts.pro.20.1: Wine is, a scoffer, and strong drink, a brawler, every one therefore who erreth therein, is unwise.
texts.pro.20.2: The growl as of a young lion, is the dread inspired by a king, he that provoketh him, endangereth his own life.
texts.pro.20.3: Honour, hath the man who sitteth away from strife, but, any fool, may break through.
texts.pro.20.4: By reason of the autumn, a sluggard will not plough, therefore shall he beg in harvest, and there be nothing.
texts.pro.20.5: Deep water, is counsel in a man’s heart, but, a man of understanding, will draw it out.
texts.pro.20.6: A kind man one may call, a great man,—but, a faithful man, who can find?
texts.pro.20.7: As for a righteous man, walking in his integrity, how happy are his children after him!
texts.pro.20.8: A king sitting on the throne of judgment, scattereth, with his eyes, all wrong.
texts.pro.20.9: Who can say, I have cleansed my heart, I am pure from my sin?
texts.pro.20.10: Divers weights, and divers measures, an abomination to Yahweh, are they, both.
texts.pro.20.11: Even, by his doings, doth a youth make himself known, whether, pure and upright, be his work.
texts.pro.20.12: The hearing ear, and the seeing eye, Yahweh hath made them, both.
texts.pro.20.13: Do not love sleep, lest thou come to poverty, open thine eyes, be satisfied with bread.
texts.pro.20.14: Bad! bad! saith the buyer, but, going his way, then, he boasteth.
texts.pro.20.15: There are gold, and an abundance of corals, but, precious jewels, are the lips of knowledge.
texts.pro.20.16: Take his garment who is pledge for a stranger,—then, for a woman unknown, accept him as surety.
texts.pro.20.17: Sweet to a man, may be the bread of falsehood, but, afterward, shall his mouth be filled with gravel.
texts.pro.20.18: Plans—by counsel, shalt thou establish, and, with concerted measures, make thou war.
texts.pro.20.19: A revealer of secrets, is one who goeth about talebearing, therefore, with him who openeth his lips, shalt thou not have fellowship.
texts.pro.20.20: Whoso revileth his father or his mother, his lamp shall be put out in deep darkness.
texts.pro.20.21: An inheritance hastily gotten at the beginning, the latter end thereof, shall not bring blessing.
texts.pro.20.22: Do not say, I will requite wrong! Wait thou for Yahweh that he may save thee.
texts.pro.20.23: An abomination to Yahweh, are divers weights, and, deceptive balances, are not good.
texts.pro.20.24: From Yahweh, are a man’s steps, a son of earth, then—how can he discern his way?
texts.pro.20.25: It is a snare to a man, that he should rashly cry Holy! and, after making vows, to reflect!
texts.pro.20.26: A wise king, winnoweth out the lawless, when he hath turned over them the wheel.
texts.pro.20.27: The lamp of Yahweh, is the spirit of a son of earth, searching all the chambers of the inner man.
texts.pro.20.28: Lovingkindness and faithfulness, will guard a king,—therefore should he support, with lovingkindness, his throne.
texts.pro.20.29: The beauty of young men, is their strength, and, the ornament of old men, a hoary head.
texts.pro.20.30: Blows that cut in, cleanse away wickedness, and, smitings, [enter] the chambers of the inner man.
texts.pro.21.1: [Like] channels of water, is the heart of a king, in the hand of Yahweh,—whithersoever he will, he turneth it.
texts.pro.21.2: Every way of a man, may be right in his own eyes, but, he that testeth hearts, is Yahweh.
texts.pro.21.3: To do righteousness and justice, is more choice to Yahweh than sacrifice.
texts.pro.21.4: Loftiness of eyes, and ambition of heart—the lamp of the lawless, are sin.
texts.pro.21.5: The plans of the diligent, tend only to abundance, but, of every one that is urgent, only to want.
texts.pro.21.6: The gaining of treasures with a tongue of falsehood, is a vapour driven away, [they who seek them] seek death,
texts.pro.21.7: The violence of the lawless, shall drag them away,—because they have refused to do justice.
texts.pro.21.8: Crooked is the way of a guilty man, but, as for the pure, straight is his dealing.
texts.pro.21.9: Better to dwell on the corner of the roof, than a quarrelsome wife, and a house in common.
texts.pro.21.10: The soul of the lawless man, craveth mischief, his own friend, findeth no favour in his eyes.
texts.pro.21.11: When the scoffer is punished, the simple, becometh wise, when the wise is instructed, he receiveth knowledge.
texts.pro.21.12: The Righteous One observeth the house of the lawless,—He is ready to cast down lawless men into misfortune.
texts.pro.21.13: He that shutteth his ear from the cry of the poor, even he, shall call, and not be answered.
texts.pro.21.14: A gift in secret, quencheth anger, and, a present in the bosom, mighty wrath.
texts.pro.21.15: It is a joy, to a righteous man, to do justice, but, dismay, to the workers of iniquity.
texts.pro.21.16: The man who wandereth from the way of discretion, in the gathered host of the shades, shall settle down.
texts.pro.21.17: A needy man, shall he be that loveth merriment, the lover of wine and oil, shall not become rich.
texts.pro.21.18: A ransom for the righteous, is the lawless, and, instead of upright men, the traitor.
texts.pro.21.19: Better to dwell in a desert land, than with a woman, quarrelsome and provoking.
texts.pro.21.20: Desirable treasure and oil, are in the home of the wise, but, a man who is a dullard, will destroy it.
texts.pro.21.21: He that pursueth righteousness and lovingkindness, shall find life, righteousness and honour.
texts.pro.21.22: A city of heroes, doth a wise man scale, and bringeth down the strength of its confidence.
texts.pro.21.23: He that keepeth his mouth and his tongue, keepeth, out of distresses, his soul.
texts.pro.21.24: A haughty insolent one—Scoffer is his name, is he that acteth in a transport of pride.
texts.pro.21.25: The craving of the sluggard, killeth him, for his hands have refused to work.
texts.pro.21.26: All the day, he greatly craveth, whereas, the righteous, giveth, and doth not spare.
texts.pro.21.27: The sacrifice of the lawless, is an abomination, how much more, when, with wickedness, he bringeth it in!
texts.pro.21.28: A false witness, shall perish, but, the man who hearkeneth, with abiding effect, shall speak.
texts.pro.21.29: A lawless man emboldeneth his face, but, as for the upright, he, directeth his ways.
texts.pro.21.30: There is no wisdom, nor understanding, nor counsel, to confront Yahweh.
texts.pro.21.31: The horse, is prepared for the day of battle, but, to Yahweh, pertaineth the victory.
texts.pro.22.1: More choice, is a name, than great riches, beyond silver and gold, is pleasant grace.
texts.pro.22.2: The rich and the poor, meet together, the maker of them all, is Yahweh.
texts.pro.22.3: A prudent man, seeth calamity, and hideth himself, but, the simple, pass on, and suffer.
texts.pro.22.4: The reward of humility, is the reverence of Yahweh, riches, and honour, and life.
texts.pro.22.5: Thorns and snares, are in the way of the perverse,—he that guardeth his soul, shall be far from them.
texts.pro.22.6: Train up a youth, in the direction of his duty, even when he becometh old, he will not depart from it.
texts.pro.22.7: The rich, over the poor, beareth rule,—and, slave, is the borrower to the lender.
texts.pro.22.8: He that soweth perversity, shall reap trouble, and, the rod of his wrath, shall be ready.
texts.pro.22.9: A benevolent eye, the same, shall be blessed,—because he hath given of his bread to the poor.
texts.pro.22.10: Drive away the scoffer, that strife may depart, and quarrel, and contempt may cease.
texts.pro.22.11: Yahweh loveth the pure in heart, gracious are his lips, his friend is the king!
texts.pro.22.12: The eyes of Yahweh, watch over knowledge, therefore hath he overturned the words of the treacherous.
texts.pro.22.13: Saith the sluggard, A lion outside! Amidst the broadways, shall I be slain.
texts.pro.22.14: A deep chasm, is the mouth of strange women, he with whom Yahweh is indignant, falleth there.
texts.pro.22.15: Foolishness, is bound up in the heart of a youth, the rod of correction, shall drive it far from him.
texts.pro.22.16: He that oppresseth the poor, to make increase for himself, giving to the rich, shall surely come to want.
texts.pro.22.17: Incline thine ear and hear the words of wise men, then, thy heart, wilt thou apply to my teaching;
texts.pro.22.18: For sweet shall they be, when thou shalt keep them in thine inmost mind, they shall fit well together, upon thy lips.
texts.pro.22.19: That in Yahweh may be thy trust, I have made them known to thee to-day, even to thee.
texts.pro.22.20: Have I not written for thee noble things, with counsels and knowledge:
texts.pro.22.21: To cause thee to know the meaning of faithful sayings, that thou mayest give back faithful sayings to them who ask thee.
texts.pro.22.22: Do not rob the poor, because he is poor, neither crush thou the oppressed in the gate;
texts.pro.22.23: For, Yahweh, will plead their cause, and will despoil their despoilers of life.
texts.pro.22.24: Do not have friendship with one given to anger, and, with a wrathful man, shall thou not enter in:
texts.pro.22.25: Lest thou learn his ways, and take a snare to thy soul.
texts.pro.22.26: Be not of them who strike hands, of them who are sureties for debts:
texts.pro.22.27: If thou hast nothing to pay, why should one take away thy bed from under thee?
texts.pro.22.28: Do not move back the ancient boundary, which thy father’s made.
texts.pro.22.29: Seest thou a man prompt in his business? before kings, shall he stand, he shall not stand before men who are obscure.
texts.pro.23.1: When thou sittest to eat with a ruler, thou shalt consider well, what is before thee;
texts.pro.23.2: And shalt put a knife to thy throat, if, of great appetite, thou art:
texts.pro.23.3: Do not crave his dainties, for, the same, are deceitful food.
texts.pro.23.4: Do not toil to get wealth, of thine own understanding, forbear:
texts.pro.23.5: Wilt thou let thine eye fly thereupon, when it is nothing? for it will, surely make, itself wings, Like an eagle, will it wing its way across the heavens.
texts.pro.23.6: Do not eat the food of him that hath a begrudging eye, neither crave thou his dainties;
texts.pro.23.7: For, just as he hath thought in his own mind, so, he is: Eat and drink! he may say to thee, but, his heart, is not with thee.
texts.pro.23.8: As for thy morsel thou hast eaten, thou shalt vomit it, so shalt thou waste thy things so sweet.
texts.pro.23.9: In the ears of a dullard, do not speak, for he will despise the good sense of thy words.
texts.pro.23.10: Do not move back the ancient boundary, and, into the fields of the fatherless, do not enter;
texts.pro.23.11: For, their near of kin, is strong, he, will plead their cause with thee.
texts.pro.23.12: Bring, to correction, thy heart, and thine ears, to the sayings of knowledge.
texts.pro.23.13: Do not withhold, from a child, correction, When thou smitest him with the rod, he shall not die:
texts.pro.23.14: Thou, with the rod, shalt smite him, and, his soul from hades, shalt thou deliver.
texts.pro.23.15: My son! if thy heart be wise, my heart shall rejoice, even mine.
texts.pro.23.16: So shall my reins exult, when thy lips speak the things that are right.
texts.pro.23.17: Let not thy heart be envious of sinners, only of the reverence of Yahweh, all day long;
texts.pro.23.18: For surely there is a future, and, thine expectation, shall not be cut off.
texts.pro.23.19: Hear, thou, my son, and be wise, and lead forward, in duty, thy heart.
texts.pro.23.20: Do not be among them who tipple with wine,—among them who are gluttons;
texts.pro.23.21: For, the tippler and the glutton, shall come to poverty, and, rags, shall Slumber put on!
texts.pro.23.22: Hearken to thy father here, who begat thee, and despise not, when she is old, thy mother.
texts.pro.23.23: Truth, buy thou, but do not sell, wisdom, and correction, and understanding.
texts.pro.23.24: Greatly shall exult, the father of a righteous man, and, he that begetteth a wise son, shall rejoice in him:
texts.pro.23.25: Rejoice shall thy father and thy mother, yea she, shall exult, who bare thee.
texts.pro.23.26: Oh give, my son, thy mind unto me, and let, thine eyes, observe, my ways;
texts.pro.23.27: For, a deep chasm, is the unchaste woman, and, a narrow pit, the female unknown;
texts.pro.23.28: Yea, she, as for prey, lieth in wait, and, the treacherous among mankind, she causeth to abound.
texts.pro.23.29: Who hath woe? Who hath outcry of pain? Who hath contentions? Who hath complaining? Who hath needless wounds? Who hath dullness of eyes?
texts.pro.23.30: They who tarry over wine, they who go in to search for mixed wine.
texts.pro.23.31: Do not look on wine when it becometh red, when it giveth in the cup its sparkle, glideth down smoothly.
texts.pro.23.32: Its after effect, is that, like a serpent, it biteth, and, like a viper, it doth sting.
texts.pro.23.33: Thine eyes, will see strange women, and, thy heart, will speak perverse things:
texts.pro.23.34: So shalt thou become, as one lying down in the heart of the sea,—or as one lying down on the top of the mastgear:
texts.pro.23.35: They smote me—I felt no pain, They struck me down—I noticed it not,—When shall I wake up? I will go on, I will seek it, again!
texts.pro.24.1: Be not thou envious of wicked men, neither crave to be with them;
texts.pro.24.2: For, violence, their heart muttereth, and, mischief, their lips do speak.
texts.pro.24.3: In wisdom, is a house builded, and, in understanding, is it established;
texts.pro.24.4: And, in knowledge, chambers are filled, with all acquisitions, costly and fair.
texts.pro.24.5: A wise man, is mighty, and, a man of knowledge, becometh alert in vigour.
texts.pro.24.6: Surely, with concerted measures, shalt thou make for thyself war, and, success, lieth in the greatness of the counsellor.
texts.pro.24.7: Unattainable to a foolish man, are the dictates of wisdom, in the gate, he openeth not his mouth.
texts.pro.24.8: He that deviseth to do mischief, him, shall men call, a master of plots.
texts.pro.24.9: The purpose of folly, is sin, and, an abomination to mankind, is a buffoon.
texts.pro.24.10: Thou hast been slothful in the day of straitness, Strait, is thy strength.
texts.pro.24.11: Deliver thou such as are being led forth to death, and, them who are tottering to slaughter, oh that thou wouldst hold back!
texts.pro.24.12: Though thou say, Lo! we knew not this, Shall not, he that proveth hearts, himself, discern? And, he that formeth thy soul, himself, know? and bring back to a son of earth according to his deed?
texts.pro.24.13: My son, eat thou honey, because it is good,—and droppings from the comb [because they are] sweet to thy palate:
texts.pro.24.14: Thus, take knowledge of wisdom, for thine own soul; If thou find it, then there is a future, and, thine expectation, shall not be cut off.
texts.pro.24.15: Do not lie in wait, thou lawless man, against the home of the righteous,—neither destroy thou his place of rest;
texts.pro.24.16: For, seven times, may the righteous fall and yet arise, but, lawless men, shall stumble into calamity.
texts.pro.24.17: When thine enemy falleth, do not thou rejoice, and, when he stumbleth, let not thy heart exult:
texts.pro.24.18: Lest Yahweh see it, and it be wicked in his eyes, and he turn away from him his anger.
texts.pro.24.19: Burn not with vexation against evil doers, be not envious of lawless men;
texts.pro.24.20: For there shall be no future for the wicked, The lamp of the lawless, shall go out.
texts.pro.24.21: Revere thou Yahweh, my son, and the king, and, with the fickle, have thou no fellowship;
texts.pro.24.22: For, suddenly, shall arise their calamity; and, the misfortune of their years, who knoweth?
texts.pro.24.23: These things also, concern the wise, To take note of faces in judgment, is not good.
texts.pro.24.24: He that saith to the lawless man, Righteous, thou art, peoples shall denounce him, populations shall curse him;
texts.pro.24.25: But, to reprovers, one should be pleasant, and, upon them, should come an excellent blessing:
texts.pro.24.26: Lips, should one kiss with one who answereth in right words.
texts.pro.24.27: Prepare, in the open, thy work, and make ready, in the field, for thyself, Afterwards, shalt thou build thy house.
texts.pro.24.28: Do not become a needless witness against thy neighbour, so mightest thou open too wide thy lips:
texts.pro.24.29: Do not say—According to what he hath done to me, so, will I do to him, I will repay every one according to his work.
texts.pro.24.30: By the field of the sluggard, I passed, and by the vineyard of a man lacking sense;
texts.pro.24.31: And lo! there had come up all over it—thorns, there had covered the face thereof—thistles, and, the stone fence thereof, had been thrown down.
texts.pro.24.32: So I observed it, for myself, I applied my heart, I looked—I accepted correction:
texts.pro.24.33: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest:
texts.pro.24.34: So shall come in, as a highwayman, thy poverty, and, thy want, as one armed with a shield.
texts.pro.25.1: These also, are proverbs of Solomon,—which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah transcribed.
texts.pro.25.2: The glory of God, is to conceal a thing, but, the glory of kings, is to search out a thing.
texts.pro.25.3: The heavens for height, and the earth for depth, but, the heart of kings, cannot be searched.
texts.pro.25.4: Remove the dross from the silver, and there cometh forth, to the refiner, a vessel:
texts.pro.25.5: Remove a lawless man from before the king, that his throne, may be established in righteousness.
texts.pro.25.6: Do not honour thyself before a king, nor, in the place of great men, do thou stand;
texts.pro.25.7: For better it be said to thee, Come up hither,—than that thou be put lower down before a noble, whom thine own eyes, have beheld.
texts.pro.25.8: Do not go forth to strive in haste,—lest [thou know not] what to do in the latter end thereof, when thy neighbour, hath put thee to shame.
texts.pro.25.9: Thy contention, urge thou with thy neighbour, and, the secret of another, do not reveal:
texts.pro.25.10: Lest he that heareth expose thee, and, the report concerning thee, turn not away.
texts.pro.25.11: Golden fruit in figured silver baskets, is a word spoken on fitting occasion.
texts.pro.25.12: A ring of gold, and a vessel of precious metal, is a wise reprover, on a hearing ear.
texts.pro.25.13: As the cold of snow in the day of harvest, is a faithful messenger to them who send him,—when, the life of his masters, he restoreth.
texts.pro.25.14: Clouds and wind, when rain there is none, is the man who boasteth himself of a pretended gift.
texts.pro.25.15: By long patience, is a judge persuaded, and, a soft tongue, breaketh the bone.
texts.pro.25.16: Honey having found, eat to suffice thee, lest thou loathe it, and vomit it forth.
texts.pro.25.17: Withhold thy foot from the house of thy neighbour,—lest he be weary of thee, and hate thee.
texts.pro.25.18: A hammer and a sword, and a sharpened arrow, is a man becoming a false witness against his neighbour.
texts.pro.25.19: A broken tooth and a faltering foot, is confidence in the treacherous, in the day of danger.
texts.pro.25.20: As splendour of dress on a cold day—vinegar upon nitre, so is a singer with songs, unto a sad heart.
texts.pro.25.21: If he that hateth thee hunger, give him bread to eat, and, if he be thirsty, give him water to drink;
texts.pro.25.22: For, burning coals, shalt thou be heaping upon his head,—and, Yahweh, will repay thee.
texts.pro.25.23: A north wind, bringeth forth rain, and, a face stirred with indignation, a secretive tongue.
texts.pro.25.24: Better to dwell on the corner of the roof, than a quarrelsome wife, and a house in common.
texts.pro.25.25: As cold water to a thirsty soul, so is a good report from a far country.
texts.pro.25.26: A fountain fouled, a spring spoiled, is a righteous man tottering before one who is lawless.
texts.pro.25.27: To eat honey in abundance, is not good, nor is, searching out their own honour, an honourable thing.
texts.pro.25.28: A city broken down without a wall, is a man who hath no control over his own spirit.
texts.pro.26.1: As snow in summer, and as rain in harvest, so, unbecoming to a dullard is honour.
texts.pro.26.2: As a sparrow in wandering, as a swallow in flying, so, a causeless curse, shall not alight.
texts.pro.26.3: A whip for the horse, a bridle for the ass, and a rod for the back of dullards.
texts.pro.26.4: Do not answer a dullard, according to his folly, lest, even thou thyself, become like him;
texts.pro.26.5: Answer a dullard according to his folly, lest he become wise in his own eyes.
texts.pro.26.6: One who cutteth off feet, one who drinketh down wrong, is he who sendeth a message by the hand of a dullard.
texts.pro.26.7: Useless are the legs of the lame, and a proverb, in the mouth of a dullard.
texts.pro.26.8: Like tying a stone to a sling, so, is he that giveth honour, to a dullard.
texts.pro.26.9: A brier cometh into the hand of a drunken-man, a proverb into the mouth of dullards.
texts.pro.26.10: [As] an archer who woundeth every thing, [so] one who hireth a dullard, and a drunkard crossing the sea.
texts.pro.26.11: As, a dog, returneth onto his own vomit, a dullard, repeateth his folly.
texts.pro.26.12: Thou hast seen a man wise in his own eye,—more hope of a dullard, than of him!
texts.pro.26.13: Saith the sluggard, A roaring lion in the road! A tearing lion in the midst of the broadways.
texts.pro.26.14: The door, turneth on its hinges, and, the sluggard, upon his bed.
texts.pro.26.15: The sluggard burieth his hand in the dish, he is too lazy to bring it back to his mouth.
texts.pro.26.16: Wiser is the sluggard in his own eyes, than, seven persons, who can answer with judgment.
texts.pro.26.17: As he who layeth hold of the ears of a dog, is a passer-by, who giveth vent to his wrath over a quarrel, not his!
texts.pro.26.18: As a madman throwing firebrands, arrows and death,
texts.pro.26.19: So, is a man who deceiveth his neighbour, and saith, Was not, I, in sport?
texts.pro.26.20: Without wood a fire is quenched, and, where there is no tattler, strife is hushed.
texts.pro.26.21: Black coal to burning blocks, and wood to fire, so is a contentious man, for kindling strife.
texts.pro.26.22: the words of a tattler, are dainties, they, therefore go down into the chambers of the inner man.
texts.pro.26.23: Dross silver overlaid upon earthenware, so are burning lips, with a mischievous heart:
texts.pro.26.24: With his lips, the hater dissembleth, but, within himself, he layeth up deceit:
texts.pro.26.25: Though he make gracious his voice, do not trust him, for, seven abominations, are in his heart:
texts.pro.26.26: Hatred may clothe itself with guile, his wickedness shall be disclosed in the convocation.
texts.pro.26.27: He that diggeth a pit, thereinto, shall fall, and, he that rolleth a stone, upon himself, shall it return.
texts.pro.26.28: A false tongue, hateth them who are crushed by it, and, a flattering mouth, worketh occasion of stumbling.
texts.pro.27.1: Do not boast thyself of to-morrow, for thou knowest not what a day may bring forth.
texts.pro.27.2: Let another praise thee, and not thine own mouth, a stranger, and not thine own lips.
texts.pro.27.3: Heavy is a stone, and weighty is sand,—but, the vexation of a fool, is heavier than both.
texts.pro.27.4: The cruelty of rage, and the overflow of anger! But who can stand before, jealousy?
texts.pro.27.5: Better is a rebuke that is open, than love carefully concealed.
texts.pro.27.6: Faithful are the wounds of a friend, but lavished are the kisses of an enemy.
texts.pro.27.7: The surfeited soul, trampleth upon droppings from the comb, but, to the hungry soul, every bitter thing, is sweet.
texts.pro.27.8: As a bird wandering from her nest, so, is a man wandering from his place.
texts.pro.27.9: Oil and perfume, rejoice the heart, the sweetness of one’s friend, more than fragrant wood.
texts.pro.27.10: Thine own friend and thy father’s friend, do not thou forsake; but, the house of thy brother, do not enter, in thy day of calamity, Better a neighbour near, than a brother far off.
texts.pro.27.11: Be wise, my son, and rejoice my heart, that I may answer him that reproacheth me in a matter.
texts.pro.27.12: A prudent man, seeth calamity—he hideth himself, the simple, pass on—they suffer.
texts.pro.27.13: Take a man’s garment when he hath become pledge for a stranger, then, for a female unknown, accept him as surety.
texts.pro.27.14: He that blesseth his friend, with a loud voice, in the morning early, a reproach, shall it be reckoned to him.
texts.pro.27.15: A continuous dripping on a day of downpour, and a contentious wife, are alike:
texts.pro.27.16: He that hideth her, hideth the wind, and, perfume, his right hand may proclaim.
texts.pro.27.17: Let, iron, by iron, become sharp, and let, a man, sharpen the face of his friend.
texts.pro.27.18: He that guardeth the fig-tree, shall eat the fruit thereof, and, he that watcheth over his master, shall be honoured.
texts.pro.27.19: As in water, face [answereth] to face, so, the heart of man to man.
texts.pro.27.20: Hades and destruction, are not satisfied, and, the eyes of a man, are not satisfied.
texts.pro.27.21: Fining pot for silver, and crucible for gold, and, a man, [is to be tried] by what he praiseth.
texts.pro.27.22: Though thou pound a fool in a mortar, amidst grain, with a pestle, his folly, will not depart from him.
texts.pro.27.23: Note well, the appearance of thy flock, apply thy mind to thy herds;
texts.pro.27.24: For, not age-abiding, are riches, nor is the diadem, from generation to generation:—
texts.pro.27.25: The grass, is taken away, and the young shoot, showeth itself, and the herbage of the mountains, is gathered;
texts.pro.27.26: There are, lambs, for thy clothing, and, for the price of thy field, there are he-goats;
texts.pro.27.27: With, enough goats-milk, for thy food—for the food of thy household, and, a maintenance, for thy maidens.
texts.pro.28.1: The lawless, fleeth when no man pursueth, but, the righteous, like a lion, are confident.
texts.pro.28.2: For the transgressions of a land, many are the rulers thereof, but, under an intelligent and discerning man, stability is prolonged.
texts.pro.28.3: A poor man, who oppresseth the helpless, [is like] a rain beating down, leaving no food.
texts.pro.28.4: They who forsake instruction, praise one who is lawless, while, they who keep instruction, are at strife with them.
texts.pro.28.5: Wicked men, consider not justice, but, they who seek Yahweh, consider everything.
texts.pro.28.6: Better a poor man walking in his integrity, than one who is crooked—turning two ways, though, he, be rich.
texts.pro.28.7: He that keepeth instruction, is a son with discernment, but, a companion of squanderers, bringeth shame to his father.
texts.pro.28.8: He that increaseth his substance by interest and profit, for one ready to favour the poor, doth gather it.
texts.pro.28.9: He that turneth away his ear from hearing instruction, even his prayer, is an abomination.
texts.pro.28.10: He that misguideth the upright into a hurtful way! into his own pit, he himself, shall fall, but, men of integrity, shall inherit good.
texts.pro.28.11: Wise in his own eyes, is the man that is rich, but, a poor man of discernment, searcheth him out.
texts.pro.28.12: In the exulting of the righteous, there is great glorying, but, when the lawless arise, a man must be sought for.
texts.pro.28.13: He that covereth his transgressions, shall not prosper, but, he that confesseth and forsaketh, shall find compassion.
texts.pro.28.14: How happy the man who is ever circumspect, whereas, he that hardeneth his heart, shall fall into calamity.
texts.pro.28.15: A growling lion, and a ranging bear, is a lawless ruler, over a poor people.
texts.pro.28.16: A leader, may lack intelligence, yet abound in oppressions, The hater of greed, shall lengthen out days.
texts.pro.28.17: A man oppressed with a person’s blood, unto a pit, shall flee, let them not hold him back.
texts.pro.28.18: He that walketh with integrity, shall be saved, but, he that is crooked, turning two ways, shall fall in one.
texts.pro.28.19: He that tilleth his ground, shall have plenty of bread, but, he that pursueth empty-heads, shall have plenty of poverty.
texts.pro.28.20: A man of fidelity, aboundeth in blessings, but, one hasting to be rich, shall not be held innocent.
texts.pro.28.21: To take note of faces [in judgment], is not good, and, for a bit of bread, a man will transgress.
texts.pro.28.22: A man, hasting to be rich, hath an evil eye, and knoweth not when want may overtake him.
texts.pro.28.23: He that reproveth a man, shall, afterwards, find more, favour, than he that useth a flattering tongue.
texts.pro.28.24: He that robbeth his father or his mother, and saith, It is no transgression, companion, is he to one who wasteth.
texts.pro.28.25: The ambitious in soul, stirreth up strife, but, he that trusteth in Yahweh, shall be enriched.
texts.pro.28.26: He that trusteth his own heart, the same, is a dullard, but, he that walketh wisely, the same, shall be delivered.
texts.pro.28.27: One who giveth to the poor, shall have no want, but, he that hideth his eyes, shall receive many a curse.
texts.pro.28.28: When lawless men rise, a common man will hide himself, but, when they perish, righteous men multiply.
texts.pro.29.1: He that being often reproved stiffeneth his neck, suddenly shall be hurt, and there be no healing.
texts.pro.29.2: When the righteous become great, the people rejoice, but, when a lawless man beareth rule, a people sigh.
texts.pro.29.3: A man who loveth wisdom, gladdeneth his father, but, a companion of harlots, destroyeth wealth.
texts.pro.29.4: A king, by justice, shall establish a land,—but, a man open to bribes, bringeth it to ruin.
texts.pro.29.5: A man who flattereth his neighbour, spreadeth, a net, over his steps.
texts.pro.29.6: In the transgression of a wicked man, is a snare, but, the righteous, doth shout in triumph and rejoice.
texts.pro.29.7: The righteous doth acknowledge the plea of the poor, but, the lawless, regardeth not knowledge.
texts.pro.29.8: Men given to mockery, inflame a city,—but, wise men, turn away anger.
texts.pro.29.9: A wise man pleading with a foolish man, whether he rage or laugh, there is no settlement.
texts.pro.29.10: Blood-thirsty men, hate the blameless man, and, as for the upright, they seek his life.
texts.pro.29.11: All his anger, doth a dullard let go, but, a wise man, by keeping it back, stilleth it.
texts.pro.29.12: When a ruler giveth heed to the word of falsehood, all his attendants, become lawless.
texts.pro.29.13: The poor man and the man of usury, meet together, he that enlighteneth the eyes of them both, is Yahweh.
texts.pro.29.14: When a king judgeth faithfully the poor, his throne, to futurity, shall be established.
texts.pro.29.15: A rod with rebuke, giveth wisdom, but, a youth unrestrained, bringeth shame to his mother.
texts.pro.29.16: When the lawless become great, transgression increaseth, but, the righteous, shall behold, their ruin.
texts.pro.29.17: Correct thy son, that he may give thee rest, that he may give delight to thy soul.
texts.pro.29.18: Where there is no vision, a people is let loose, but, he that keepeth instruction, how happy is he!
texts.pro.29.19: By words, a servant will not be corrected, though he perceiveth, yet is there no answer.
texts.pro.29.20: Thou hast seen a man hasty in his words,—there is, more hope of a dullard, than of him.
texts.pro.29.21: He that dealeth tenderly with his servant from childhood, in his after life, shall have him for a son.
texts.pro.29.22: A man given to anger, stirreth up strife, and, he that exceedeth in wrath, aboundeth in transgression.
texts.pro.29.23: The loftiness of a man, layeth him low,—but, one of a lowly spirit, shall attain unto honour.
texts.pro.29.24: He that shareth with a thief, hateth himself, an oath, he heareth, yet may not tell.
texts.pro.29.25: The fear of man, setteth a snare, but, he that trusteth in Yahweh, shall be placed on high.
texts.pro.29.26: Many, seek the face of a ruler, but, from Yahweh, is the sentence of each one.
texts.pro.29.27: An abomination to the righteous, is the man of perversity, and, an abomination to the lawless, is a man of straightforward way.
texts.pro.30.1: The words of Agur, son of Jakeh, [even] the oracle,—The utterance of the man, for Ithiel, for Ithiel and Ucal.
texts.pro.30.2: Surely, more brutish, am, I, than any man, nor doth, the understanding of a son of earth, pertain to me;
texts.pro.30.3: Neither have I learned wisdom, nor, the knowledge of the Holy Ones, can I acquire.
texts.pro.30.4: Who hath ascended the heavens and then descended? Who hath gathered the wind into his two hands? Who hath wrapped up the waters in a mantle? Who hath set up all the ends of the earth? What is his name and what the name of his son, when thou knowest?
texts.pro.30.5: Every saying of God is refined, A shield, is, he, to them who seek refuge in him.
texts.pro.30.6: Do not add unto his words, lest he convict thee, and thou be found false.
texts.pro.30.7: Two things, have I asked of thee, withhold them not from me, ere yet I die:
texts.pro.30.8: Vanity and falsehood, remove far from me, Neither poverty nor riches, give me, Feed me with the food appointed me:
texts.pro.30.9: Lest I be full, and deny, and say—Who is Yahweh? or lest I be impoverished and steal, and do violence to the Name of my God.
texts.pro.30.10: Do not slander a servant to his master, lest he revile thee, and thou be found guilty.
texts.pro.30.11: A generation! Its father, it revileth, and, its mother, it doth not bless.
texts.pro.30.12: A generation! Pure in its own eyes, yet, from its filth, hath it not been bathed,
texts.pro.30.13: A generation! How lofty are its eyes, and its eyelashes uplifted.
texts.pro.30.14: A generation! Swords, are its teeth, and, knives, its incisors,—to devour the humbled out of the earth, and the needy, from among men.
texts.pro.30.15: The vampire, hath two daughters, Give! Give! Three, there are will not be satisfied, four, have not said, Enough!
texts.pro.30.16: Hades, and barrenness,—A land not satisfied with water, and fire, that saith not, Enough!
texts.pro.30.17: The eye that mocketh a father, and despiseth to obey a mother, the ravens of the valley shall pick it out, and the young of the eagle shall eat it.
texts.pro.30.18: Three, things there are, too difficult for me, yea, four, which I do not understand:
texts.pro.30.19: The way of an eagle in the heavens, the way of a serpent on the rock,—the way of a ship in the heart of the sea, and the way of a man with a maid.
texts.pro.30.20: So, is the way of a woman committing adultery,—she eateth, and wipeth her mouth, and saith, I have done no iniquity!
texts.pro.30.21: Under three things, a land is stirred, yea, under four, she cannot bear up:
texts.pro.30.22: Under a servant, when he reigneth, and a base man, when he is surfeited with food;
texts.pro.30.23: Under a hateful woman, when she is married, and a handmaid when she driveth out her mistress.
texts.pro.30.24: Four, things there are, the small of the earth,—yet, they, are wiser than the wise:
texts.pro.30.25: The ants, a people, not strong,—yet prepare they, in summer, their food;
texts.pro.30.26: The conies, a people of, no power, yet set they, among the crags, their house;
texts.pro.30.27: King, is there none, to, the locusts,—yet go forth in swarms, do they all;
texts.pro.30.28: The lizard, with hands, reneweth its hold,—yet, the same, is in the palaces of the king.
texts.pro.30.29: Three, things there are which step along well, ye, four, which excel in going:
texts.pro.30.30: The lion, hero among beasts, which turneth aside from the face of no one;
texts.pro.30.31: The greyhound, or the he-goat,—and a king, having a band of soldiers with him.
texts.pro.30.32: If thou hast acted basely by lifting thyself up,—if thou hast plotted evil, [put thy] hand to [thy] mouth!
texts.pro.30.33: Surely, the pressing of milk, bringeth forth curd, and, the pressing of the nose, bringeth forth blood, and, the pressing of wrath, bringeth forth strife.
texts.pro.31.1: The words of Lemuel the king,—the strain which was taught him by his mother:—
texts.pro.31.2: What, my son? and what, the son of my womb? aye what, the son of my vows?
texts.pro.31.3: Do not give, to women, thy strength, nor thy ways, to them who ruin kings.
texts.pro.31.4: It is not for kings, O Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine, nor, for dignitaries, to desire strong drink,
texts.pro.31.5: Lest he drink, and forget that which is decreed, and alter the plea of any who are sorely oppressed.
texts.pro.31.6: Give strong drink, to him that is perishing, and wine, to such as are embittered in soul:
texts.pro.31.7: Let him drink, and forget his poverty, and, his wearying toil, let him remember no more.
texts.pro.31.8: Open thy mouth for the dumb, for the cause of all the children of the departed.
texts.pro.31.9: Open thy mouth—judge righteously,—and administer justice for the poor and the needy.
texts.pro.31.10: A virtuous woman, who can find? for, far beyond corals, is her worth.
texts.pro.31.11: The heart of her husband, trusteth her, and, gain, he shall not lack:
texts.pro.31.12: She doeth him good and not evil, all the days of her life:
texts.pro.31.13: She seeketh wool and flax, and worketh willingly with her hands:
texts.pro.31.14: She is like the ships of the merchant, from afar, she bringeth in her food;
texts.pro.31.15: And she riseth, while yet it is night, and giveth food to her household, and a task to her maidens:
texts.pro.31.16: She considereth a field, and procureth it, Out of the fruit of her hands, she planteth a vineyard:
texts.pro.31.17: She girdeth, with strength her loins, and putteth vigour into her arms:
texts.pro.31.18: She tasteth, whether, good, be her merchandise, and her lamp, goeth not out by night:
texts.pro.31.19: Her hands, she putteth forth to the distaff, and, her palms, lay hold of the spindle:
texts.pro.31.20: Her palm, she spreadeth out to the oppressed, and, her hands, she extendeth to the needy:
texts.pro.31.21: She feareth not, for her household, because of the snow, for, all her household, are clothed with crimson:
texts.pro.31.22: Coverlets, she maketh for herself, Of white linen and of purple, is her clothing:
texts.pro.31.23: Known in the gates, is her husband, when he sitteth, with the elders of the land:
texts.pro.31.24: Fine linen wraps, she maketh and selleth, and, girdles, doth she deliver to the trader:
texts.pro.31.25: Strength and dignity, are her clothing, and she laugheth at the time to come:
texts.pro.31.26: Her mouth, she openeth with wisdom, and, the instruction of kindness, is on her tongue:
texts.pro.31.27: She looketh well to the goings of her household, and, the bread of idleness, will she not eat.
texts.pro.31.28: Her children rise up, and call her happy! her husband, and he praiseth her:—
texts.pro.31.29: Many daughters, have done virtuously, but, thou, excellest them all!
texts.pro.31.30: Deceitful is loveliness and vain is beauty, The woman that revereth Yahweh, she, shall be praised:
texts.pro.31.31: Give her of the fruit of her own hands, and let her own works, praise her in the gates.

texts.pro.1.1: Los proverbios de Salomón, hijo de David, rey de Israel:
texts.pro.1.2: para conocer sabiduría y disciplina; para comprender los dichos de la inteligencia; para discernir las palabras del entendimiento;
texts.pro.1.3: para recibir instrucción en el trato sabio, en la rectitud, la justicia y la equidad;
texts.pro.1.4: para dar sagacidad a los simples, conocimiento y discreción al joven —
texts.pro.1.5: para que el sabio escuche y aumente su saber; para que el hombre de entendimiento adquiera sabios consejos;
texts.pro.1.6: para entender los proverbios y las parábolas, las palabras y los enigmas de los sabios.
texts.pro.1.7: El temor de Yahvé es el principio de la sabiduría, mas los necios desprecian la sabiduría y la instrucción.
texts.pro.1.8: Escucha, hijo mío, la instrucción de tu padre, y no abandones la enseñanza de tu madre;
texts.pro.1.9: pues serán corona de gracia para tu cabeza, y collares para tu cuello.
texts.pro.1.10: Hijo mío, si los pecadores quisieren seducirte, no consientas en ello.
texts.pro.1.11: Si dijeren: «Ven con nosotros; pongamos asechanzas para derramar sangre; acechemos al inocente sin motivo;
texts.pro.1.12: devorémoslos vivos como el Seol, y enteros, como los que descienden a la fosa;
texts.pro.1.13: hallaremos toda suerte de riquezas, llenaremos nuestras casas con el botín;
texts.pro.1.14: echa tu suerte con nosotros; tengamos todos una sola bolsa» —
texts.pro.1.15: hijo mío, no andes en el camino con ellos; aparta tu pie de sus veredas,
texts.pro.1.16: porque sus pies corren hacia el mal, y se apresuran a derramar sangre.
texts.pro.1.17: Pues en vano se tiende la red ante los ojos de cualquier ave;
texts.pro.1.18: mas ellos a su propia sangre ponen asechanzas, y contra su propia vida tienden la red.
texts.pro.1.19: Tales son las sendas de todo el que es dado a la codicia; la cual quita la vida de sus poseedores.
texts.pro.1.20: La sabiduría clama por las calles; alza su voz en las plazas;
texts.pro.1.21: clama en los lugares de mucho estruendo; a la entrada de las puertas de la ciudad pronuncia sus palabras:
texts.pro.1.22: “¿Hasta cuándo, oh simples, amaréis la simpleza? ¿Y hasta cuándo los burladores se deleitarán en el escarnio, y los insensatos aborrecerán el conocimiento?
texts.pro.1.23: Volveos a mi reprensión. He aquí, yo derramaré mi espíritu sobre vosotros; os haré saber mis palabras.
texts.pro.1.24: Por cuanto llamé y no quisisteis oír, extendí mi mano y no hubo quien atendiese,
texts.pro.1.25: sino que habéis desechado todo consejo mío y mi reprensión no habéis querido;
texts.pro.1.26: también yo me reiré de vuestra desdicha; me burlaré cuando os viniere lo que teméis,
texts.pro.1.27: cuando viniere como una tormenta lo que teméis, y vuestra calamidad llegare como un torbellino; cuando sobre vosotros viniere tribulación y angustia.
texts.pro.1.28: Entonces me llamaréis, y no responderé; me buscaréis con diligencia, y no me hallaréis.
texts.pro.1.29: Por cuanto aborrecieron la sabiduría, y no escogieron el temor de Yahvé,
texts.pro.1.30: ni quisieron mi consejo, y menospreciaron toda mi reprensión,
texts.pro.1.31: comerán, pues, del fruto de su camino, y se hartarán de sus propios consejos.
texts.pro.1.32: Porque el desvío de los ignorantes los matará, y la prosperidad de los necios los echará a perder.
texts.pro.1.33: Mas el que me oyere, habitará confiadamente y vivirá tranquilo, sin temor del mal”.
texts.pro.2.1: Hijo mío, si recibes mis palabras y atesoras mis mandamientos dentro de ti,
texts.pro.2.2: haciendo que tu oído se incline a la sabiduría y entregues tu corazón a la prudencia;
texts.pro.2.3: si de veras invocas a la inteligencia y a la prudencia elevas tu voz;
texts.pro.2.4: si como a la plata la buscas y la rastreas como a tesoros escondidos,
texts.pro.2.5: entonces entenderás el temor de Yahvé y hallarás el conocimiento de Dios.
texts.pro.2.6: Porque Yahvé da la sabiduría; de su boca proceden la ciencia y la inteligencia.
texts.pro.2.7: Él reserva la sana sabiduría para los rectos; es broquel para los que caminan en integridad,
texts.pro.2.8: a fin de que guarden las sendas del juicio y preserve el camino de sus santos.
texts.pro.2.9: Entonces entenderás justicia, juicio y equidad, y todo buen camino.
texts.pro.2.10: Cuando la sabiduría entrare en tu corazón y el conocimiento fuere grato a tu alma,
texts.pro.2.11: la discreción te guardará; te preservará la inteligencia,
texts.pro.2.12: para librarte del mal camino, de los hombres que hablan perversidades,
texts.pro.2.13: que abandonan las sendas derechas para andar por caminos de tinieblas;
texts.pro.2.14: que se alegran haciendo el mal, que se huelgan en las perversidades del vicio;
texts.pro.2.15: cuyas veredas son torcidas y torcidos sus caminos;
texts.pro.2.16: para librarte de la mujer ajena, de la extraña que halaga con sus palabras,
texts.pro.2.17: la cual abandona al compañero de su juventud y se olvida del pacto de su Dios.
texts.pro.2.18: Por lo cual su casa se desliza hacia la muerte, y sus sendas hacia las sombras.
texts.pro.2.19: Todos los que a ella van, no volverán, ni alcanzarán los senderos de la vida.
texts.pro.2.20: Así andarás por el camino de los buenos y guardarás las veredas de los justos;
texts.pro.2.21: porque los rectos habitarán la tierra y los íntegros permanecerán en ella,
texts.pro.2.22: mas los impíos serán cortados de la tierra y los prevaricadores serán de ella desarraigados.
texts.pro.3.1: Hijo mío, no te olvides de mi ley, y tu corazón guarde mis mandamientos;
texts.pro.3.2: porque largura de días y años de vida y paz te aumentarán.
texts.pro.3.3: Nunca se aparten de ti la misericordia y la verdad; átalas a tu cuello, escríbelas en la tabla de tu corazón;
texts.pro.3.4: y hallarás gracia y buena opinión ante los ojos de Dios y de los hombres.
texts.pro.3.5: Fíate de Yahvé de todo tu corazón, y no te apoyes en tu propia prudencia.
texts.pro.3.6: Reconócelo en todos tus caminos, y él enderezará tus veredas.
texts.pro.3.7: No seas sabio en tu propia opinión; teme a Yahvé y apártate del mal;
texts.pro.3.8: porque será medicina a tu cuerpo, y refrigerio para tus huesos.
texts.pro.3.9: Honra a Yahvé con tus bienes, y con las primicias de todos tus frutos;
texts.pro.3.10: y serán llenos tus graneros con abundancia, y tus lagares rebosarán de mosto.
texts.pro.3.11: No menosprecies, hijo mío, el castigo de Yahvé, ni te fatigues de su corrección;
texts.pro.3.12: porque Yahvé al que ama castiga, como el padre al hijo a quien quiere.
texts.pro.3.13: Bienaventurado el hombre que halla la sabiduría, y que obtiene la inteligencia;
texts.pro.3.14: porque su ganancia es mejor que la ganancia de la plata, y sus frutos más que el oro fino.
texts.pro.3.15: Más preciosa es que las piedras preciosas; y todo lo que puedes desear, no se puede comparar con ella.
texts.pro.3.16: Largura de días está en su mano derecha; en su izquierda, riquezas y honra.
texts.pro.3.17: Sus caminos son caminos deleitosos, y todas sus veredas paz.
texts.pro.3.18: Ella es árbol de vida a los que de ella echan mano, y bienaventurados son los que la retienen.
texts.pro.3.19: Yahvé con sabiduría fundó la tierra; afirmó los cielos con inteligencia.
texts.pro.3.20: Con su ciencia los abismos fueron divididos, y destilan rocío los cielos.
texts.pro.3.21: Hijo mío, no se aparten estas cosas de tus ojos; guarda la prudencia y el consejo,
texts.pro.3.22: y serán vida a tu alma, y gracia a tu cuello.
texts.pro.3.23: Entonces andarás por tu camino confiadamente, y tu pie no tropezará.
texts.pro.3.24: Cuando te acostares, no tendrás temor, sino que te acostarás, y tu sueño será grato.
texts.pro.3.25: No tendrás temor de pavor repentino, ni de la ruina de los impíos cuando viniere,
texts.pro.3.26: porque Yahvé será tu confianza, y él preservará tu pie de quedar preso.
texts.pro.3.27: No te niegues a hacer el bien a quien es debido, cuando tuvieres poder para hacerlo.
texts.pro.3.28: No digas a tu prójimo: Vete, y vuelve, y mañana te daré, cuando tienes contigo qué darle.
texts.pro.3.29: No intentes mal contra tu prójimo que habita confiado junto a ti.
texts.pro.3.30: No pleitees con alguno sin causa, si él no te ha hecho agravio.
texts.pro.3.31: No envidies al hombre injusto, ni escojas ninguno de sus caminos.
texts.pro.3.32: Porque el perverso es abominado de Yahvé; mas su comunión íntima es con los rectos.
texts.pro.3.33: La maldición de Yahvé está en la casa del impío, pero bendecirá la morada de los justos.
texts.pro.3.34: Ciertamente él escarnecerá a los escarnecedores, y a los humildes dará gracia.
texts.pro.3.35: Los sabios heredarán honra, mas los necios llevarán ignominia.
texts.pro.4.1: Oíd, hijos, la enseñanza de un padre; estad atentos para que conozcáis cordura.
texts.pro.4.2: Porque os doy buena doctrina; no abandonéis mi ley.
texts.pro.4.3: Pues yo también fui hijo de mi padre, delicado y único a los ojos de mi madre.
texts.pro.4.4: Él me enseñaba y me decía: «Retenga tu corazón mis razones; guarda mis mandamientos y vivirás.
texts.pro.4.5: Adquiere sabiduría, adquiere inteligencia; no te olvides ni te apartes de las razones de mi boca.
texts.pro.4.6: No la dejes, y ella te guardará; ámala, y ella te conservará.
texts.pro.4.7: Sabiduría ante todo: adquiere sabiduría; y sobre todas tus posesiones adquiere inteligencia.
texts.pro.4.8: Engrandécela, y ella te engrandecerá; ella te honrará cuando tú la hayas abrazado.
texts.pro.4.9: Adorno de gracia dará a tu cabeza; corona de hermosura te entregará».
texts.pro.4.10: Escucha, hijo mío, y recibe mis razones, y se te multiplicarán años de vida.
texts.pro.4.11: Por el camino de la sabiduría te he encaminado, y por veredas derechas te he hecho andar.
texts.pro.4.12: Cuando anduvieres, no se estrecharán tus pasos, y si corrieres, no tropezarás.
texts.pro.4.13: Retén la instrucción, no la dejes; guárdala, porque ella es tu vida.
texts.pro.4.14: No entres por la vereda de los impíos, ni vayas por el camino de los malos.
texts.pro.4.15: Evítalo, no pases por él; apártate de él, pasa de largo.
texts.pro.4.16: Porque ellos no duermen si no han hecho mal, y pierden el sueño si no han hecho caer a alguno.
texts.pro.4.17: Porque comen pan de maldad, y beben vino de violencias.
texts.pro.4.18: Mas la senda de los justos es como la luz de la aurora, que va en aumento hasta que el día es perfecto.
texts.pro.4.19: El camino de los impíos es como la oscuridad; no saben en qué tropiezan.
texts.pro.4.20: Hijo mío, está atento a mis palabras; inclina tu oído a mis razones.
texts.pro.4.21: No se aparten de tus ojos; guárdalas en medio de tu corazón;
texts.pro.4.22: porque son vida a los que las hallan, y medicina a todo su cuerpo.
texts.pro.4.23: Sobre toda cosa guardada, guarda tu corazón; porque de él mana la vida.
texts.pro.4.24: Aparta de ti la perversidad de la boca, y aleja de ti la iniquidad de los labios.
texts.pro.4.25: Tus ojos miren lo recto, y fíjese tu mirada en lo que tienes delante.
texts.pro.4.26: Examina la senda de tus pies, y todos tus caminos sean rectos.
texts.pro.4.27: No te desvíes a la derecha ni a la izquierda; aparta tu pie del mal.
texts.pro.5.1: Hijo mío, está atento a mi sabiduría, e inclina tu oído a mi inteligencia;
texts.pro.5.2: para que guardes la discreción, y tus labios conserven la ciencia.
texts.pro.5.3: Porque los labios de la mujer ajena destilan miel, y su paladar es más suave que el aceite;
texts.pro.5.4: mas su fin es amargo como el ajenjo, y agudo como espada de dos filos.
texts.pro.5.5: Sus pies descenderán a la muerte; sus pasos conducen al Seol.
texts.pro.5.6: No considera el camino de la vida; sus caminos son torcidos, y no lo sabe.
texts.pro.5.7: Ahora pues, hijos, escuchadme, y no os apartéis de las razones de mi boca.
texts.pro.5.8: Aleja de ella tu camino, y no te acerques a la puerta de su casa;
texts.pro.5.9: para que no des tu honor a otros, y tus años al cruel;
